title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I recently got a Galaxy Tab S8 tablet and considered getting a ketyboard cover for it. My older Tab S6 came with a keyboard which was okay but Sansung was using adhesive strips to hold the back cover onto the tablet and whether it always stayed on was hit and miss. When I began to look for a keyboard cover for my new Tab S8, the less expensive one had no trackpad, making it a non-starter and the model with the trackpad was too expensive. I found this model here on Amazon, used, for $55, a tremendous bargain. Even though, techically, it was made for the tab S7, it works perfectly with the S8. Samsung has finally abandoned the adhesive strips on the back cover and now uses pretty strong magnets instead. I have yet to have the back cover come off. The keyboard itself is very good, even with some shortcomings compared to a PC's keyboard but, overall it beats using any of the onscreen keyboards that are available for Android tablets. One thing that I really like is being able to disconnect from the keyboard and use the S8 strictly as a tablet with the back cover on only. The magnets on the back hold so well that I can adjust the bottom flap to suit me without the cover coming off. It's much better than having a full normal cover on the tablet. The bottom line is that the keyboard is more than adequate and the price made it too good to pass up.

text: I was debating on getting a third party keyboard for my galaxy tab but decided that I didn't want the hassle of charging a detachable keyboard. There have been many reviews praising the galaxy tab and Samsung keyboard combo, so I gave it a try. I bought this keyboard used for a small fraction of the price and I'm happy with the results. It was used but pretty much like new. The only visible use was seen in the torn up packaging, but everything works fine. Not much to complain about a tablet keyboard, its keypresses are adequate but the track pad is not the most responsive which is a small annoyance. The keyboard is easy to detach which is both a blessing and a curse because it makes it easy to convert back to a regular tablet and easy to hold but it can come off easily when in use, which sucks. The best part about this keyboard case is the back cover. The metal hinge is strong and durable and gives you so many viewing angles that stay stable the whole time. The worst part about this is the lack of protection around the edges. I like to protect my tablet that costs a couple hundred dollars, and this doesn't act as a protection at all. I'm buying a slim tpu case to at least cover the edges and will alter it to leave the side connecting to the keyboard free. We'll see if that works, but as a standalone keyboard and back cover this item is pretty good and performs well.

I liked the idea that this is an attachment to the device so you can take it on and off whenever you like instead of being adhered directly on the screen for one time use, but there are a few major issues.

If you remove the privacy screen protector, you feel that there is a lot of build up, and if you accidentally touch the area where the pins are at the bottom of the tablet, you get a jolt of electric shock. You don't even need to directly touch the pins with your skin, it passes through the bottom of the attachment if you still have it connected.

I definitely do not recommend this product, it is very flawed in many ways.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This isn't going to provide your tablet much protection,
1) can't use even a TPU case on this since the magnets are too weak.
2) Edges are exposed
3) Weak Magnets means the tablet will fall out or shift dangerously out of the case that leave it open to be stepped on.

Pros:
-Feels APPLE quality, I've had the PRO Keyboard from Apple for my iPad Pros, and this functions in pretty much the same way, sans the charging passthrough, which could probably easily be implemented.
-The keys on this are PERFECTLY SPRINGY. Now, I'm not a keyboard snob, I write this on a mechanical keyboard, but I rarely have issues with membrane or laptop style scissor switch keyboards. This one feels great, like a perfect 50gram key press, little lighter than the 60gram I rock daily, but stiffer than a 30g or 40 gram a lot of gamers like to use. They feel great.
-Trackpad isn't bad, functions, is responsive, and gets the job done, just slightly cramped. Given the "FLOATING" nature of this case, could probably do away with the creature comfort S-Pen holder and moved the keyboard up more, and give you an extra millimeter or two of trackpad space and that would probably be the sweet spot. Though, it functions and since the tablet is right there, and your tablet supports S-Pen, means... not really lacking in screen manipulation options that you can forgive a tiny trackpad.
-I got the blue one, and it's more of a proper NAVY Blue, very sharp and not toy looking.
-Backlight LED Blending, this must have a diffusion layer over the LEDs, since there's none of that annoying shimmer issue from cheaper backlight keyboards. Usually the biggest culprits for this are White, Yellow, and Purple. What I mean, is if your eyes are sensitive to this, you'll notice that white is Red Green and Blue mixed, there are clearly 2 sets of those colors with about a millimeter gap between the arrays providing the backlight on each key. you can clearly see the LEDs Though whatever diffusion they're using hides the off axis color shift. So for instance on cheaper keyboards, tilt one direction you'll see the Green being used for Yellow, tilt the other direction and you'd see the Red as well. and as a result would create a weird shimmer effect that bothers me. NOT HERE, this blends the colors, even Yellow and Purple, pretty well. I'm personally a CYAN person.

Cons:
-Viewing angle, I need just like 10 degrees more tilt in this to make it comfortable for me, this was the issue I had with the official Magic Keyboard. This copies that keyboard so well that it copies that flaw, also. I got frustraited with the magic keyboard that I broke it, would never close flat, but did give me 20 more degrees to play with and held its position, not at this point with this keyboard since when on my lap, the device tilts back a little bit to give me that extra 10 degrees. though resting on a desk, it's not the most comfortable. You don't have to always copy Apple nearly 1:1. You can iterate and improve. Like personally I would love if this acted more like a laptop hing and you could fold this nearly flat back. And maybe add a feature where you can put your tablet into a vertical/portrait orientation as well.
-Magnets are WEAK. Wanted to use this with a TPU Case to just give my tablet some extra protection and the weak magnets wouldn't go through the thin TPU.

Conclusion:
My favorite tablet cases for ipads are the laptop style cases, but for whatever reason, those manufacturers refuse to make those for Samsung tablets. I get not making them for EVERY android tablets out there, but Samsung is pretty popular... This is a great case in its own right, and works well, connects fast and has a function row, which is kind of nice, since it means the number row isn't home to media keys and kind of keeps them out of the way. I would recommend this keyboard, it's super comfy to type on, and is just as nice as the Magic Keyboard for half the price, while giving you a 7 color backlight keyboard.

text:
With the Dexnor case and keyboard being 130 dollars I was a bit worried it would not hold up to my extremely high standards. The construction of the device is secondary to none, It is very well built and solid. The hinges hold firm and dont wobble around. The only construction criticism I have is that the keyboard and base is pretty light compared to the tablet so its a bit backheavy when open. I wish they would have added some weight to the base, but I totally understand why they didnt. Second is the lack of rubber feet on the bottom. This thing likes to slide around a bit and again, I understand that adding feet would add "Deck flex" to the keyboard.

The typing experience is one of the best from a compact keyboard like this. The keys have a great feel to them and typing is very enjoyable. Its a little cramped but absolutely nothing I couldn't get used to after a few minutes of typing. My biggest complaint with the lower half of this device is the trackpad. The trackpad isnt great, a bit on the small side and the sensitivity or latency on it seems just a bit off. It could be the tablet settings but Ive looked and cant seem to get it just right. Now I mostly use a bluetooth mouse and turn off the trackpad (Which is an excellent feature).

The RGB keys is a great addition and helps me see at night or in the dark which is excellent. The timeout feature is a bit short and I haven't been able to figure out a way to make it longer which kinda sucks but thats a small thing.

Lastly, I dislike that the S Pen has no cover on it to keep it in place while charging. I wish there was a magnetic flap that went over the pen even though they include a place for it inside. The pen dosen't seem to charge when inside.

Overall 10/10 rating on this device. Just a few minor things that can be overlooked. Would absolutely buy again even though Its built sturdily enough I doubt Ill ever have to.

I've been on the fence about this product, because I was not sure how much of an upgrade it would be from other keyboard cases for tablets I have used before.

It is a definite upgrade from the cramped FINTIE brand keyboard I was using.

Connectivity: easy to connect. No lag between waking the device up and beginning to type. The keyboard isn't cramped.

Trackpad: despite other reviews I don't find it scrolls too fast. It is responsive. You can also adjust speed through the settings on the tablet.

Magnetivity: The tablet feels very secure propped open. You can gently pull on it and it does not budge.

Stability: when using the keyboard there is no wiggling or instability, as other people have reported.

Screen share: I found this to be very cool! I had to download an app from the Windows store but it took no time to set my tablet up as an extnded display. The trackpad and the keyboard on the case can be used as well.

Weight: it is heavier than my surface tablet by about half the weight. It's no heavier than the hard cover cases I got for my samsung tablet that did not come with a keyboard. A bit heavy, but it is a 12.4" tablet after all.

I like using my tablet without a case. This magnetic case is much better for anyone who likes to do the same. With other cases I felt like I was working too hard to get the tablet out and worried about potential damage popping it in and out. This case takes care of that issue altogether.

I was worried about closing the tablet on the screen and the potential for scratches. Everything is soft enough and recessed enough that it doesn't seem like a proble. Glad I got it!

- Storage for the SPen
- Solid corner protection
- Rechargable (that it is USB C like almost everything else I own is a plus)
- Works with a screen protector (You have to be a little careful. The first one I ordered didn't work. Get one labeled for use with a case.). [This one worked for me - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CBLV7X7F?psc=1&ref=ppx_pop_dt_b_product_details]

2. No way to keep the case closed and the screen protected if dropped. True, and I knew that when I bought it, but I used extra strong fabric glue and a scrap of nylon webbing to attach a Velcro strip to the case (see photo - the Velcro loops side; the case edge is sandwiched between the webbing and the Velcro and has been stable for daily use), and put a self stick matching Velcro dot with the hooks on the back of the case in the small space between the pen slot and the kickstand. It works well for me. I just tuck the end of the strip under the keyboard edge to get it out of the way if I want to use the trackpad. (A plus to this fix is that the Velcro holds my SPen in place in the back if I'm trying to leave it in the charging slot while having the case closed in my bag.)

3. Misc: It is slightly finicky to get the corners seated smoothly, but once you do, it is fine. I haven't seen any issues with the snaps breaking unlike other users, but I would be fine with replacing them with a strip of self stick Velcro if I needed to. I have had the camera cover pop out a few times, but it isn't a big deal for me. It just snaps back, and that was a bonus feature anyway.

I've now had the case for about 8 months of daily use. I would say I'm reasonably careful with the keyboard, but I don't baby it since it goes everywhere with me. I meant to write a review a long time ago, but I can now comment a little on its longevity. It still works perfectly, and I still love it. (I haven't dropped my tablet seriously, though.)

Thank you for a great product! This is one of a very few reviews I have ever written on Amazon, and it makes me happy to sing a product's praises. This case adds to the joy I have in my S9. Right now, my only regret is that Samsung appears to be abandoning this lovely, small form factor. We'll see what the future brings. Returning to an iPad or iPad mini wouldn't be my first choice. I love having flagship specs on a small tablet. If they made an 8 inch variation, I'd probably buy that.

text:
I have the Samsung S10 Ultra tablet and have used its default stylus pen. I also purchased the S11 stylus pen to try out. Here is my review, which may help others decide if they need the S11 pen.

1. The TIP DESIGN
The tip of the S11 pen is the major difference compared to the S10 stylus. The S11 tip is made of plastic, but the very top features a rubber material. This provides more friction, but it also leads to hand fatigue. After using both tips for a while, I found that while the S11 offers better control, the S10 provides a much smoother experience. The extra rubbery friction on the S11 causes the hand to tire after extended use.

2. SHAPE AND ERGONOMICS
The S11 stylus has a traditional hexagonal shape like a standard pencil, while the S10 is mostly rounded with only one flat side. I believe both designs are workable, and neither offers a significant advantage over the other. More of a personal preference. For my S10's rounded shape (with one flat side) was good enough.

3. The ERASE BUTTON
The erase button on the S11 is less convenient due to the pen's shape. I found myself having to look for the button every time I needed it. In contrast, the S10 pen’s erase button feels more natural to use because of the pen's overall design.

SUMMARY:
I prefer the S10 stylus because it causes less fatigue during regular use and has a more intuitive eraser button. In my opinion, the S10 pen's rounded shape is superior to the S11.

I got this for my Tab S7+. The program in the picture is Infinite Painter (if you're looking to get into more drawing apps, try CSP or Krita).

If your pen doesn't automatically connect/charge, you'll want to go to:

settings > s pen, then turn off "Allow multiple S pens" and then
settings > s pen > air actions, and then turn on air actions.

It should connect then, but it might take a few minutes. Charging will also only take a few minutes to go from 0 to 100.

The pen has pressure sensitivity, tilt features, and gestures--everything the original pen has because it is the normal pen. However, it does NOT come with extra nibs or the nib removal tool, nor does it say. It's just the luck of the draw, you might get them or you might not. I got a refurbished pen. The tip of the pen is very soft and doesn't make any noise against the screen. You might like that, but I'm more used to Wacom pens where you can actually feel the tip hitting the surface. This feels more like a paint brush, but I don't entirely dislike it.

The only maybe bad thing about it was that every piece of tape that was holding the s pen box together had at least 1 eyebrow sized hair in it. Ugh. How does that even happen?

I've tested a wide range of microSD cards over the years, but the Samsung PRO Plus 512GB stands out as one of the most reliable and high-performing options available. From 4K video recording to gaming and mobile storage, this card delivers consistent speed and durability, making it an excellent choice for professionals and everyday users alike.

Real-World Performance
I put this card through its paces in multiple devices, and it exceeded expectations in every scenario:

🔹 4K Video Recording: Installed in my DJI Mini 4 Pro, the card handled 4K 60fps video flawlessly—no dropped frames, no stuttering, just smooth and stable footage. I also used it with my GoPro Hero 12 on a snowboarding trip, where it kept up with high-action shots without skipping a beat.

🔹 Mobile & File Transfers: In my Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, I transferred over 100GB of 4K videos and high-resolution photos, and the speeds were impressive. With read speeds up to 180MB/s and write speeds around 130MB/s, I didn’t have to wait long for large files to move—something I’ve struggled with on cheaper microSD cards. The A2 rating also made a noticeable difference in app performance and load times.

🔹 Gaming & Storage: When tested in a Steam Deck and Nintendo Switch, the card handled large game files effortlessly. No lag, no stuttering—just smooth gameplay and quick load times. With 512GB of storage, I didn’t have to constantly delete old files to make room for new ones.

Pros & Cons
✅ Pros:

✔ High-Speed Performance – Read speeds up to 180MB/s, write speeds around 130MB/s—perfect for 4K recording and high-res file transfers.
✔ Reliable for High-End Devices – Works seamlessly with GoPro, DJI drones, flagship smartphones, gaming consoles, and more.
✔ Massive Storage – 512GB capacity means fewer worries about running out of space.
✔ Durability & Ruggedness – Survived freezing temperatures on a mountain and even a coffee spill without any data loss.
✔ Optimized for Gaming & Apps – The A2 rating ensures fast app loading and smooth performance in portable gaming consoles.

❌ Cons:

✖ Not UHS-II – If you’re a professional video editor working with 8K RAW footage, you may need an even faster card.
✖ Premium Price – While not the cheapest option, the performance and reliability justify the cost.

text: Ordered this at the same time as the Tab S7, mostly as I needed to replace a damaged S2, and did NOT want to damage my 12.4 screen S7 on the first day. Upon reflection and after using it for a few days, I'm greatly disappointed as the only protection this case does is keep the screen clean This case is a smidge smaller than the outer rim of the tablet, so the tablet is protecting the edges of the case, not vice-a-versa. Yes, it looks nice, matches the case color, but I wanted and needed a case with near sacrificial protection for the tablet. One other point is the so-called Pen Storage. The pen is stored in a magnetic manner between the binder spaces, if you fully fold open the case, and hold it like a book (or mag), the pen is hanging down under the tablet and is easily dislodged. I have to manage whether the pen is still there and have once or twice had to go back and find it as dropped. The only time it is truly stored/stowed, is when the cover is closed where two raised capture ends are present in the binder spine. Currently I now leave the pen on my nightstand, as I can't afford to replace it, if it falls off unbeknownst to me. Samsung should have a better solution for pen storage but with the Fold3 and 4 cases as examples, they do not seem to care about pen management. It would have been easy enough at boring out one of the spine capture ends on the binder, and allowed the pen to be inserted and have their magnet capture more effectively hold the pen in and not on. Looking at getting a true shield type case and most of them have a pen pocket. Sad part is those much more capable cases are half the price what I paid here. Oh Well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The m1 IPad Pro is a widely known premium product, especially the price gap for the 12.9 inch. And most people would stray away from refurbished devices of this caliber. The question is: Was buying a 2 year old (refurbished) model the right choice? Well, yes and no. I come from the brilliant iPad Air 4; which I would Reccomend to just about anyone. I am a supporter of the m2 IPad Pro, and I believe that if you have a device older than that iPad Air 4, that is the one you should spring for. However, for those I’m my boat. The m1 iPad Pro is the way to go!

Let’s start with the negatives; The packaging had me a bit worried, though there was no shipping damage. The cable and charger included are not apple products, though I half expected this. And though the power brick is nice. (((EDIT: the brick was broken, as a person who has plenty of chargers and cablesI, I do not mind this))) The cable was very cheap, I am not docking points, but I have to consider that this is an expensive product and the included cable feels like it came with an alcatel flip phone. Upon inspection, there is 2 toothpick sized blemishes on the chassis. Though one of these wiped clean with a bit of force.

The positives are that this product feels like a brand new machine, once I took it out I tested it for any flaws, the screen is like new, no issue with HDR content … no speaker or port damage was noticeable, no issue with the Apple Pencil charger or the Magic Keyboard connector either. Face ID works great. Cameras (both front and back) worked fine.
Performance is Great, My model scored 1% under average for single core performance and about the same for multi-core. Of course I also tested the battery, by using a software called coconut battery; you can plug your device into a computer and it can tell you the full charge capacity it has. Amazon states that its renewed products have a battery health score of 80% or more, so you outta test that. My model scored a 96.4% put simply, my model has lost about 14.5 minutes of possible screen on time.
To end this off, I do reccomend this product, my model was in tip top shape and an excellent bargain, that is the thing however; MY model was in tip top shape, there is always risk with refurbished products, and you have to go into it with some acceptance that something might be wrong. But if you are willing to accept that, this is an excellent deal and based off of my experience: if you are looking for an m1 iPad Pro, this is the spot.
(Apple has a refurbished website too! They completely replace the battery and chassis of all devices (note: these certified refurbished ones are more expensive, a model like the one I bought would run me another 200$ more from their store). I would reccomend looking there as well for future apple products you may buy. Say, a new phone or a Mac.)

Long term check in.
Things are running smoothly as of October 16th, 2023. And no major errors have peaked their head, so not much else to add;
The only thing I will add is a plethora of low battery Warnings, I will get multiple “20% battery remaining from 20%-11%, and 3-4 “battery at 10% warnings from the range of 10-8%, its like the battery or the device cannot tell or flip flops between it being above or below 20%,10%, etc.

—errors I have encountered—
The battery indicator does not jump from 19-21, and then give the the warning again once it goes back down to 20, it just gives the the 20% warning at 20,19, and 18%

—long term ownership “understandings”—
I still believe that this is a great deal and a great buy, but after living with the 12.9 inch I would have to advise going for the smaller one unless you get a keyboard case or the Magic Keyboard, I also feel like the 10.9 inch is more attuned for the usage of the magic pencil or any stylus. That doesn’t mean the pencil is bad for the 12.9, but that its a bit cumbersome in some areas.
I heard people complaining about the weight of the device (with the Magic Keyboard especially) and I mean yea… but it is something you get used to, and when you do just use it as a handheld, it is lighter than you would expect.
I’m not doing a review of the Magic Keyboard here; but any keyboard (especially the Magic Keyboard) completely transforms the experience of this device, and it is 100% worth it to get a keyboard with the 12.9 inch, doesn’t have to be the Magic Keyboard, but a keyboard none the less. The Logitech folio touch is a great option. I’ll let you do your own research about it but I’ll just jot down some things if you’re curious.
Magic Keyboard: magnetic attachment, great typing feel, and completely detaches. Has passthrough charging — 349 (get open box at best buy, I got mine for 260, make sure to ask to test the device and just make sure all the buttons work, along with the SHIFT + KEY combos, feel for actuation discrepancies)
Folio touch: removable keyboard but case stays on, ok typing feel, and has a stand for drawing angles. — 170
Both have touchpad, but Magic Keyboards is way better
Now for the only thing I think I could’ve saved money on:
The Cellular connection.
I. Love the cellular connection! . . . . . . Hey wait a minute….
Cellular connectivity on an iPad is way cooler than a phone, and is so worth it and I’m totally hooked to a parasitic exchange.
I don’t use the cellular connectivity enough to justify getting the cellular model, I thought I was going to a lot.
When the internet goes out, its awesome, when you’re travelling, its great, when you’re internet is slow, it’s convenient, for streaming, its good.
All in all, I would recommend the cellular model, but ask yourself if you will use it, not in the term of ‘future proofing’ which is a phrase i don’t agree with to an extent. But its a lot like that 49” monitor i got, I Love it, and I will get 49” monitors again, but I’ve locked myself into a more expensive chain, that is kinda how i can describe what going for the cellular model is.

I love this iPad, and i love how i got it for such a good price, usually when i get a new tech thing, I end up semi regretting or wishing i got something more, or something newer, that something could’ve been better. But i have not once said or thought: “i wish I would’ve gone for a 10.9 inch, i wish i sprung for a newer model, i wish i got more storage. The cellular thing is something I could’ve saved money on, but i have not regretted it.
I think the m1 iPad Pro is the best value tablet you can get right now, and I don’t know if the next iPad Air will change that, (because of the rumoured larger screen size option)
If you use the magic pencil a lot, you should consider the 10.9 inch, its more portable, its easier to use as a stand-alone tablet (without a keyboard case) its cheaper (obviously) and with the money you can save or put towards a higher capacity storage, or towards cellular, or a peripheral. And slightly more battery because of the lower screen spec, it’s a budget powerhouse.
But the 12.9 inch is fantastic!
And now to loosely connect this to this product.
This good deal for fantastic device, i approve.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The m1 IPad Pro is a widely known premium product, especially the price gap for the 12.9 inch. And most people would stray away from refurbished devices of this caliber. The question is: Was buying a 2 year old (refurbished) model the right choice? Well, yes and no. I come from the brilliant iPad Air 4; which I would Reccomend to just about anyone. I am a supporter of the m2 IPad Pro, and I believe that if you have a device older than that iPad Air 4, that is the one you should spring for. However, for those I’m my boat. The m1 iPad Pro is the way to go!

Let’s start with the negatives; The packaging had me a bit worried, though there was no shipping damage. The cable and charger included are not apple products, though I half expected this. And though the power brick is nice. (((EDIT: the brick was broken, as a person who has plenty of chargers and cablesI, I do not mind this))) The cable was very cheap, I am not docking points, but I have to consider that this is an expensive product and the included cable feels like it came with an alcatel flip phone. Upon inspection, there is 2 toothpick sized blemishes on the chassis. Though one of these wiped clean with a bit of force.

The positives are that this product feels like a brand new machine, once I took it out I tested it for any flaws, the screen is like new, no issue with HDR content … no speaker or port damage was noticeable, no issue with the Apple Pencil charger or the Magic Keyboard connector either. Face ID works great. Cameras (both front and back) worked fine.
Performance is Great, My model scored 1% under average for single core performance and about the same for multi-core. Of course I also tested the battery, by using a software called coconut battery; you can plug your device into a computer and it can tell you the full charge capacity it has. Amazon states that its renewed products have a battery health score of 80% or more, so you outta test that. My model scored a 96.4% put simply, my model has lost about 14.5 minutes of possible screen on time.
To end this off, I do reccomend this product, my model was in tip top shape and an excellent bargain, that is the thing however; MY model was in tip top shape, there is always risk with refurbished products, and you have to go into it with some acceptance that something might be wrong. But if you are willing to accept that, this is an excellent deal and based off of my experience: if you are looking for an m1 iPad Pro, this is the spot.
(Apple has a refurbished website too! They completely replace the battery and chassis of all devices (note: these certified refurbished ones are more expensive, a model like the one I bought would run me another 200$ more from their store). I would reccomend looking there as well for future apple products you may buy. Say, a new phone or a Mac.)

Long term check in.
Things are running smoothly as of October 16th, 2023. And no major errors have peaked their head, so not much else to add;
The only thing I will add is a plethora of low battery Warnings, I will get multiple “20% battery remaining from 20%-11%, and 3-4 “battery at 10% warnings from the range of 10-8%, its like the battery or the device cannot tell or flip flops between it being above or below 20%,10%, etc.

—errors I have encountered—
The battery indicator does not jump from 19-21, and then give the the warning again once it goes back down to 20, it just gives the the 20% warning at 20,19, and 18%

—long term ownership “understandings”—
I still believe that this is a great deal and a great buy, but after living with the 12.9 inch I would have to advise going for the smaller one unless you get a keyboard case or the Magic Keyboard, I also feel like the 10.9 inch is more attuned for the usage of the magic pencil or any stylus. That doesn’t mean the pencil is bad for the 12.9, but that its a bit cumbersome in some areas.
I heard people complaining about the weight of the device (with the Magic Keyboard especially) and I mean yea… but it is something you get used to, and when you do just use it as a handheld, it is lighter than you would expect.
I’m not doing a review of the Magic Keyboard here; but any keyboard (especially the Magic Keyboard) completely transforms the experience of this device, and it is 100% worth it to get a keyboard with the 12.9 inch, doesn’t have to be the Magic Keyboard, but a keyboard none the less. The Logitech folio touch is a great option. I’ll let you do your own research about it but I’ll just jot down some things if you’re curious.
Magic Keyboard: magnetic attachment, great typing feel, and completely detaches. Has passthrough charging — 349 (get open box at best buy, I got mine for 260, make sure to ask to test the device and just make sure all the buttons work, along with the SHIFT + KEY combos, feel for actuation discrepancies)
Folio touch: removable keyboard but case stays on, ok typing feel, and has a stand for drawing angles. — 170
Both have touchpad, but Magic Keyboards is way better
Now for the only thing I think I could’ve saved money on:
The Cellular connection.
I. Love the cellular connection! . . . . . . Hey wait a minute….
Cellular connectivity on an iPad is way cooler than a phone, and is so worth it and I’m totally hooked to a parasitic exchange.
I don’t use the cellular connectivity enough to justify getting the cellular model, I thought I was going to a lot.
When the internet goes out, its awesome, when you’re travelling, its great, when you’re internet is slow, it’s convenient, for streaming, its good.
All in all, I would recommend the cellular model, but ask yourself if you will use it, not in the term of ‘future proofing’ which is a phrase i don’t agree with to an extent. But its a lot like that 49” monitor i got, I Love it, and I will get 49” monitors again, but I’ve locked myself into a more expensive chain, that is kinda how i can describe what going for the cellular model is.

I love this iPad, and i love how i got it for such a good price, usually when i get a new tech thing, I end up semi regretting or wishing i got something more, or something newer, that something could’ve been better. But i have not once said or thought: “i wish I would’ve gone for a 10.9 inch, i wish i sprung for a newer model, i wish i got more storage. The cellular thing is something I could’ve saved money on, but i have not regretted it.
I think the m1 iPad Pro is the best value tablet you can get right now, and I don’t know if the next iPad Air will change that, (because of the rumoured larger screen size option)
If you use the magic pencil a lot, you should consider the 10.9 inch, its more portable, its easier to use as a stand-alone tablet (without a keyboard case) its cheaper (obviously) and with the money you can save or put towards a higher capacity storage, or towards cellular, or a peripheral. And slightly more battery because of the lower screen spec, it’s a budget powerhouse.
But the 12.9 inch is fantastic!
And now to loosely connect this to this product.
This good deal for fantastic device, i approve.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The m1 IPad Pro is a widely known premium product, especially the price gap for the 12.9 inch. And most people would stray away from refurbished devices of this caliber. The question is: Was buying a 2 year old (refurbished) model the right choice? Well, yes and no. I come from the brilliant iPad Air 4; which I would Reccomend to just about anyone. I am a supporter of the m2 IPad Pro, and I believe that if you have a device older than that iPad Air 4, that is the one you should spring for. However, for those I’m my boat. The m1 iPad Pro is the way to go!

Let’s start with the negatives; The packaging had me a bit worried, though there was no shipping damage. The cable and charger included are not apple products, though I half expected this. And though the power brick is nice. (((EDIT: the brick was broken, as a person who has plenty of chargers and cablesI, I do not mind this))) The cable was very cheap, I am not docking points, but I have to consider that this is an expensive product and the included cable feels like it came with an alcatel flip phone. Upon inspection, there is 2 toothpick sized blemishes on the chassis. Though one of these wiped clean with a bit of force.

The positives are that this product feels like a brand new machine, once I took it out I tested it for any flaws, the screen is like new, no issue with HDR content … no speaker or port damage was noticeable, no issue with the Apple Pencil charger or the Magic Keyboard connector either. Face ID works great. Cameras (both front and back) worked fine.
Performance is Great, My model scored 1% under average for single core performance and about the same for multi-core. Of course I also tested the battery, by using a software called coconut battery; you can plug your device into a computer and it can tell you the full charge capacity it has. Amazon states that its renewed products have a battery health score of 80% or more, so you outta test that. My model scored a 96.4% put simply, my model has lost about 14.5 minutes of possible screen on time.
To end this off, I do reccomend this product, my model was in tip top shape and an excellent bargain, that is the thing however; MY model was in tip top shape, there is always risk with refurbished products, and you have to go into it with some acceptance that something might be wrong. But if you are willing to accept that, this is an excellent deal and based off of my experience: if you are looking for an m1 iPad Pro, this is the spot.
(Apple has a refurbished website too! They completely replace the battery and chassis of all devices (note: these certified refurbished ones are more expensive, a model like the one I bought would run me another 200$ more from their store). I would reccomend looking there as well for future apple products you may buy. Say, a new phone or a Mac.)

Long term check in.
Things are running smoothly as of October 16th, 2023. And no major errors have peaked their head, so not much else to add;
The only thing I will add is a plethora of low battery Warnings, I will get multiple “20% battery remaining from 20%-11%, and 3-4 “battery at 10% warnings from the range of 10-8%, its like the battery or the device cannot tell or flip flops between it being above or below 20%,10%, etc.

—errors I have encountered—
The battery indicator does not jump from 19-21, and then give the the warning again once it goes back down to 20, it just gives the the 20% warning at 20,19, and 18%

—long term ownership “understandings”—
I still believe that this is a great deal and a great buy, but after living with the 12.9 inch I would have to advise going for the smaller one unless you get a keyboard case or the Magic Keyboard, I also feel like the 10.9 inch is more attuned for the usage of the magic pencil or any stylus. That doesn’t mean the pencil is bad for the 12.9, but that its a bit cumbersome in some areas.
I heard people complaining about the weight of the device (with the Magic Keyboard especially) and I mean yea… but it is something you get used to, and when you do just use it as a handheld, it is lighter than you would expect.
I’m not doing a review of the Magic Keyboard here; but any keyboard (especially the Magic Keyboard) completely transforms the experience of this device, and it is 100% worth it to get a keyboard with the 12.9 inch, doesn’t have to be the Magic Keyboard, but a keyboard none the less. The Logitech folio touch is a great option. I’ll let you do your own research about it but I’ll just jot down some things if you’re curious.
Magic Keyboard: magnetic attachment, great typing feel, and completely detaches. Has passthrough charging — 349 (get open box at best buy, I got mine for 260, make sure to ask to test the device and just make sure all the buttons work, along with the SHIFT + KEY combos, feel for actuation discrepancies)
Folio touch: removable keyboard but case stays on, ok typing feel, and has a stand for drawing angles. — 170
Both have touchpad, but Magic Keyboards is way better
Now for the only thing I think I could’ve saved money on:
The Cellular connection.
I. Love the cellular connection! . . . . . . Hey wait a minute….
Cellular connectivity on an iPad is way cooler than a phone, and is so worth it and I’m totally hooked to a parasitic exchange.
I don’t use the cellular connectivity enough to justify getting the cellular model, I thought I was going to a lot.
When the internet goes out, its awesome, when you’re travelling, its great, when you’re internet is slow, it’s convenient, for streaming, its good.
All in all, I would recommend the cellular model, but ask yourself if you will use it, not in the term of ‘future proofing’ which is a phrase i don’t agree with to an extent. But its a lot like that 49” monitor i got, I Love it, and I will get 49” monitors again, but I’ve locked myself into a more expensive chain, that is kinda how i can describe what going for the cellular model is.

I love this iPad, and i love how i got it for such a good price, usually when i get a new tech thing, I end up semi regretting or wishing i got something more, or something newer, that something could’ve been better. But i have not once said or thought: “i wish I would’ve gone for a 10.9 inch, i wish i sprung for a newer model, i wish i got more storage. The cellular thing is something I could’ve saved money on, but i have not regretted it.
I think the m1 iPad Pro is the best value tablet you can get right now, and I don’t know if the next iPad Air will change that, (because of the rumoured larger screen size option)
If you use the magic pencil a lot, you should consider the 10.9 inch, its more portable, its easier to use as a stand-alone tablet (without a keyboard case) its cheaper (obviously) and with the money you can save or put towards a higher capacity storage, or towards cellular, or a peripheral. And slightly more battery because of the lower screen spec, it’s a budget powerhouse.
But the 12.9 inch is fantastic!
And now to loosely connect this to this product.
This good deal for fantastic device, i approve.

So, I opened it and plugged it in with the power connector that came with it. It seemed to be charging but a couple minutes later I looked over and it no longer was. Unplugged it, plugged it back in and the same thing happened, it charged 2% and then stopped (up to 72% fully charged). That time, when I went to plug it in again it would not charge at all. Put it away till the next day. Pulled it out, at 52%. Plugged it in, went back an hour later and was at 54% saying it was no longer charging.

That was it for me! Too much money for something that doesn’t properly work out of the box and I’m not setting my daughter up for disappointment. Spent the extra money to get a brand new one ($50 more for a fifth generation but without cellular) from Best Buy. Spent an extra hundred on a 2 year warranty in case this is an apple thing as opposed to an improperly refurbished thing.

Amazon does great with returns, UPS picked it up the next day and my confidence is high that my money will be refunded with no problem.

Glad I didn’t wait until the last moment before Christmas, and folks always check your devices before giving them to your children!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Don’t get me wrong, fantastic device. The only problem for me that would be worth a star or two itself is there is NO HOME BUTTON. I knew this going in and I always have the accessibility option for an on-screen “button” enabled. I really only wanted this for the second gen pen pineapple Apple Pen…cil. I decided to get the 4 instead of the 5 because from what I read the spec differences were not worth the cost. The new processor differences weren’t worth the 200 dollar difference.

REFURBISHED, MODEL DIFFERENCES-
I got a refurbished, it was absolutely perfect. The charging cable was actually longer. I found a returned Apple Pencil 2 for 65 dollars, was able to max out the specs on this one for the same price as the new air 5 stock standard. The colors on this gen are super boring, but it’s always in a case so who cares.

STORAGE-
You can put so many apps on this that run perfectly. I’ve never seen it have a problem.

KEYBOARD—
The new keyboard is odd. I still haven’t quite figured it out yet. Passwords are cumbersome now. Some of it doesn’t make sense and does not feel organic at all.

FOR ARTISTS AND WRITERS—
As an artist by hobby more than profession, the pro was just always out of reach with regards to cost. Like, ffff how many major electronics can a normal person afford in this day and age? I have no frame of reference but I can say this pencil is PHENOMENAL, it’s like using an actual pencil. The pressure and sensitivity are incredible. If you take off the nib, the tip is actually made of gold, surprisingly. I can’t stand that the only way to charge it is to magnetically attach it to the side of the device, HOWEVER, it charges 2% in about 1 minute.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Giving five stars, despite a couple cons. Here’s my opinion on this purchase:

1.) Price: I purchased the 2020 iPad Air 10.9” on a sale price of $239 which is great for a fairly new Apple product so no complaints there!

2.) Quality: The condition was listed as Refurbished - Excellent… and it is! No scratches, no cracks, no dings or dents, looks BRAND NEW and is true to size 10.9”!

3.) Super lightweight making it comfortable to hold and use for extended periods of time.

4.) Just like any Apple product, set up is always a breeze. If you have other Apple products then you already understand.

Here’s my complaint:
Shipping was not so good. I have previously worked for FedEx so when I saw my iPad was shipping through them I thought “I’ll be lucky if it isn’t broken or lost”. With that being said, it was delivered 2 days late but arrived undamaged and in one piece so I’ll let that be.

The packaging, however, was hugely disappointing. (Pics for reference) The iPad was not shipped in an original Apple box. It was shipped in a thin brown box, wrapped in a single bubble mailer with a single sheet of brown packaging paper in the box. There was too much space in the box for my liking and could definitely use improvement. I wouldn’t be surprised if someone else orders from this company and receives an excellent condition iPad in damaged condition due to shipping. These products are cheaper than typical retail price BUT $200+ is still a lot of money in this economy. Overall great experience, iPad is perfect and in perfect condition, just hate that the packaging was so insufficient.

text:
The Logitech rugged folio keyboard case is well-crafted and securely holds an iPad (A16). The keyboard has a nice tactile feel and includes a comprehensive set of keys similar to those found on a full-size Apple keyboard. The magnetic “latch” securely closes the case and folds out of the way when the case is open. Since the case and keyboard interface through Apple’s Smart Connector, there’s no need to use Bluetooth or charge the case. The fold-out stand is continuously adjustable over 40 degrees and securely holds the iPad at various angles. The case is reinforced at the edges and corners and might protect the iPad if dropped. My only complaint is that the thin plastic “hinge” between the keyboard and iPad is quite flimsy. A rigid hinge would have been much more suitable.

Considering its cost, quality, and functionality, this case is a worthwhile investment for those who require a keyboard.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It is very hard to find a decent, inexpensive, keyboard case these days. In the past my go to brand was INCASE but over the years they ceased making iPhone and iPad cases. ZAGG was my next go-to maker of keyboard cases but from reading reviews it seems their quality has slipped over the years. I recently tried an Otterbox for my new A16 iPad but while it did offer great coverage it was just too bulky for my needs and it had no keyboard case option.

Then I found Logitech! I looked through their many different offering of keyboard cases and found one that suited my needs perfectly: Logitech Slim Folio Case. I didn't need a keyboard case with a build in trackpad as I have a Logitech Pebble Mouse 2 M350s which pairs well with this keyboard case. The keyboard case offer full protection on all edges while still offering access to the USB-C port as well as volume and Touch ID button. The iPad connects to the keyboard via the magnetic contacts and holds good. It is a little floppy but not so bad you notice.

The case runs off of two CR2032 batteries; so it requires no separate charging. While that might seem like an inconvenience for some I think it's a better option than worrying about charging both my iPad and keyboard case. The keys feel great when typing and the build quality is what you would come to expect from Logitech. Simple and direct and reliable. I love the design and feel it will hold up for the life of my iPad as long as I take good care of it. Nothing is obscured or blocked and the sound quality while is not compromised. The keys are not backlit unfortunately but I do not see that as a problem except if I'm writing in the dark and need to find a function key. However, my last iPad keyboard case wasn't backlit and it managed me fine for over five years.

I do recommend this case if you are looking for a quality build keyboard case that costs much less than an Apple brand. I feel this is going keep me happy for a long time and serve me well when I travel.

text:
I have been a Logitech user for ever, since the late 1980's. I don't recall ever having trouble with any of their products (well maybe the CyberMan but I know I was not alone).

Got the Slim Folio for my iPad 10th gen and it certainly honours the quality tradition I have come to expect from this company. It's quite sturdy and the keyboard... Oh the keyboard. I used the Apple Keyboard Folio on another iPad a few years ago. While the Apple product was a membrane keyboard, the Slim Folio is actually a real keyboard which is super comfortable to use.

Things to keep in mind if you are planning to purchase this product :

- It does add a bit of bulk. It's actually thrice as thick as the iPad itself so if you don't like bulky case this one is not for you. However it does product the table from all sides so there's that.

- The keyboard is NOT backlighted.

- There is no trackpad. I resolved this by pairing a mouse. But you can absolutely use it with no mouse of course.

- The keyboard is Bluetooth and it's not rechargeable. It uses two CR2032 coin batteries. Logitech claims they will provide three years worth of power.

All in all an excellent product which I will be using for years to come.

EDIT : I actually returned the Slim Folio and got the Combo Touch. The fact that the Slim Folio’s keyboard was not backlighted was kind of a hindrance to me. Plus I found it unconfortable to hold the iPad with the keyboard folded back.

The Combo Touch solved both of these problems and also I find the iPad very confortable to hold without the detachable keyboard. The case does not add that much bulk. Much happier with the Combo Touch.

text:
Hi everybody,

I've actually had one of these for nearly 4 years now. I came on Amazon to "save a second one for later." :-) Because I am getting a second tablet for a specific purpose, which I probably will describe shortly.I apparently bought the one that I own all the way back in 2019. When I came on here looking for a second one, I only then realized I had never written a review. So here is my review. I should perhaps start by explaining but I am physically disabled, I use a wheelchair for mobility and I have very limited use of my hands. Actually I have no functional use of my left hand. I am only saying this so that you can get an idea of how absolutely essential to good tablet stand would be for me. I really can't hold tablets or phones in my hand for any length of time without feeling pain, much like another video reviewer on here who has carpal tunnel in both hands. For us holding things even relatively late things in our hands for any extended period of time is really not a possibility.
Okay, with that money should out-of-the-way they that I now remember really working to find the ideal tablet stand for my iPad, at the time. An iPad that I no longer own, by the way. I remembered that I struggled and searched for long time, mainly because at the time I had limited experience with tablets and didn't know what I would need. So naturally I thought I would need something complex and expensive. :-) WRONG. But that's my nature. I dried out three or four other types of tablet stands, bought them and either immediately return them or threw them away. Most of them were much bulkier and more complex. Most of them were also made of plastic. If you haven't bought a tablet stand before, don't buy a plastic one. It probably will not last.

This tablet stand is superior to most all the others, because it is neither complex nor bulky. It seems perfectly designed, in its simplicity. The designers seem to have carefully considered every aspect. Because it is made of relatively thick aluminum metal is both rugged and lightweight. This allows it to easily be moved around or packed away and traveled with. I have moved the one that I have all around the house, I have also taken it with me to numerous college courses, both those in which I am a student, and those in which I am the instructor. Unlike a lot of supposedly similar stands, it has a perfect cutout for charging cable. So if you are going to leave your tablet in one place for an extended period of time, as I do now, your tablet can live on charge without a problem. My stand is now the relatively permanent home of my Kindle on my reading desk.

Another, enormous advantage, of this stand, is that it is very… Cost-effectively priced. At its current price of $15 and change, or something like that, and even a higher price, it is inexpensive enough that you can buy a few and I will be doing shortly. The second one that I will be purchasing, will probably be permanent home of a new android tablet which I will use for streaming and playing music over some Bluetooth speakers to replace my outdated bulky stereo system, which by the way I hardly ever use anyway anymore.

In fairness, the only small "Con" that this stand has is that it does not have a second hinge at the base to make it completely foldable to flat. If it had a second hinge to fold flat it would be even better and completely perfect rather than nearly perfect, but as it is is small enough that it can be packed away and carried easily. There are other stands that fold flat, but in my experience most of them are made of plastic and they break easily.

So in conclusion, as I said in the title this is a nearly perfect tablet stand which is which is everything most people will ever need in a tablet stand and, in its simplicity is far superior to war expensive and complex competitors that usually come in multiple pieces and are often made of easily breakable materials

I am only saying this so that you can get an idea of how absolutely essential to good tablet stand would be for me. I really can't hold tablets or phones in my hand for any length of time without feeling pain, much like another video reviewer on here who has carpal tunnel in both hands. For us holding things even relatively late things in our hands for any extended period of time is really not a possibility.
Okay, with that money should out-of-the-way they that I now remember really working to find the ideal tablet stand for my iPad, at the time. An iPad that I no longer own, by the way. I remembered that I struggled and searched for long time, mainly because at the time I had limited experience with tablets and didn't know what I would need. So naturally I thought I would need something complex and expensive. :-) WRONG. But that's my nature. I dried out three or four other types of tablet stands, bought them and either immediately return them or threw them away. Most of them were much bulkier and more complex. Most of them were also made of plastic. If you haven't bought a tablet stand before, don't buy a plastic one. It probably will not last.

This tablet stand is superior to most all the others, because it is neither complex nor bulky. It seems perfectly designed, in its simplicity. The designers seem to have carefully considered every aspect. Because it is made of relatively thick aluminum metal is both rugged and lightweight. This allows it to easily be moved around or packed away and traveled with. I have moved the one that I have all around the house, I have also taken it with me to numerous college courses, both those in which I am a student, and those in which I am the instructor. Unlike a lot of supposedly similar stands, it has a perfect cutout for charging cable. So if you are going to leave your tablet in one place for an extended period of time, as I do now, your tablet can live on charge without a problem. My stand is now the relatively permanent home of my Kindle on my reading desk.

Another, enormous advantage, of this stand, is that it is very… Cost-effectively priced. At its current price of $15 and change, or something like that, and even a higher price, it is inexpensive enough that you can buy a few and I will be doing shortly. The second one that I will be purchasing, will probably be permanent home of a new android tablet which I will use for streaming and playing music over some Bluetooth speakers to replace my outdated bulky stereo system, which by the way I hardly ever use anyway anymore.

In fairness, the only small "Con" that this stand has is that it does not have a second hinge at the base to make it completely foldable to flat. If it had a second hinge to fold flat it would be even better and completely perfect rather than nearly perfect, but as it is is small enough that it can be packed away and carried easily. There are other stands that fold flat, but in my experience most of them are made of plastic and they break easily.

So in conclusion, as I said in the title this is a nearly perfect tablet stand which is which is everything most people will ever need in a tablet stand and, in its simplicity is far superior to war expensive and complex competitors that usually come in multiple pieces and are often made of easily breakable materials

text:
I purchased this refurbished case for my iPad Pro, seeking a cost-effective alternative to the exorbitantly priced new keyboard cases on the market. The case functions superbly and presents a significant value, especially when compared to new cases priced between $150 to $300.

The craftsmanship of the case is commendable, and it proves to be quite reliable in daily use. However, I've encountered a few design challenges, presumably from Apple's original specifications. The case is top-heavy, which makes it prone to tipping backward and causing the iPad to fall when jostled, especially when used on my lap. To mitigate this, I applied clear packing tape to overlap the screen slightly, extending about a half-inch behind the case on strategic points between the volume buttons and around the speakers. This makeshift solution has enhanced the stability significantly.

Despite these workarounds, it's worth noting that the case's magnets could be stronger, and it lacks protective edges around the tablet, leaving the sides vulnerable. For those considering a purchase, I recommend looking for cases that offer robust edge protection.

The seller did an excellent job refurbishing this case, and their work is commendable. If you're in the market for a refurbished case, I suggest considering this company first—you won’t regret it.
I bought this case hoping to use it with my iPad Pro. It works very well. I've shopped for similar cases, but paying $150 to $300 for a keyboard case is just ridiculous. That's why I was looking for a gently used case.

The case is very nice to use, absolutely relyable. I've used a few work-arounds to coap with Apple's design flaws.

The case is quite top heavy, and tends to fall backword if jossled. When using it on my lap, this can happen easily. The result is that the iPad falls off the case, hits the ground, and drives me nuts. My work around is to use clear packing tape overlapping the screen by about a half inch, folding behind the case. I put one between the volume buttons and the corner, and another between the two speakers on the left. Now it seems to stay on. I've seen other cases that have better and stronger magnets. Apple also made the case nearly exactly the size of the tablet, so even if it were to stay in the case, the edges and sides are unprotected. My suggestion would be to go for a case with protective edges.

I have no problem with this company, they did an excellent job with my case before I got it. I'd suggest shopping here first. You won't regret it.

text:
I have a 5th gen iPad Air and I wanted one of these smart folio covers for it because I like the idea of not having to charge the keyboard or connect it to Bluetooth. One thing I could not figure out with this one was whether or not it would fit the 5th gen iPad Air, as the description doesn't say it and there is another one specifically sold for 5th gen that is $100 more. I ultimately compared the size of 4th gen and 5th gen and they were nearly identical (the thickness is slightly different, by something tiny like a millimeter). I figured to save $100, it was worth it to try given the size difference was so minimal it probably wouldn't matter. But "probably" isn't "definitely" so....

I can tell you that it definitely does not matter.

This folio fits my 5th gen perfectly. I thought I would switch between this and the normal smart cover when I didn't need the keyboard, but I don't actually do that. This one work so well and is comfortable for me to use and hold, even when it's in its "flipped back" position, that I never found a real reason to switch between the two options.

Here's some general feedback:

--Fits the 5th gen iPad Air, which is cost-saving
--Does not require pairing or charging
--Does not drain the battery (no noticeable difference at all with the battery)
--has two positions you can set the iPad in when looking to type, straight up like a laptop or slightly angled. Sits well in both positions
--Strong magnetic closures so it does not feel like it's going to fall off, fall down, or dislodge. Even when you flip the cover closed abruptly
--keyboard itself is covered with a very thin cloth-like material. I didn't even notice it at first. But because it is fabric, it can't possibly scratch the screen (also makes it easier to clean and wipe down, and there's no spaces between the key and where the key sits for dust and particles to get lodged in between)

Great value on this. Refurbished/Renewed was just as good as brand new. I would have had no idea this wasn't a brand new item. Highly recommended for folks looking for a keyboard cover that is easy on the wallet and on the battery of your device.

Ultimately, I decided to go with the brand I was familiar with, Huion so I took the leap and got this. Here is my experience.

I just got the tablet today and the first thing is that the delivery even came earlier than was announced ✅

It was packed in a huge Amazon box to protect the smaller product from damage ✅

Now for the unboxing and initial experience. Note that I will change my rating once I paint on this or if there's any trouble down the line.

I was very nervous because of some bad experiences that others had, so I started up my tablet with a bit of concern.

Prayed so hard and I was so happy when it actually worked first without the display.

There was a little difficulty when I connected the HDMI cable for the screen though because first it was showing that there was no signal but then after toggling the HDMI cable it started to show the screen and everything.

Another reviewer had said that it worked right out of the box and I was skeptical about that but it's true 😯 And I think that happened for me because I have the other tablet with driver installed.

I had just tried it for fun before uninstalling the driver and was so pleasantly surprised that it works with my old Huion driver for my q11k pen tablet. I suspected that there would be some unity between drivers but still!

But as the driver for the pen tablet was most likely outdated, I went to the website and downloaded the newest driver which was a 15.132 (or something) version when I was using the 14.1 version ( the newest driver was updated in 2022 so I got that and uninstalled the old one)

The test:

I did a few circles and lines in CSP to test the pen and it is working well 😏

The screen is a bit bright but it can be adjusted. The colors are nice too. I can't wait to paint on it but not tonight...I'm tired after pulling an all nighter to paint yesterday 😩

I also customized the keys on the side of the tablet and stuck the stickers they provided to identify which key is which.

These stickers are such a nice touch for me ✅ because with my other pen tablet there weren't any stickers and it was always confusing to remember which key was which. And since I work in a darkened space that's even worse so I never used the keys. I'm grateful for this now.

My laptop doesn't even have a battery but it works with it. I thought that would have been an issue but I use the adapter that comes with the display tablet just in case.

I'm good to go and that's it I don't think I need to buy anything else because this is perfect.

Even my setup is perfect for me because now I don't regret not buying a tablet stand at all. I am using the box that the Huion kamvas tablet came in as a stand 😅

How I do it is use half the box to rest the tablet and the other half the rest my laptop and I am as happy as ever because it has elevated the laptop and the tablet and is comfortable to use. So the box gets a 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ for being sturdy and having a recyclable purpose 😅

As my bed is my workspace, I only have a small space to sleep on now though but that is something I can work around. Do artists sleep anyways? 🙈

So that's it. Fast delivery. Very easy to use. No disappointment.... If I think of anything else or my experience changes I'll update this 👍

Update:
03/July/23
I have done a few paintings on this so far. The only problem I've experienced with it is how sometimes the hot keys will reset, particularly the long one that you can use to scroll / zoom in or out. But that isn't a huge issue for me because everything else is great.

I love painting on this without the delay of making sure my pen tablet and my hand is cooperating.

It's a lot less of a headache than what I was using before.

Oh and I didn't buy a remote for extending the shortcut keys. I simply bought a wireless keyboard and mouse and that has been the best thing ever in using this.

This display tablet is perfect for me. I use it for everything: watching movies, my writing, art and video editing. It's just so convenient to be able to recline with it on my lap.

And let me say, I never thought that I'd be painting on a tablet while lying down! Works for the days when I'm tired after work or just woke up and I don't want to sit down and paint. Good for the back!

So this encourages me to paint more since using it is painless. Plus it's already in my hand when I'm using it for something else so I'd just open CSP and start working on one of my many procrastinations. It doesn't get ignored like my pen tablet that would be to the side of my bed crying out to be used for art and getting used as a coaster instead 🙈

Conclusion: I love this display tablet. Painting is a whole lot more precise, fun and a tad bit easier.

Will update with more as time goes along!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Okay so I have the Huion Inspiroy q11k pen tablet. That is a decent tablet but the pen is a bit glitchy and the customizable keys never worked. Still I'd give it 4.5 out of 5 so when I started to get the itch for a display tablet, I researched so many brands that I got sick of research 😔

Ultimately, I decided to go with the brand I was familiar with, Huion so I took the leap and got this. Here is my experience.

I just got the tablet today and the first thing is that the delivery even came earlier than was announced ✅

It was packed in a huge Amazon box to protect the smaller product from damage ✅

Now for the unboxing and initial experience. Note that I will change my rating once I paint on this or if there's any trouble down the line.

I was very nervous because of some bad experiences that others had, so I started up my tablet with a bit of concern.

Prayed so hard and I was so happy when it actually worked first without the display.

There was a little difficulty when I connected the HDMI cable for the screen though because first it was showing that there was no signal but then after toggling the HDMI cable it started to show the screen and everything.

Another reviewer had said that it worked right out of the box and I was skeptical about that but it's true 😯 And I think that happened for me because I have the other tablet with driver installed.

I had just tried it for fun before uninstalling the driver and was so pleasantly surprised that it works with my old Huion driver for my q11k pen tablet. I suspected that there would be some unity between drivers but still!

But as the driver for the pen tablet was most likely outdated, I went to the website and downloaded the newest driver which was a 15.132 (or something) version when I was using the 14.1 version ( the newest driver was updated in 2022 so I got that and uninstalled the old one)

The test:

I did a few circles and lines in CSP to test the pen and it is working well 😏

The screen is a bit bright but it can be adjusted. The colors are nice too. I can't wait to paint on it but not tonight...I'm tired after pulling an all nighter to paint yesterday 😩

I also customized the keys on the side of the tablet and stuck the stickers they provided to identify which key is which.

These stickers are such a nice touch for me ✅ because with my other pen tablet there weren't any stickers and it was always confusing to remember which key was which. And since I work in a darkened space that's even worse so I never used the keys. I'm grateful for this now.

My laptop doesn't even have a battery but it works with it. I thought that would have been an issue but I use the adapter that comes with the display tablet just in case.

I'm good to go and that's it I don't think I need to buy anything else because this is perfect.

Even my setup is perfect for me because now I don't regret not buying a tablet stand at all. I am using the box that the Huion kamvas tablet came in as a stand 😅

How I do it is use half the box to rest the tablet and the other half the rest my laptop and I am as happy as ever because it has elevated the laptop and the tablet and is comfortable to use. So the box gets a 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ for being sturdy and having a recyclable purpose 😅

As my bed is my workspace, I only have a small space to sleep on now though but that is something I can work around. Do artists sleep anyways? 🙈

So that's it. Fast delivery. Very easy to use. No disappointment.... If I think of anything else or my experience changes I'll update this 👍

Update:
03/July/23
I have done a few paintings on this so far. The only problem I've experienced with it is how sometimes the hot keys will reset, particularly the long one that you can use to scroll / zoom in or out. But that isn't a huge issue for me because everything else is great.

I love painting on this without the delay of making sure my pen tablet and my hand is cooperating.

It's a lot less of a headache than what I was using before.

Oh and I didn't buy a remote for extending the shortcut keys. I simply bought a wireless keyboard and mouse and that has been the best thing ever in using this.

This display tablet is perfect for me. I use it for everything: watching movies, my writing, art and video editing. It's just so convenient to be able to recline with it on my lap.

And let me say, I never thought that I'd be painting on a tablet while lying down! Works for the days when I'm tired after work or just woke up and I don't want to sit down and paint. Good for the back!

So this encourages me to paint more since using it is painless. Plus it's already in my hand when I'm using it for something else so I'd just open CSP and start working on one of my many procrastinations. It doesn't get ignored like my pen tablet that would be to the side of my bed crying out to be used for art and getting used as a coaster instead 🙈

Conclusion: I love this display tablet. Painting is a whole lot more precise, fun and a tad bit easier.

Will update with more as time goes along!

text:
this review is for the kamvas 13” gen 3.

i will cut to the chase – i liked it so much that i purchased the 16” gen 3 model the next day. then i used both for 1.5 months to really get a feel for the devices. my verdict is that they rock and were worth every penny.

yesterday i gave my kamvas 13” away to a friend as a gift through no fault of the device itself (tbh i wanted to do something nice for my friend). we set up the device for my friend yesterday and then drew with it all night. friend loves it. friend was able to easily adapt from using an ipad to using a kamvas. friend has never owned a tablet of this type before while my perspective is coming from owning a wacom cintiq pro and an xp pen artist pro gen 2.

the setup and drivers are finicky, but that’s just the nature of this sort of device. if you are struggling with setup, check your display settings in windows and check your workspace settings in the huion app. make sure that those both match and that you have selected the correct monitor in the huion driver app. then do a system restart. this will solve your problems 9 times out of 10.

the kamvas 13” gen 3 has a plastic body for its build, so i have been babying it and storing it in a case. this is the way to go. considering its $200 price point, i would consider it to have been a very good investment if it lasts 1-2 years. if it lasts longer, i will be an even happier customer on behalf of my friend who now owns it.

text:
My iPad Pro is a 2021 model as is my OG Apple Magic Keyboard. In the 4 years since purchasing the set up my iPad Pro is thankfully still going strong but the OG Magic Keyboard has definitely seen better days with significant seam splitting around the edges and a couple of annoying sticky keys. Okay, so time for a new keyboard was the original plan but not as simple as first anticipated. Firstly it’s almost impossible to find an OG 12.9’ Magic Keyboard (pretty sure Apple have ceased production) and when one is found was cost prohibitive. Fine, time to explore 3rd party keyboards that fit a 12.9’ iPad and after much research landed on this product and its been really good

✅ Is backlight with 3 backlight brightness levels

✅ Fitted my 12.9’ iPad Pro perfectly

✅ Seems to have a long battery life - I can sometimes be on it for 5+ hours a day and its yet to run out of juice (charges separately to the iPad and connects via bluetooth)

✅ Keys feels nice to depress (soft) not unlike the OG Apple Magic Keyboard

✅ Great value for money in comparison to purchasing an OG Apple equivalent

✅ Has a responsive Trackpad which also allows for a Right Click activation (some trackpads don’t have this feature)

✅ The iPad snaps securely magnetically onto the back of the keyboard just like a Magic Keyboard

✅ Adds a little extra weight in comparison to a Magic Keyboard but not significantly so

But all is not perfect with a few niggles

❌ There is no IOS Globe button found on Apple Keyboards which requires learning some keyboard shortcuts to get around some input needs. For example to bring up Emojis you will need to press control / cmd / spacebar. You do get used to using keyboard commands but there is a learning curve when used to a Globe Button

❌ I am not a fan of the angle of the iPad once in place - I would prefer it to be tilted back further because it largely sits vertically. This is possibly a personal preference and others may be perfectly okay with the screens verticality

❌ iPad and this keyboard connect via bluetooth meaning whilst using this combination the iPad cannot to another Bluetooth device without disconnecting from the Keyboard first

Honestly I am very satisfied with this product and the difference between the OG in terms of features and functionality really is marginal. However the huge advantage here is price representing excellent value for money

A few small niggles yet happy to give . .

5 Stars

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently purchased a refurb 2021 12.9 iPad Pro here on Amazon and wanted the Magic Keyboard to go with it as it is absolutely the best accessory for the tablet other than the Apple Pencil. The seller I purchased from is A4C and the item was described as “Excellent”. Mine was packaged in the OEM Apple box but had 2 round sticker seals vs the shrink warp if you bought it new.

There was a very slight dent in the lower right corner of the box and I’m wondering if this is how a perfectly new item turns into a refurb. Apple is very stringent with how their items are packaged and displayed and may allow 3rd party resellers to refurb them if the item still looks and works like new when they open it up to inspect for damage. I’m just speculating here but I think I might not be that far off.

The keyboard had clearly been examined by the seller who left their warranty card inside the box before resealing it. The item was not placed back in the plastic sleeve that it usually gets packed in from the factory while it sits inside the box. But the owner’s manual was still included along with the “spacer” box that is the same thickness of the ipad to keep the keyboard packaged tightly inside the box.

I examined the entire keyboard with a fine tooth comb under bright light and there was zero evidence that anyone had used it at all. There were no scuff marks, rips, tears, scratches, lint on any of the surfaces or inside the keyboard. The keys all look pristine. Keyboards have a tendency to get a “sheen” on them as they wear from use and all the keys looked dull as they should fresh from the factory. My iPad Pro connected perfectly to the keyboard vis the built in magnets and all the keys lit up and worked. In fact, I’m typing this very review with this Magic Keyboard.

I was lucky enough to snag mine at almost 50% off from the $349 MSRP. Pricing will fluctuate based on vendor and demand. But i would jump on these refurbished units when they are in stock as it is downright ludicrous to pay what Apple sells them for at full price. And you have 90 days to return it if you are not truly satisfied with your purchase so you have nothing to lose.
