text:
Me sorprendió que, aunque fuera un producto reacondicionado, parece que fuera completamente nuevo.
El teclado tiene una sensación super cómoda.
Aunque está en inglés y no tiene caractéres especiales como ñ, acentos o diéresis, puedes añadirlos sosteniendo (por ejemplo) la n y te da la opción para ñ, como lo que haría con los acentos en el teclado del celular; incluso creo que tiene más opciones que otros teclados en español. Por otro lado, de todas formas el autocorrector es muy intuitivo, así que muchas veces solo escribo y dejo que entre en acción.
Antes tenía un teclado Logi con controles adicionales (play/pause, volumen, adelantar, pantalla, etc.) bastante cómodos, así que en un principio tenía dudas porque este no los trae, PERO… realmente no me han hecho falta. Puedes dar play/pause con la barra espaciadora, adelantar/retroceder con las flechas, no trae el control para el brillo de pantalla… de todas formas no le movía tanto y lo puedo hacer desde los accesos rápidos, el único que extraño es el de volumen, aunque tal vez se pueda configurar (no lo sé). Ahora, si me dan a elegir entre los controles adicionales y la sensación de escritura del teclado, me quedo con la sensación de éste teclado. He trabajado con otros teclados de diferentes marcas y este me gusta tanto que ya no quiero trabajar con otros jajaja.
Lo hemos probado con iPad Pro 12.9” de 3ª y 6ª generación, y con ambas funciona muy bien.

En cuanto al color… había leído que el blanco se ensucia casi con nada, pero por la diferencia de precio con el negro, me animé por el blanco. Tengo casi 2 meses trabajando con él (rudo) y sigue como nuevo. Lo que sí es que siempre limpio mi base de trabajo y me lavo las manos antes de empezar, así que si eres de los que trabajan donde no hay acceso fácil para hacerlo, tal vez te convenga elegir el negro. Le han caído gotas de café, pero limpiando luego luego con paño húmedo se la ha quitado por completo sin dejar manchas.

En cuanto a la protección para el iPad, pues no cubre las orillas aunque tiene como 1mm de extensión (no suficiente para mi gusto), pero le compré un protector compatible y lo solucioné. Pesa más? Pues sí, pero eso de poder usarla como iPad en 0.5 segundos está genial.

También me gusta mucho poder cargar el iPad desde el teclado, o tener el acceso por ambos lados porque no siempre se puede alargar el cable hasta donde lo quieres, verdad? (Como cuando una trabaja en la cama jajaja).
Obviamente, también me encantó que su precio fuera la mitad. Si eres de los que tiene dudas por ser reacondicionado, te puedo decir que desde el principio ha tenido un uso ultra rudo (entre 8 y 14 horas al día, 7 días a la semana (Estoy haciendo posgrado, no me juzguen jejeje)), y sigue funcionando perfecto.

También había leído algo negativo relacionado con la duración de la batería: yo no noto diferencia alguna. La única vez que me fijé, con la pila al 100%, me dió 10 horas de uso casi continuo antes de llegar al 5%, que es básicamente el mismo tiempo de uso con mi teclado anterior. También la he dejado puesta en stand by (cerrada) durante 24 horas y sólo bajó 1% la batería. Muy bueno, si me preguntan a mí.

Aunque no puede variarse la intensidad del teclado retroiluminado, puedo decir que tiene un tono muy agradable y una intensidad suficiententemente buena para ver las teclas en la oscuridad, pero suficientemente suave para no ser molesta; además, se apaga después de unos segundos de no usarlo y se enciende si tocas el trackpad, alguna tecla o la pantalla, lo que me parece muy conveniente si estás viendo pelis, por ejemplo, porque no estorba la luz.

También me gusta mucho el diseño flotante tan firme que tiene. Con otros diseños, los soportes perdieron firmeza después de un tiempo y tuve que acabar comprando un soporte adicional. Este no se ve que vaya a perder firmeza en muuuuucho tiempo. No se le pueda dar la vuelta, pero no me hace falta realmente: si saco el iPad, cierro el teclado y trabajo sobre el teclado cerrado, me da una inclinación suficiente para poder trabajar cómodamente.

Y lo cómodo que es escribir en él… Amo la sensación de las teclas! Creo que no hay uno que se le compare en ese sentido. Si eres alguien que escribe tanto como yo, seguro que lo entiendes. Si no, es algo así como cambiar de máquina de escribir mecánica a teclado de computadora.
Lo compraría otra vez? Espero que no “tenga que” hacerlo pronto, pero definitivamente sí.

Updated Review:
While I really loved this case originally, it stopped working within 6 months. I assumed it must be my fault or something because I had loved the first one I bought for over a year. Unfortunately, it was outside the warranty, so I bought another in March 2023.

I mostly use my iPad to watch shows or read, but I used the keyboard once a month to take notes during a committee meetings as secretary. Yet, at the end of June 2023, it stopped working yet again.

Both times, most of the keys have stopped registering. This time, caps lock is stuck “on” and I can’t even get the keyboard as a whole to turn off.

Unfortunately… there’s only a month warranty on the product. So twice in less than a year I’m left hanging. I’ve emailed the company, but they responded that I’m outside of warranty.

Despite originally loving this product, I cannot in good faith suggest a product that stops working within a few months. I think my next move is to order on the actual Zagg website as they have extensive warranties and have been amazing to work with in the past — they just can’t fulfill warranties on products bought by a 3rd party.

********************
Original Review:
I use my iPad mini like a computer all the time. I originally had this keyboard on my first iPad mini, but after I got a new one, I thought I could go with one that didn't seem so hefty (read: I wanted a super cute pink one instead). Dear reader, let me tell you, that was a mistake. I finally decided after 2 years of hardly using my iPad that maybe if I had the same keyboard I had before that I would use it more. And I do!

It is hefty, but in a sturdy kind of way not a too heavy kind of way. The iPad section easily pops off if I just want to have that without the keyboard. The keyboard's battery life lasts and lasts, and easily connects to the iPad.

People are always asking me where I got it and are saying how cute my "tiny laptop" is. Plus, it's made doing my on-the-go writing way easier. My fingers fit perfectly to the keys and I type just as easily as I do my full sized laptop. Lastly, I no longer have to worry about being clumsy... I've dropped this thing a few times and it's protected.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My older (10.5”) iPad is running out of options for a keyboard/case. Bought a few cheaper ‘rotaty’ style cases, minimal protection but they worked great for a while, then the hinge broke the case and it was always past the warranty. When the last one went in less than a month, I opted for something better. Read the mostly positive reviews on this guy. Bit the bullet and grabbed it. Well, the Zagg is WELL BUILT!!! It’s now past 90 days and it’s still solid as a rock! I found I miss a dedicated ‘Screen Grab’ key, but I can get around that. My ONLY disappointment is I miss having a trackpad, but I can see and understand why it’s not offered, and it’s not a deal breaker. Keyboard battery life seems quite reasonable. Others commented on keyboard failures after 6 months or so, I guess I’ll find out. But until then, I am beyond happy with this case. Would I buy another? In a heartbeat!

UPDATE - 4 months in and it WAS holding up quite well, occasionally missing a space bar click, but nothing horrible. Today the iPad was left on the roof of the car and subsequently ended up on the ground, in the road and lost! Discovered it missing at home and went crazy. Found that someone had picked it up and was wondering what to do. I got the iPad back with just some minor scratches on the Zagg case! Well done to Zagg for the awesome protection of my iPad! The keyboard wasn’t quite as fortunate, the hinge is now one dimensional! The stylus is now truly one dimensional! Another Zagg is on order, with pleasure!

text:
Ever since I got my new iPad Air and the updates to iPad OS I was desperate to try using an iPad keyboard case and actually do more than just content consumption on this expensive piece of glass. But I also refused to pay $400 for the Apple Magic Keyboard. After trying a few crummier cases I finally came upon this one, and am happy to report it is SO CLOSE to being perfect.

Let's start with the good: Setup couldn't be easier. Just turn it on, pair in the bluetooth setting pane and away you go. The magnets are strong, but not so strong that you can't easily remove the iPad when you need to. It holds a charge for a surprisingly long time: I've yet to charge it and have been using it basically every day since getting it nearly 2 weeks ago. The backlight is adjustable and, perhaps wisely, doesn't stay on indefinitely (like on, say, a laptop keyboard) to preserve battery life. It has multiple brightness settings and colours.

The keys are *more or less* full size; a few keys are smaller (like the " key) but on the whole typing is a perfectly decent experience. Is it as nice as my MacBook Pro? No. But it's good enough that I can actually compose notes or emails and type longer that 2 minutes without getting frustrated (which is more than can be said of some of the cheaper keyboard cases I tried).

It's also nice and sturdy. I've yet to have it fall over and the adjustable angle of the screen is great; I do wish it was slightly *more* adjustable, but it works well enough. Having not used the first party Magic Keyboard version I can't really say how similar or not it is to that, but for my needs it's been working great.

Now for the less good: the trackpad on this thing isn't the best. Part of why I got it was because of the trackpad and the newer features in the latest version of iOS to take advantage of trackpads. The problem is the trackpad click is completely unreliable. You really have to click the very bottom edge to get it to register a click. I'm not sure if this is the same across the board or just I got a lemon because I've actually tried similar keyboard cases from this manufacturer for other sized iPads (long story short, I got them through Amazon Vine thinking they were for an 11-inch Air when they were in fact not) and the trackpads on those seem to have a much better click. I also found the tracking speed to be WAY too fast to actually use the thing.

The better news is that both of these things have some fixes. You can turn on trackpad taps in the iPad settings so you don't actually have to click, and you can also adjust the tracking speed. With that being said, there's still been multiple times when my palm has registered as a tap/drag and sent my insertion point flying while typing and it drives me insane. Long story short: the trackpad is the worst part of this otherwise fantastic case.

As for the case itself: it's a little on the heavy side, but that makes sense since it has to act as a counterweight so it doesn't topple over. It has a nice soft touch feel and while I wish it came in more exciting colours than black or white (how about a nice forest green?), they look fine. They're a bit of a fingerprint magnet though so be aware...

When you consider this is a 1/4 of the price of the Apple version, it's a great deal. It has its flaws but they're not *deal breakers* and of all the iPad keyboard cases I've played with this is the best one. I now actually use my iPad for more than just watching videos, which makes it worth the purchase.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this tablet the same day it was released!
I'll start with Pros and cons, and go into the story of what I was looking for and the main issue I had below.
Pros:
- No etched glass "rainbow pixilation" - its very clean and smooth with no weird light refraction happening. Please view close up photos.
- Buttery smooth, I really love the high pressure sensitivity (newer users won't feel a difference between 16k over 8k, but people drawing for many many years will noticed the difference immediately.)
- Crazy thin parallax, I forgot parallax was even a thing because of this device.
- Great design, buttons and dials all feel great.
- Quality hardware*: Does not feel cheap or clacky, it's just the right weight and solid form (*could use better adhesive, more on this later)
- I really love the feel of everything: the screen, the pen, the buttons, the dials.
- The third button is heaven, further the tool wheel it pulls up really increases the range of efficient work. Little extra ditbit is the driver UI is super clean, very nice touch.
- No diagonal jitter.
- 1080p is clean in this screen size.
- Huion customer service is A++++ (more on this below)
- I love it's thick tapered pen, I don't like pencil-style styluses for drawing tablets.

Cons:
- It can get a bit too warm on the port side after a few hours of use. Just warm enough to be uncomfortable, I have to take a breaks by turning it off to let it cool down. This usually happens around the 3 hour mark, and cools down quickly.
- Relatively dark screen, only gets up to 200 nits, which is a bit of a bummer, so its not very good in bright situations. I did found a workaround with this by playing with the settings, but you do end up with too much high contrast, so you are potentially losing some of the color range. I'm okay with it as it is a balance with making it power efficient, which I was prioritizing for this on-the-go setup. Simply don't sit in the sun and you'll be good!
- I feel it's almost a bit long for backpacking it, but it does have to accommodate the buttons and dials.

TL:DR: Wanted tablet for school, when in my past life was a professional artist so I was picky. The tablet received had a physical issue where the screen was pulling up from the case near the C-port, but Huion came through with a replacement, and I received EXCELLENT and VERY SWIFT assistance from Huions customer support team. They made the replacement process genuinely pain-free.

So as the title states, I'm a huge XP-PEN fan, all my models at home/for work have been XP-PEN.
So when I started school I wanted a graphic tablet for on the go.
My requirements were:
- Portability: Must be small but large enough, slim and lightweight
- Energy efficient: the lower the better, but enough balance for a bright enough screen
- A dial: I became spoiled with dials from XP-PENs pro series at home.
- Etched Glass Screen: I wanted the screen to last/not get damaged from tons of use, nor did I want to replace any screen protectors.
- Thunderbolt compatible, I wanted a single cable situation. It'd be embarrassing doing the whole 3-1 cable setup in the middle of class.
- Pressure sensitivity: I realllly wanted to get something with 16k pressure.
- Decent Color Gamut ranges: I could have gotten an iPad but I wanted the power of and access of a windows PC.
- Affordability would be cool but not a priority as long as it fit the above.

I researched for a week straight and unfortunately XP-PEN tablets didn't fit this bill all at once so I broadened my search to Huion. I found this tablet the night before it's release just as I was about to settle for something that didn't match enough of my requirements. The Kamvas 13 Gen3 hits ALL of my requirements!

When I received it and tested it, I was blown away. I was VERY satisfied, even with the slightly dark screen. It felt better than my at-home XP-PEN 22r pro which is simply insane to me. Even though I was just testing it, doing nothing serious with it yet, the tactile feel of it was so satisfying that I was sucked in immediately to drawing something much more in-depth than just a few spirals and writing.

A few days in however, I noticed that the screen was pulling up near the C-ports as I could see into the body of the tablet. At first I was worried it was from the heat of use, but my husband mentioned he saw it the first day initially. I quickly registered the tablet and submitted a support ticket. They responded to me within 24 hours, and initially asked if I were able to push it back into place, and if I was okay with that they could offered me a 30.00 refund for the inconvenience. The reason for why it may have been pulling up was that it may have faced some high heat on its travel to me. Makes sense as it was summer and Im out in the desert.
I wanted/need this tablet to last the next 2.5 years of school, so I requested a replacement after some hesitancy. They were able to assist me with processing a replacement easily. They sent me a return label, and sent the replacement after receiving back the original tablet. They were also very patient with me as I lagged a bit during returning the original as by this time, I was in my first rounds of exams in school. The label they sent, was VERY fast, so a day after dropping it off, they had the original back, and a day later I had the replacement on my door step through Amazon. To be frank, I was astounded and in awe by the number of people who assisted me with this process, so professionally and so quickly/efficiently despite the affordability of the device.

The replacement has a 0.01 difference in the screen calibration paperwork, and is in perfect working order - No screen issues this time around and is just as magnificent as the first one, sans screen lifting.

Anyways, this is a lot of words to say I'm a new believer/Fan and will certainly be recommending Huion products to my hobby and professional art friends and professional colleagues from now on!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my first time ever reviewing a product on Amazon but I just had to because the low reviews left me a little nervous I was dropping $215 (it was 20% off when I purchased) on a faulty tablet when I could save my money on a better tablet but I am absolutely in LOVE with this tablet. I have been an artist for over 12 years and I have tried different tablets from Wacom (usually non screen) until I purchased my iPad but it has been getting slow so I decided to purchase my first screen tablet!
This tablet is a beautiful beginner tablet and it is super easy to use. Not to mention the size was bigger than I thought but I am definitely not complaining. The screen is matte and anti glare but not so much as to eat away at the nibs super duper fast like the matte screen protectors for an iPad (I've had to purchase MANY new nibs for my apple pencil.) The buttons are silent but still give a small enough pop so you know you've pressed them and the function of the dials is super easy and are very customizable, I use mine to zoom in/zoom out and rotate my canvas with ease. The box was heavier than I expected and realized that it was the weight of the tablet AND the STAND that comes with it! The stand is very good quality and sturdy and has different levels of tilt so you can adjust it however you'd like.
Drawing on the tablet itself is buttery smooth and the sensitivity is amazing, giving you very precise and consistent lines within the drawing program (Clip Studio for example since that is my main one).
The screen is neither too dim or too bright when messing with some settings, but if you work in the dark like I do, it will be a perfect brightness.
The set up was easy and simple, I have an HP Laptop with limited USB ports but as long as you have 1 HDMI port and two USB ports, you are good to go! They do sell an all in one cable to skip the hassle of all of that but it is $30 on their website and does NOT come with the tablet itself but if you have great cable management, it shouldn't be a problem.
My only complaint is NOT about the tablet itself, but the driver needed to install to customize your keys and let the tablet run better since I did install the driver designated for the tablet however, when I launched up Clip Studio, the cursor offset was SO far off I physically could not draw and I could not find the problem anywhere. BUT I did find the solution! I had a Huion tablet before (Inspiroy H1060P) and had the driver installed previously, so I got rid of the Kamvas driver and downloaded that old one instead and problem was solved! I have not had a problem since but I will update if anything pops up!

In conclusion, the Kamvas 13 (Gen 3) is amazing and functions comfortably and beautifully with Clip Studio (I haven't had a chance to try out other art programs), the pressure sensitivity is great, the customization of the buttons is easy through the driver and it's a really good size for the price. If you are thinking of getting this for yourself on a budget or if you're getting this as a gift for an artist that is starting out or wants to get a bit of an upgrade from their pen tablet, iPad, finger and screen, this is a great beginner tool. Happy drawing!! <3

This 600W Charging Station (15-in-1) is a great all-in-one solution for charging multiple devices at the same time. The 600 watts is the total shared power across all ports, which is more than enough for a full desk or nightstand setup.
It includes two 100W USB-C ports, which work very well for charging laptops. I also like that it has two additional 65W USB-C ports, perfect for fast-charging phones and other USB-C devices. The remaining ports, including the USB-A ports, delivered charging speeds in the 8–15 watt range, which is fine for accessories and smaller devices.

One of my favorite features is the organized layout on top, which makes it easy to keep multiple devices neatly placed instead of having cables everywhere. The wireless charging pad works well with my iPhone, and it also supports Apple Watch and wireless earbuds. I don’t have those devices to test, but it’s nice to have everything built into one station.

Another big plus is that two 100W USB-C cables are included, which adds real value and saves money compared to buying them separately.

Overall, this is a powerful, compact, and well-designed charging station that’s perfect for charging laptops, phones, and accessories all in one place. Highly recommended if you need a high-watt, multi-device charger.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a very nice charging station.
I put it next to my bed. I really like the slots in the top to lay my devices in. I also use it for loose papers and notebooks.
I don't have a wireless charging phone right now but my next phone might be and this will be very handy when that time comes. I did try out though with an old wireless charging adapter that I had on my note 4. When active, one of the two green lives on the front left will turn on. These are fairly bright btw. If you're wirelessly charging a watch (behind the stand) and a phone (against the stand) then both green lights will illuminate. If you don't use wireless charging then there are no lights on the device which is a good thing.
I love how many ports it has, and that it has enough USB A ports. I still have plenty of older stuff so having 4 type A and 8 type C is fantastic. 600W is a lot of power. The orange type C ports will have no problem charging tablets or smaller laptops.
The unit feels sturdy to me and I like the horizontal layout of it. The rubber feet are secure and grip well.

I give it 4.8 stars.
There is only one thing I would change:
It would help if the slots on top had some rubber between them (on top of the charger between each fin). Then my devices would be less prone to sliding around (I had to put the station at an angle cuz my night stand is not flat).

Charging seems to work well. I tested the ports with a USB ammeter and was happy to see 9V show up during fast charging. I don't have enough stuff to really test the limits of this thing.
The gallium nitride mosfets are a great technological advancement. In my experience they do stay very cool. I have only used the unit for about a day but I'll come back and update if anything changes. Overall I'm very happy with it and I would recommend it.

The remaining ports, including the USB-A ports, delivered charging speeds in the 8–15 watt range, which is fine for accessories and smaller devices.

One of my favorite features is the organized layout on top, which makes it easy to keep multiple devices neatly placed instead of having cables everywhere. The wireless charging pad works well with my iPhone, and it also supports Apple Watch and wireless earbuds. I don’t have those devices to test, but it’s nice to have everything built into one station.

Another big plus is that two 100W USB-C cables are included, which adds real value and saves money compared to buying them separately.

Overall, this is a powerful, compact, and well-designed charging station that’s perfect for charging laptops, phones, and accessories all in one place. Highly recommended if you need a high-watt, multi-device charger.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve been a loyal OtterBox user for years, outfitting every iPhone and iPad I’ve owned with their Defender series cases. They’ve always delivered top-tier rugged protection, and I’ve been completely satisfied with the build quality and — most importantly — their outstanding customer support.
I bought this Defender case for my iPad 10th generation about three years ago, and it has held up incredibly well through daily use, drops, and travel. The multi-layer design (hard shell + outer slipcover + port covers) has kept my iPad scratch-free and safe, and the overall protection is still as reliable as day one.
The only issue I’ve encountered is with the built-in tilt-adjusting stand mechanism. After three years of regular use (adjusting it frequently for viewing and typing), two of the little plastic nubs that help lock the stand into position finally broke off. It was disappointing, as the stand no longer holds securely in certain angles.
That said, OtterBox’s customer service stepped up as they always do. I submitted a warranty claim, and they promptly replaced the entire case at no cost for the product itself — I only paid $12.99 for shipping. No hassle, quick turnaround, and they honored their commitment even after three years.
Overall, this is still one of the best rugged cases you can get for the iPad 10th gen. The minor stand wear is something I’ve seen mentioned in a few other reviews over time, but the protection and peace of mind (plus their willingness to replace it) make it well worth it. Highly recommend for anyone who needs serious drop and dirt protection — just be aware the stand components may eventually need that warranty love after heavy, long-term use.
Would buy again? Yes — and I’d happily go through the warranty process if needed.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This case is an Otterbox Defender, complete with all the familiar pro and cons you’ve come to expect from the Defender series.

Pros: the teal is a nice color, not too light to stain easily like many of the brands I’ve been looking at, fits iPad A16 2025 well, the material is slightly grippy and helps with traction when leaning the device or holding it (this is the biggest reason I keep buying the phone cases!), the ridge around the screen and the rear camera is the highest of any case I’ve tried so far, which will provide great protection from scratches on uneven surfaces, all buttons and cutouts work, including the Touch ID, the weight is less than 1lb without the kickstand and less than many of the other cases I tried, materials are sturdy and high quality, frame feels just as strong as the ones that have protected my phone from many drops, falls, and accidental flinging across the parking lot while being much slimmer than other “rugged” case brands, is covered by the amazing OtterBox Warranty for the “lifetime of the product” which is listed as 7 years. I’ve received multiple replacement phone cases utilizing this warranty and customer service has always been amazing to work with!

Cons: this is an Otterbox Defender. Some of the features I love for my phone case make it less than optimal for an iPad case. The kickstand piece that comes separately is heavy, cumbersome, unstable, and very tricky to position, with no comfortable position for on-screen typing and I couldn’t get the portrait orientation to stay—I can’t see myself ever using it, without the kickstand, there is no Apple Pencil storage or lid to cover the screen, which is probably my biggest complaint with this style of case, it’s a bit tricky to install the case, this is definitely something you put on and leave, there is an additional cutout on the screen adjacent to the volume keys that doesn’t match any features on my device, so that’s annoying.

The other important thing to know is that this case comes with a built-in plastic screen protector like the old Defender phone cases did. It doesn’t lay exactly flush to the screen, so with every tap and swipe, you’re pushing the plastic down to meet the glass. It adds a significant amount of glare, impedes the sharpness of the Retina display a bit, and makes the iPad significantly less responsive. I’ve managed to type this review using the on-screen keyboard, but I have to press a little with each tap, unlike using just the glass. It gets very smudgy very fast, doesn’t clean as easily as a glass screen protector, and it’s tricky to do anything involving a lot of swiping. Past experience tells me you’ll want a glass screen protector underneath to protect against scratches as it’s very difficult to get and keep the plastic free of dust and debris. I remember back in the old days, people used to remove the plastic screen protector from the phone cases and use a glass protector instead, but there’s always the risk that may damage the case or impact the warranty coverage.

I’ve tried 5 cases so far, and this is the top contender, but I’ll probably remove the plastic screen protector and purchase a separate iPad stand with multiple angles instead of using the one that’s included. I have a magnetic folio option coming soon that I hope to like better for daily use, but I absolutely have confidence that this case will protect an iPad from lots of wear and tear!

Logitech Support info is sketchy on the subject and I don't believe half the people on Reddit that insist you can connect it to a UR. The check on that is when you turn off Bluetooth in Settings the mouse keeps working and the keyboard stops. Now I have to solve the debate in my head as to whether this thing gets returned.....sigh. Amended 9/22: I solved the receiver problem. I bought an M550L from Amazon that came today. It was equipped with the Bolt Receiver. When I ran the Logi Options+ on Windows 11 looking for the K380s and it took all of 2 seconds to find it. The two work like champs in Ubuntu 24.04.01. The small size and the utility now that the receiver issue is solved makes this K380s a great addition to my complicated office environment and takes two other keyboards out of the crowded picture.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is simply an awesome compact keyboard folio and has been far and away well worth the money. I would argue it has paid for itself, despite not actually generating any revenue but just being there with its feature list, portability, and general usefulness.

I'll also preface by saying that my intention with buying a small Bluetooth keyboard was to pair it with my Galaxy Fold 7 as a mini laptop replacement. This isn't a review of the phone, so I'll quickly just mention that the Fold 7 does have an 8" unfolded display, all of Samsung's multitasking/multi window features, and at $2000 the fates be damned if I wasn't going to make more of this phone than just texting my wife and scrolling YouTube (mind you I paid much less with promo deals, trade-ins, and good old fashioned selling on eBay).

To make this is as much of a "tl;dr" as possible, I'll break it down by section. My usages, must haves, nice-to-haves and cons. Hopefully this helps to give you a quick and informed decision :-).

Usage:

- Work. I'm a software engineer and while I have a primary work laptop, I do occasionally use other devices for things I can quickly do. This can include light dev work, answering emails, taking meetings, or even multitasking with all 3, which I recently had to do and found surprisingly joyous with this mini setup.
- Gaming. To be specific, I mean what is essentially the full gamut of what's possible on Android. This includes native games like Diablo Immortal and the recently released Destiny, emulators up through the Wii era, where I'm currently replaying Wind Waker and trying to get PS3 titles past the intro screen, and finally full Windows titles streamed through GeForce Now and Steam (replaying CP2077 as corpo, GW2, and usually a couple rotating titles).
- Casual usage. This is just standard stuff like web browsing or even writing this actual review.

Must haves:

- Fn-lock, which I found is activated by using the Fn+Del key combo. This was non-negotiable for me. Media keys are nice and all but I need my standard F1-F12 if I'm treating this setup like a laptop. Not to mention, since I'm using this with an actual smartphone, the volume rocker and touchscreen are almost literally a pinky's distance away so having dedicated controls on the keyboard was very unimportant.
- Backlit keys. The 3 levels of brightness (4 if you include turning it off) is a bonus. Could I have lived without backlit keys, yes of course. But in 2025, come on. I've seen Bluetooth earbud cases with cycling RGB LEDs, which, while visually cool and I would absolutely plop down the money for one, is basically pointless. Backlighting a keyboard, even one this small, should just be a given and I'm glad it is in this keyboard.
- A built-in stand. Given that what I'm going for is a mini laptop, I wanted as few separate parts as possible. I have my mouse and headphones, which is pretty standard kit, and my "screen" is my phone so it goes in my pocket. That leaves the focal point that your body is facing in a standard computer setup, i.e. where the keyboard and monitor are. I bought the original Microsoft Surface Pro years ago, and the way that worked with a keyboard is ultimately very similar to this mini laptop setup. The keyboard snaps onto the main laptop part, but unless it's placed on top of something (a desk, your lap, etc) it just hangs lazily because it has no solid hinge with the screen outside of the magnetic attachment. The Surface was large and heavy, though, so shuttling it around was awkward. This keyboard is small and light so it's very easy to just fold it up, move to where I want to go, then unfold.
- A rational, sane, key layout. I have looked at several of these tiny keyboards and one thing that kept striking me was the ridiculous choice for where certain keys should go. Some keys were utterly overloaded with their standard usage, the modified Shift usage, and then an Fn modified usage beyond that. I think in a lot of cases, these choices were done to mimic as much of a 100% keyboard as possible. But, I personally don't think that is worth having to relearn decades of finger memory. Surely, keys like quotation, slash, and question mark have earned their spot on the keyboard without needing to be modified with some Fn combo. Mercifully, this keyboard puts all those needed keys exactly where they should be without any fuss. Not to mention Android recognizes long presses on this keyboard as it normally would and when appropriate, so it's easy to get to accented characters.

Nice-to-haves:

- 7 different backlight key colors plus an 8th cycling "breathing" mode. It basically goes through all 7 colors and fades in and out as it does so.
- Some sort of built-in memory, so it remembers the backlight setting and the FN-lock mode you last set. A nice touch so you don't have to setup the keyboard every time you turn it off/on.
- Phone stand does not "click" into place, but the angle is basically infinitely adjustable.

Cons, since there are some. At ~$35, its affordable, but at that price you shouldn't be expecting anything premium:

- The on/off switch is a little small and at an angle that's a little finicky to actuate. This is more something to get used to than an actual issue.
- The 4 status lights, BT #1, #2, caps lock, and charging seem to be buried deeper in the keyboard housing so they are harder to see unless dead on. A little annoying, mostly for when I want to confirm if the keyboard is charging/charged, but not an issue outside that.
- The overall case quality might leave something to be desired. It's a handsome but can feel cheap. The stand, for example, is pretty obviously a piece of rectangular metal that is connected with a hinge. I could see it getting bent if it were handled improperly. Of course, one could argue that if it did get damaged, it would be a simple matter of taking off the faux leather and replacing the bent bits with new ones from the hardware store.
- The keys require that they be almost fully pressed down before they will register. This might be the biggest sticking point (no pun intended). Combined with the overall smaller keyboard size, this could lead to easier finger fatigue. I have had a few ~2 hours gaming sessions and my left hand did feel a bit more "claw-like" than I'd have liked. It was easy enough to shake off, but I imagine that certain people, my parents who are in their 70s for example, would find the fatigue makes this keyboard unusable for anything longer than writing an email.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I own the smaller version of this keyboard and have been very pleased with it. The 7.5”, however, is not really for extended typing. It fits in a large pocket and it works in your lap, but some of the key compromises are sort of iffy as in some users legitimately won’t be okay with them. For me, it’s ideal for times when I’m wandering around and might want to type something, but I’m not really expecting to do so or if I’m in an arena that has a clear bag policy. It’s more or less the same deal as my reading books on my cell phone. I have an e-reader, but I don’t carry it with me everywhere or all the time the way I do with the phone. In fact, the 7” inch version’s best use may be paired with a cell phone or small tablet.

This, the 9” version has enough room so the apostrophe and quote keys have their own button, It fits most hands more comfortably, and it’s backlit (though I’m not sure anyone needs 7 different backlighting colors).

After years of looking for the right portable keyboard for my tablets, I believe they all involve compromises. I went through a number of foldables and found that the fold invariably results in irregular key sensitivity near the folds over time. More significant, the stowaway keyboard was maybe the only foldable that locked well enough for lap use (is it a patent issue?) Basically, it’s easy to find a place to sit down when you’re out and about; it’s not always easy to find a table or counter, sometimes even in places that have tables.

Rigid keyboards generally hold up better and they tend to have better key feel. The biggest issue is that they don’t fit in pockets or smallish bags. In general, they do work better for lap use simply because they don’t collapse as soon as you start typing on keys near the fold. I do find the better feeling rigid keyboards tend to weigh a pound or more. The other issue is that you often need a separate stand for your device and most case stands for tablets and phones either don’t work in the lap or even the smallest movements cause them to collapse (there’s a reason Zugg still gets a premium for their cases).

There just aren’t many rigid portable cases that come with a cover that doubles as a stand. While I really like the cleverness of origami style stands, a lot of them collapse too easily or have a very small footprint that limits you to table top use. The Surface style stand appears to be the best compromise, assuming the spring for the flap is stable enough.

Bottom line, the Universal Travel Keyboard plus is a rigid keyboard, decently sized and laid out for most hands, that has a built in keyboard case that works in your lap. It fits in any 10” plus bag (it helps that it’s also relatively narrow). I’d say the key feel is good to very good (maybe a little more spongy than clicky but it’s a very positive feel). It’s well under a pound. The adjustable backlighting is useful as is the ability to synch to 2 different devices, though I would mention that if you have the 7” version too it gets confused because the two keyboard synchs appear to interfere with on another. If I were on a trip and could only take 1 keyboard, this might be it. I can type several pages at a time comfortably (though not ideally), can work most anywhere I can sit down, and it’s genuinely if not ultimately portable.

I almost didn't purchase this due to some of the negative reviews. I'm glad I gave it a chance, because it suits my specific needs perfectly.

I use my iPad Pro 11" as a tablet 85-90% of the time, to take notes with, sketch models in Shapr3D, read books, documents, and consume media. The other 10-15% of the time, I found myself wanting a keyboard to respond to lengthy emails and conversations.

The Apple Magic Keyboard is amazing, but I did not like how hefty it made the setup as well as the iPad itself having no protection when off of it to use as a tablet. Other options were too bulky to fit in my already cluttered bag. I narrowed it down to either this keyboard or an official Apple BT Magic Keyboard. Decided to this one a shot before I went the Apple route and I found that it checked most of my boxes.

Pros
- Exact width of my iPad Pro 11 setup, so it looks very sleek and aesthetic.
- Can be used with multiple devices, like your iPhone and AppleTV.
- Super thin and lightweight, with a magnetic protective flap. Stacks with the iPad perfectly.

Cons
- The keys are definitely a bit smaller and cramped, but I found that is the case with the Apple Magic Keyboard case as well.
- The keypress is a tad bit more shallow than the magic keyboard, but found that it isn't an issue for me personally.
- Takes a little but of time to get accustomed to the more cramped layout, found my WPM wasn't as high, but feel that will improve over time.

I find that it works great in tandem w/ the ESR Shift case that allows you to raise the iPad higher and also use it in portrait mode. Give it a shot if your iPad use case is similar to mine. If you do a lot of typing on the iPad, the magic keyboard case or separate magic keyboard is the way to go.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a great little keyboard for pairing with an iPad or a Raspberry Pi. It's really easy to switch between devices with just a button press and perfect for travel.

I use this with my iPad mini. It's perfect for that device as there are no cases with a built-in keyboard made for it and it's about as small and portable as an iPad mini. I really like how slim it is and how I can carry it in a bag or wherever. I keep it in a drawer these days and bring it out when I need to do some serious typing on a touchscreen device.

I also use this with my Raspberry Pi because I don't always use it and don't want to have to pair my Mac keyboard with it so I have this very slim portable keys-to-go that I can flip open, press a button on, and it's connected.

The typing experience is great for long form typing. It's not going to be an experience like you'll get out of a full sized keyboard but it's the best quality and feel and experience you can get from a portable keyboard.

The cover also doubles as a sort of stand so that the keyboard lays at an angle and you get a decent typing angle. Then when you're done you can just flip it shut and travel. You can (but don't have to) turn the keyboard off to save even more power. Speaking of power, this thing last something like a whole year and takes just one replaceable coin cell battery.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I can’t tell you how much I love this keyboard. I’ve been recommending it to everyone who asks me about accessories for their iPads or for traveling, even the ones that DON’T ask.

The profile is perfect for traveling. I even left my MacBook Air at home in favor of my more versatile iPad Mini and this keyboard. It’s about as thin as the iPad itself. Also having an attached cover helps keep the keyboard clean and prevents anything from potentially snagging on the keys when backed in a bag.

Being able to connect to more than one device at a time is great feature. I can pair it to my two iPads and my iPhone and with a push of a button, switch between them.

The typing experience is also very satisfying. There’s just enough key travel to feel like your fingers really are pressing on something tangible and not just tapping on a flat surface. The feel is very similar to the Apple Magic Keyboard, actually.

The length of the keyboard is also terrific. Even with my small hands, I don’t feel cramped when typing on it. It works better than any keyboard that fits my iPad mini and the form factor isn’t cumbersome.

I also love that there’s a purple/lavender option. Slight half a start for having my favorite color.

Only “con” is that I wish the keyboard was re-chargeable and not by battery. This isn’t too much of a big deal and not a dealbreaker as the coin battery inside is touted to last at least a year or longer. Plus with a physical off/on switch, it should preserve the battery life. I don’t foresee having to change it anytime soon however I would have prefer a mechanism to charge it if/when needed.

As you can tell, there were no problems in doing so. Clearly this is not a problem with the phone. The phone works with several other Bluetooth keyboards. It simply does not work with _this_ one.
This is not even a "you get what you pay for" situation. Logitech charges $70.00 for these things on Amazon. It's an absolute scam. You can easily find much better quality keyboards for half the price or less, but few as lightweight and portable, sadly.
If it had worked okay, it felt good to type on and it was the right shape size and weight for carrying anywhere with you. But it didn't work okay, so basically my advice is if you're thinking of buying this, instead take 70 dollars out of the ATM and burn it, it will be more useful to you that way.

Know what you’re buying. I feel like the people who are complaining in reviews didn’t realize what they were purchasing when they purchased it. Of course this keyboard isn’t going to be the most comfortable typing experience, you can just tell that from the pictures.

So what are you sacrificing comfortable typing for? You’re sacrificing it for portability. It’s called “Keys-To-Go”, you’re meant to be able to just throw this in your bag with your tablet and be ok with that. The fact that there aren’t switches/keycaps is what makes it so portable. You don’t have to worry about them breaking or falling off and it makes it easier to clean.

Anyways, typing on this keyboard definitely takes some getting used to. If you’re an experienced/comfortable typist you will adjust quickly. Just be aware that this isn’t a mechanical keyboard, typing on this is pretty funky. You can write papers and essays on it if you need to, it won’t be impossible. I just think it’s important to know what you’re getting yourself into when purchasing this product.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I just got this case so keep in mind I haven’t had more than a day with it.

This is the Magic Keyboard that Apple should have made. 1/3 the cost AND it includes a case for the iPad so when you don’t want to use the keyboard, your iPad isn’t naked! The keyboard is nice and clicky, easy to type on, and I like the backlight and the ability to change the color/brightness. The touchpad is small but responsive and easy to use, I love having a mouse cursor on my iPad! (I wish it was closer to a MacBook touchpad because it pushes down a bit further than I am used to but that is really nit-picky.) It remains to be seen how long this will last but the quality is nice. The manufacturer included a 24-month warranty so as long as they honor that, I can’t see any reason not to buy this case!

PROS:
- price is unbeatable at 1/3 the cost of Apple’s keyboard case with very similar features
- keyboard is clicky and nice to type on, backlight is great and it changes colors and brightness levels
- USB-C charging means I only need to carry one cable to charge either the case or iPad
- feels like a good design, the hinge is sturdy and feels solid nice and the case material is slightly grippy, feels great in my hands with a soft touch
- 24-month warranty seems really stellar (hopefully it lasts so I never have to use it!)
- supports multiple positions you can use it in, landscape or portrait mode (and there are enough magnets to move the iPad further up on the case if you need a slightly different angle or more space to type)

CONS:
- since it’s a Bluetooth keyboard, it needs to be charged separately from the iPad, no pass-through charging like Apple’s Keyboard
- the viewing angle doesn’t go back as far as I’d like and there is only really one angle you can use this case in, but it’s good for typing on a desk or coffee table from the couch
- the whole case+keyboard adds quite a bit of weight to the iPad, this is expected so it’s not really a negative for me
- (ADDED) the case makes the whole combination very top-heavy so it’s quite difficult to type while it’s sitting on your lap; it’s fine on a table or flat surface but any angle and it’s a bit unstable

More pros than cons and for the price, a lot of the negatives are easy to overcome.

If you want a keyboard case for your iPad Pro, you’re looking for something similar to the Magic Keyboard BUT you want to avoid the “Apple tax” — this is a great option on the market. A missing feature compared to Apple’s MK is the pass-through charging. But the trade off is having a solid case around the iPad so you can use it without the keyboard and not feel concerned about dropping and damaging the iPad.

UPDATE:
After using the keyboard case on my iPad Pro 13” for several days now, the viewing angle is actually bothering me more than I assumed it would. There is no flexibility and it doesn’t have any other angles you can use this in. When you remove it from the keyboard, the protective case around the iPad can only sit flat on a table or be held in your hands, making it impossible to use at any normal angle for drawing or casual reading. Unfortunately, this may become a dealbreaker for me as I like to use my iPad in multiple different positions, both on a desk and in my lap. Which this does not support.

(Will update this review if anything changes. Updated once on 11/13/2025 after several days of use.)

There was a lacking in the ESR Rebound in that I missed the Magic Keyboard. I kept finding myself researching the Magic Keyboard and looking at comparison videos even though I claimed to be happy with the ESR Rebound. I couldn’t get it out of my mind! So there you are, I gave in to the $299 on amazon and now I am typing on a keyboard that checks all my boxes, it’s asethetically and functionally JUST RIGHT.

I bought this for my IPad Pro 13 M4, which is ginormous and quite thin. This is awesome but it causes my anxiety over the safety of the iPad to rise to a new level. I upgraded from my iPad Air 4th generation (~11”) with the white Magic Keyboard. I had my iPad Air for about 5 years and I was so used to it I would treat it very casually and throw it around, it was my go to so this big thin iPad is something to get used to.

I loved the Magic Keyboard I had. I couldn’t justify spending the extra money on the Magic Keyboard even at $299 on Amazon this time around. My second go to would have been the Logitech keyboard however even on Amazon at $259 I might as well have shelled out the money for the Apple Magic Keyboard.
After doing some research on compatible keyboards I found ESR made this Rebound Keyboard Case. I already am a big fan of this brand so it made it even easier to choose with the price tag on it being about $100 which is much more affordable than the previously mentioned keyboards that obviously have their quality behind them and their brands as well.

It had all the things I could have asked for in the specs. A case for the random time I take my iPad off the keyboard and backlit keys. Not much to ask for however when I received the keyboard it had so much more! The function keys on the top row, the different colors for backlit keys, it’s sturdy and I feel my IPad is protected.

The feeling of typing is unlike the magic keyboard in that it is clicky, somewhat like a mechanical keyboard but it is obviously not to that quality. I like how it sounds and feels while typing. I appreciate the different colors for the backlit keys however I would have been fine with just a white backlight because of what I’m used to. The trackpad to me feels like a good size, I am used to the 11” Magic Keyboard and it is about the same size, I have to get used to how loud the clicks are on the trackpad, quite different from a Magic Keyboard especially the new one with the haptic feedback. It doesn’t bother me so much as I just tap on the screen if I need to move or click on anything for the most part.

The quality of the material this is made out of is easy smeared onto. If I have lotion or even semi oily hands from cuticle oil, something of that sort it definitely shows on the keys and arm rests. It’s not hard to clean but it’s just a little unsightly and I’m being overly careful with my new big toy so I am constantly cleaning. It might not be a big deal to many but I am a little neat freak.

Many have commented or complained about the weight of the case and keyboard. I actually like it. My iPad has not tipped over as my old iPad Air 4th gen with the Magic Keyboard would constantly which I appreciate because it’s a big iPad and I want to keep it safe instead of having it fall off my lap or fall back on the bed because it’s top heavy. I am not one to travel around with my iPad, being a stay at home mom it does not go very far from my home unless we go on vacation and even then it depends on where we’re going. So I cannot account for traveling weight. I still feel IMO it’s not that heavy and if I were a student or if I used it to bring to work it would not be inconvenient to me. Of course in comparison to the Magic Keyboard and the Logitech keyboard they are much thinner and would be more travel friendly.

The keyboard has its own battery which holds very well. I’ll be using the set up all day starting at 100% and it’ll go down to 90% by the end of the day. It does have a standby mode that it goes to automatically after a certain amount of time. You can charge the keyboard by charging the iPad but it does not work the other way around. It’s very easy to connect to the Bluetooth and I haven’t had any problems with connectivity. There is a slight lag to get it out of standby mode but it’s 2 seconds to wake the keyboard and it’s back and running, not something you’d see in the Magic Keyboard or Logitech but I can live with the 2 seconds to wake up the keyboard to keep $150-200 or more dollars.

For the price this keyboard is with about the same features as the other keyboards and good quality I’m happy with it. I use my iPad everyday for productivity, organization, videos, research, recipes, messaging and browsing. I’m on here more than I am on my phone. This keyboard has been a great affordable addition to my new IPad Pro

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I just got this case so keep in mind I haven’t had more than a day with it.

This is the Magic Keyboard that Apple should have made. 1/3 the cost AND it includes a case for the iPad so when you don’t want to use the keyboard, your iPad isn’t naked! The keyboard is nice and clicky, easy to type on, and I like the backlight and the ability to change the color/brightness. The touchpad is small but responsive and easy to use, I love having a mouse cursor on my iPad! (I wish it was closer to a MacBook touchpad because it pushes down a bit further than I am used to but that is really nit-picky.) It remains to be seen how long this will last but the quality is nice. The manufacturer included a 24-month warranty so as long as they honor that, I can’t see any reason not to buy this case!

PROS:
- price is unbeatable at 1/3 the cost of Apple’s keyboard case with very similar features
- keyboard is clicky and nice to type on, backlight is great and it changes colors and brightness levels
- USB-C charging means I only need to carry one cable to charge either the case or iPad
- feels like a good design, the hinge is sturdy and feels solid nice and the case material is slightly grippy, feels great in my hands with a soft touch
- 24-month warranty seems really stellar (hopefully it lasts so I never have to use it!)
- supports multiple positions you can use it in, landscape or portrait mode (and there are enough magnets to move the iPad further up on the case if you need a slightly different angle or more space to type)

CONS:
- since it’s a Bluetooth keyboard, it needs to be charged separately from the iPad, no pass-through charging like Apple’s Keyboard
- the viewing angle doesn’t go back as far as I’d like and there is only really one angle you can use this case in, but it’s good for typing on a desk or coffee table from the couch
- the whole case+keyboard adds quite a bit of weight to the iPad, this is expected so it’s not really a negative for me
- (ADDED) the case makes the whole combination very top-heavy so it’s quite difficult to type while it’s sitting on your lap; it’s fine on a table or flat surface but any angle and it’s a bit unstable

More pros than cons and for the price, a lot of the negatives are easy to overcome.

If you want a keyboard case for your iPad Pro, you’re looking for something similar to the Magic Keyboard BUT you want to avoid the “Apple tax” — this is a great option on the market. A missing feature compared to Apple’s MK is the pass-through charging. But the trade off is having a solid case around the iPad so you can use it without the keyboard and not feel concerned about dropping and damaging the iPad.

UPDATE:
After using the keyboard case on my iPad Pro 13” for several days now, the viewing angle is actually bothering me more than I assumed it would. There is no flexibility and it doesn’t have any other angles you can use this in. When you remove it from the keyboard, the protective case around the iPad can only sit flat on a table or be held in your hands, making it impossible to use at any normal angle for drawing or casual reading. Unfortunately, this may become a dealbreaker for me as I like to use my iPad in multiple different positions, both on a desk and in my lap. Which this does not support.

(Will update this review if anything changes. Updated once on 11/13/2025 after several days of use.)

text:
I ordered this because I wanted to do some productivity work on a tablet without having to worry about finding a suitable place to prop it up while relaxing on a couch. I have a stand I can use to keep my tablet vertical, but it didn't sit quite right on my lap or on an armrest, and leaving it on an end table was both too far away and caused a pain in my neck after looking in its direction for too long. Comparatively, this keyboard and mouse combo is great for keeping my work right in front of me while keeping my hands free.

Build quality seems good, with solid-feeling components. The buttons are quiet but still satisfyingly tactile, and the included keyboard mat does a good job at keeping dust and crumbs off of the keyboard itself. The only minor nitpick is that the plastic for the battery compartment covers feels a little thin, and I've got a sneaking suspicion that if anything winds up breaking on these items it'll be that. Still, it's a very minor concern.

Connectivity has been perfectly fine for both the keyboard and mouse over Bluetooth. I did test out the USB dongle just to make sure it worked on my PC as well, and it wound up working perfectly fine. I think there was some mild improvement to the range with the 2.4GHz connection over the Bluetooth one, but the distances involved for that test make it unlikely to be a relevant comparison for most people outside of a few niche use cases. Unless you plan to use this from multiple living rooms away, it shouldn't make a difference.

The groove for seating your tablet or phone is deep enough to make my tablet feel relatively secure while it's in position, so long as you don't tilt it too far to one side. However, there is a slight drawback in that it's too thin if you happen to be using a protective case for your tablet. Thinner cosmetic cases should be alright, but I use one that has a 3/4 inch rubber trim around the edge, and it's way too thick for this product. Fortunately for me, I have a few different tablets to choose from, so I've mostly been sticking with the one I'm least worried about having to replace if I should happen to drop it.

Overall, I think this is a great value for a Bluetooth keyboard. It's priced similarly to a lot of its competition, but it also comes with a mouse. I've got a few different options to compare with at home, and it keeps up with more expensive alternatives with ease. Unless you want something flashier or there's a great deal on another product, I can't really think of any reason not to get this one over its competition.

text:
Overall, this keyboard is okay, but I'm not a very big fan.

The keyboard is not travel-friendly. To hold an iPad without tipping over, the base is extra heavy. Including the batteries, the weight is 728g (1.6Lb). It's also thick compared to ultra-low-profile keyboards. On a better note, it has no problem holding the weight of my iPad Air 13 with M2. The cut-out for the tablet is 35.5cm (14") long and 8mm (0.31") wide, so I absolutely need to remove my iPad from its case to fit this keyboard. There's also no back support, and the weight of the entire iPad rests in that little wedge at the bottom.

The typing feel is just okay. The keys wobble a lot but don't jam on their way down. The action is kind of crisp, but there's a strong bouncing when the keys bottom out. In short, it's totally usable but not a high-end feel. It's pretty much what I expected for a keyboard in this price range. The key layout takes a bit of time to get used to. The arrow keys are not easily distinguishable by feel, and the right Shift key is small. On Mac, when connected over Bluetooth, the Option and Command keys follow the Apple layout, but when using the 2.4 GHz dongle, the keyboard follows the PC layout, so they are inverted. It's an easy fix in System Settings, though.

The mouse is flat but pretty good. The USB receiver is stored in the mouse next to the battery compartment. Due to the location of the battery, the mouse is heavier on one side, but it's not bothersome because of the shape of the mouse. It's still easy to hold and pick up. I only have two issues with this mouse. First, the lift-off distance is really high. Normally, it should be 1mm to 3mm. This mouse has a lift-off distance of 5.5mm. I can stack 3 Loonies (Canadian $1 coins) under the mouse, and the sensor is still able to track the mouse pad. This mouse is really not ideal if you are the type to reposition your mouse often. Second, there are no back and forward buttons. The other aspect of the mouse is good. It's easy to transport, the clicks are very quiet, the scroll wheel is ultra grippy, and the wireless connectivity is reliable.

Overall, it's not bad. This is best for people who don't want to spend too much, don't use a case with their tablet or phone, and don't need a portable keyboard.

I ordered this because I wanted to do some productivity work on a tablet without having to worry about finding a suitable place to prop it up while relaxing on a couch. I have a stand I can use to keep my tablet vertical, but it didn't sit quite right on my lap or on an armrest, and leaving it on an end table was both too far away and caused a pain in my neck after looking in its direction for too long. Comparatively, this keyboard and mouse combo is great for keeping my work right in front of me while keeping my hands free.

Build quality seems good, with solid-feeling components. The buttons are quiet but still satisfyingly tactile, and the included keyboard mat does a good job at keeping dust and crumbs off of the keyboard itself. The only minor nitpick is that the plastic for the battery compartment covers feels a little thin, and I've got a sneaking suspicion that if anything winds up breaking on these items it'll be that. Still, it's a very minor concern.

Connectivity has been perfectly fine for both the keyboard and mouse over Bluetooth. I did test out the USB dongle just to make sure it worked on my PC as well, and it wound up working perfectly fine. I think there was some mild improvement to the range with the 2.4GHz connection over the Bluetooth one, but the distances involved for that test make it unlikely to be a relevant comparison for most people outside of a few niche use cases. Unless you plan to use this from multiple living rooms away, it shouldn't make a difference.

The groove for seating your tablet or phone is deep enough to make my tablet feel relatively secure while it's in position, so long as you don't tilt it too far to one side. However, there is a slight drawback in that it's too thin if you happen to be using a protective case for your tablet. Thinner cosmetic cases should be alright, but I use one that has a 3/4 inch rubber trim around the edge, and it's way too thick for this product. Fortunately for me, I have a few different tablets to choose from, so I've mostly been sticking with the one I'm least worried about having to replace if I should happen to drop it.

Overall, I think this is a great value for a Bluetooth keyboard. It's priced similarly to a lot of its competition, but it also comes with a mouse. I've got a few different options to compare with at home, and it keeps up with more expensive alternatives with ease. Unless you want something flashier or there's a great deal on another product, I can't really think of any reason not to get this one over its competition.

text:
Overall, this keyboard is okay, but I'm not a very big fan.

The keyboard is not travel-friendly. To hold an iPad without tipping over, the base is extra heavy. Including the batteries, the weight is 728g (1.6Lb). It's also thick compared to ultra-low-profile keyboards. On a better note, it has no problem holding the weight of my iPad Air 13 with M2. The cut-out for the tablet is 35.5cm (14") long and 8mm (0.31") wide, so I absolutely need to remove my iPad from its case to fit this keyboard. There's also no back support, and the weight of the entire iPad rests in that little wedge at the bottom.

The typing feel is just okay. The keys wobble a lot but don't jam on their way down. The action is kind of crisp, but there's a strong bouncing when the keys bottom out. In short, it's totally usable but not a high-end feel. It's pretty much what I expected for a keyboard in this price range. The key layout takes a bit of time to get used to. The arrow keys are not easily distinguishable by feel, and the right Shift key is small. On Mac, when connected over Bluetooth, the Option and Command keys follow the Apple layout, but when using the 2.4 GHz dongle, the keyboard follows the PC layout, so they are inverted. It's an easy fix in System Settings, though.

The mouse is flat but pretty good. The USB receiver is stored in the mouse next to the battery compartment. Due to the location of the battery, the mouse is heavier on one side, but it's not bothersome because of the shape of the mouse. It's still easy to hold and pick up. I only have two issues with this mouse. First, the lift-off distance is really high. Normally, it should be 1mm to 3mm. This mouse has a lift-off distance of 5.5mm. I can stack 3 Loonies (Canadian $1 coins) under the mouse, and the sensor is still able to track the mouse pad. This mouse is really not ideal if you are the type to reposition your mouse often. Second, there are no back and forward buttons. The other aspect of the mouse is good. It's easy to transport, the clicks are very quiet, the scroll wheel is ultra grippy, and the wireless connectivity is reliable.

Overall, it's not bad. This is best for people who don't want to spend too much, don't use a case with their tablet or phone, and don't need a portable keyboard.

I'd give them a 10 if I could...
I've thought about using a stylus the last couple of years - wasn't sure if they'd work with iPhones. Lately it's been increasingly frustrating with my fingers somehow hitting the letter next to the one I want. It's gotten to the point I was having to back off things I use it for: reading, editing, writing. During Amazon Prime days I decided to take a look, found these Stylus (5 Pcs), 2-in-1 Stylus Pens, and told my wife I couldn't keep waiting. Got them the next day and haven't stopped using them since. I'm typing faster than ever, editing easier, making a fraction of "mistakes," and overall enjoying my phone again. These Stylus (5 Pcs), 2-in-1 Stylus Pens are a great find: lightweight, but substantial. The colors are great. A good amount in this package, plus the included backup tips. I did look at the other packaged options from this vender, but decided on this Stylus (5 Pcs), 2-in-1 Stylus Pen set as the best all around deal. And yes, they've already been added to our Buy Again list.

I knew nothing until I was desperate and got these. Turns out this Stylus (5 Pcs), 2-in-1 Stylus Pen set style has tips on both ends. The one end is the "bubble" that allows you to slide, scroll, even tap. I personally feel like it has "less control" in that I make more mistakes and often get the pressure wrong, almost feeling like a copy of my fingers. I do use it, but not as often and in certain situations. Or if that's the way I picked it up and just start using it.

The other end is an odd looking tip: it's like the end of a ballpoint pen, with a small, round, plastic disk. Yes, you're using the disk that "floats" or "pivots" to how it's being positioned and used. It's all very interesting, and does use a bit of practice, but now that I've gotten comfortable with it, I have a hard time going back to fingers. I'm fine with that and happy to keep using the stylus. The stunning part is that I can scroll, type, edit, and overall use the iPhone with increased speed, ease, accuracy, you name it, finding it's even better than I've ever experienced using an iPhone. I'm sold. *** My wife is not as comfortable with using a stylus and so uses it on and off. She's not pushing to use it as much as I am, can do it, but it's not as important to her. Overall this Stylus (5 Pcs), 2-in-1 Stylus Pen set is a great find.

** Extra tips for both ends mean you've got both multiple stylus pens and back up tips to keep the set lasting

text:
I've used two Toshiba external drives for many years now, one for my laptop and one for my PS4, and when the laptop seemed to be having more and more trouble recognizing its external drive, even after cleaning the plug contacts, I figured it was time for a new drive.

This new drive does not disappoint. In fact, it makes such short work of backing up files that it became clear to me that the previous drive must have been dying for some time...

I am amused too that the LED indicator light on this new drive doesn't flash like a coquette blinking her eyes the way the previous drives did. Instead, this drive blinks the LED very slowly and deliberately while it's working, as if to say, "I've got this; nothing to worry about!"

At first I had a problem getting the drive to back up my laptop. The computer recognized the drive and the LED lit up solid, but my repeated command "Back up now" kept failing.

I tried cleaning the plug contacts, rebooting the laptop, and even reformatting the drive, but still no successful backup. Then I discovered that Windows 10 makes you click on a "Stop using this drive" button (your previous drive) before you tell it to "Add a new drive."

Once I had gone through that little ritual, all was well. And indeed, I was amazed how fast the new drive backed up all my files, accomplishing in less than an hour what the old drive had taken a number of hours to do.

All in all, this drive does its job, and I trust I will get years of use out of it, as I did the Toshiba's before...

text:
I want to clarify, this HD does exactly what it's meant to, exceptionally. It is plug n play, it requires no formatting or complicated software, its transfer rates are great & it has a rugged protective design that means it'll last a long time.

BUT I want to let folks know, specifically, if they're utilizing USB wireless devices such as a keyboard, mouse, etc; You must plug this in as far away from the recievers for those devices as possible. In fact, if you have a laptop, I recommend using a far longer cord & putting the HD as far away as the Hard Drive allows.

To be clear, I'm not sure this is a real manufacturing or producer error, this just seems like signal interference inherent to the power output of the hard drive. It WILL cause your mouse, keyboard, etc to lag. It can cause wireless connections to drop. If you have a little plug in USB reciever for any device you use on your computer, move it to the opposite side from the HD. In fact, try to keep the HD out of the line of signal entirely AND as far away from it as possible.

If you plug a WD Elements Portable External Hard Drive & experience:
- Lag of keyboard input
- Lag of wireless mouse input
- Intermittent or disruptive wireless disconnections
- Signal or Detection dropout of a microphone or webcam using a wireless reciever

It is because of the WD Elements Portable Hard Drive. It is not an error, it's not malfunctioning, it is just disrupting the signal. Get a long USB transfer cord, or turn your laptop, or MOVE your wireless recievers so the HD is not between them & the device. I swear, it's working fine, it's super easy to work around, you do not need to refund/return, etc.

The product is great, I'm just writing this to thank the seller & also to make sure anyone googling this has a clear, reliable, understandable result in search as to what to do. Your computer isn't dying, nothing's wrong, it's just way too much in the airways.

I usually dont write reviews, but I felt compelled to do this...

Seagate's manual doesn't include Mac setup instructions, which is probably why some people think this hard drive isn't compatible, but it absolutely is.

After doing extensive research, I found that you don't need to download anything. The only thing required is a quick setup on your Mac:

1. Plug the Seagate external hard drive into your Mac
2. Open Disk Utility
3. Select the external hard drive from the list
4. Click Erase (top right)
5. Rename it to whatever you want
6. For the format, make sure you choose EXFAT (this is very important)!!!!

After that, it works perfectly.

For the other key points:

- Functionality / Computer recognition: Works perfectly once formatted correctly and is recognized without issues
- Portable / Compact size: Small, lightweight, and easy to carry around
- Scalability: Great for general storage needs like files, backups, and everyday use
- Power source: If you have a newer Mac with USB-C ports, the included cable uses USB-A, so you'll need a simple adapter or a compatible USB-C cable

So if you're seeing reviews saying it's not compatible, that's incorrect. It just needs to be formatted properly first.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
UPDATE on November 3

My problems with this keyboard have been resolved. The replacement is working perfectly.

Amazon replaced it quickly when I complained about the problem and the new keyboard works just as well as the one I owned before I dumped a beer on it.

The vendor was also monitoring my situation and quickly offered to replace the defective unit. But Amazon had already taken care of the problem.

When I read reviews from people who diss a product because they happened tp get one with a manufacturing defect I get annoyed. Every manufactured product has a small chance of failing. What is important is customer service and how quickly the problem can be resolved. In this case both Amazon and the vendor were on top of the situation as soon as they heard about it.

Companies that sell $15 keyboards can not afford many warranty claims. They have to design their products so that the failure rate is very low or they wont make any money. That is why I have had such good experience , with inexpensive electronic devices. They cant afford to build them to mil spec standards, like a satellite that is going to be put in orbit, so there will be occasional failures. In my experience they are few and far between and that's where customer service comes into play. If, in the very unlikely chance, that I get a defective unit, prompt attention to the problem can resolve it painlessly.

I had this exact same model for many months before I accidentally destroyed it by pouring a beer on it. When I needed a new keyboard I tried another model what was rechargeable. That seemed like a good idea but the charges did not last nearly as long at the AAA batteries on this keyboard and I had to be somewhere with a USB port when it failed or I was out of business. With this keyboard I just need to keep a couple of AAA batteries with my traveling stuff and I can be back in business in seconds.

This is a good keyboard. Its light, easy to pair with devices, the keys have a nice feel (but that is a very personal thing) and the battery life is good. I use it with my phone and tablet.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Updating the review to reflect a more accurate review, originally I posted that it was completely useless under MacOS because it would go to sleep and never wake up. While the keyboard I received did this, Omoton has worked with me and replaced the keyboard and the new one does not have this defect. Big thumbs up to Omoton who has tried hard to make me happy.

MacOS (take two) - While the keyboard works almost flawlessly under MacOS, the wakeup speed is fast and does doe what it is supposed to do; the lack of a n Escape key is a problem. I have tried hard to find a way to map the HOME button to an Escape key but was not able to do so, it just isn't seen as any key under MacOS. Generally this is not a problem and the keyboard would be find as it is; as long as whatever applications you are using do not need the ESC key (I'm look at you VIM coders, this is not the keyboard for you then).

Windows - Didn't spend a lot of time with it under windows, it is not recommended in general for windows; thus I didn't try too hard to get it to work.

iOS (Pad & Phone) - This is where the keyboard shined, worked flawlessly. Work up rapidly, synced to the device without a problem and did great. If this is what you want to use the keyboard for, then this keyboard will be great. It's not expensive, it is well designed. Did everything that I needed it to do under iOS.

AppleTV Gen 4 - Synced and just worked. Much like under iOS, it worked perfectly.

If there was something that I would change, I would love to see the home button have a switch on the back side (just like the power switch) that allows it to be Escape instead of Home. That way the keyboard would work without a problem for either MacOS or iOS.
