title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
UPDATE on November 3

My problems with this keyboard have been resolved. The replacement is working perfectly.

Amazon replaced it quickly when I complained about the problem and the new keyboard works just as well as the one I owned before I dumped a beer on it.

The vendor was also monitoring my situation and quickly offered to replace the defective unit. But Amazon had already taken care of the problem.

When I read reviews from people who diss a product because they happened tp get one with a manufacturing defect I get annoyed. Every manufactured product has a small chance of failing. What is important is customer service and how quickly the problem can be resolved. In this case both Amazon and the vendor were on top of the situation as soon as they heard about it.

Companies that sell $15 keyboards can not afford many warranty claims. They have to design their products so that the failure rate is very low or they wont make any money. That is why I have had such good experience , with inexpensive electronic devices. They cant afford to build them to mil spec standards, like a satellite that is going to be put in orbit, so there will be occasional failures. In my experience they are few and far between and that's where customer service comes into play. If, in the very unlikely chance, that I get a defective unit, prompt attention to the problem can resolve it painlessly.

I had this exact same model for many months before I accidentally destroyed it by pouring a beer on it. When I needed a new keyboard I tried another model what was rechargeable. That seemed like a good idea but the charges did not last nearly as long at the AAA batteries on this keyboard and I had to be somewhere with a USB port when it failed or I was out of business. With this keyboard I just need to keep a couple of AAA batteries with my traveling stuff and I can be back in business in seconds.

This is a good keyboard. Its light, easy to pair with devices, the keys have a nice feel (but that is a very personal thing) and the battery life is good. I use it with my phone and tablet.

************************************************
What follows is my initial review

I have had this keyboard for a couple of months and am having problems with the repeating characters for several rows of text. If I turn it off and turn it back on the problem goes away for a while.

Im going to contact the vendor and see if they can do anything about the problem or if there is something I am doing wrong.

I owned one of these previously and it was fine until I dumped a beer on it.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Updating the review to reflect a more accurate review, originally I posted that it was completely useless under MacOS because it would go to sleep and never wake up. While the keyboard I received did this, Omoton has worked with me and replaced the keyboard and the new one does not have this defect. Big thumbs up to Omoton who has tried hard to make me happy.

MacOS (take two) - While the keyboard works almost flawlessly under MacOS, the wakeup speed is fast and does doe what it is supposed to do; the lack of a n Escape key is a problem. I have tried hard to find a way to map the HOME button to an Escape key but was not able to do so, it just isn't seen as any key under MacOS. Generally this is not a problem and the keyboard would be find as it is; as long as whatever applications you are using do not need the ESC key (I'm look at you VIM coders, this is not the keyboard for you then).

Windows - Didn't spend a lot of time with it under windows, it is not recommended in general for windows; thus I didn't try too hard to get it to work.

iOS (Pad & Phone) - This is where the keyboard shined, worked flawlessly. Work up rapidly, synced to the device without a problem and did great. If this is what you want to use the keyboard for, then this keyboard will be great. It's not expensive, it is well designed. Did everything that I needed it to do under iOS.

AppleTV Gen 4 - Synced and just worked. Much like under iOS, it worked perfectly.

If there was something that I would change, I would love to see the home button have a switch on the back side (just like the power switch) that allows it to be Escape instead of Home. That way the keyboard would work without a problem for either MacOS or iOS.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars

Companies that sell $15 keyboards can not afford many warranty claims. They have to design their products so that the failure rate is very low or they wont make any money. That is why I have had such good experience , with inexpensive electronic devices. They cant afford to build them to mil spec standards, like a satellite that is going to be put in orbit, so there will be occasional failures. In my experience they are few and far between and that's where customer service comes into play. If, in the very unlikely chance, that I get a defective unit, prompt attention to the problem can resolve it painlessly.

I had this exact same model for many months before I accidentally destroyed it by pouring a beer on it. When I needed a new keyboard I tried another model what was rechargeable. This is a good keyboard. Its light, easy to pair with devices, the keys have a nice feel (but that is a very personal thing) and the battery life is good. I use it with my phone and tablet.

text:
I have been purchasing Zagg products for years and will continue to do so. The products they offer are very durable; so durable it’s a challenge to remove them if they need to be replaced.

I purchased this screen protector for my iPad 11” - M3 and it fits nicely. The picture instructions are easy to follow. Package includes: the screen protector, a plastic guide/cradle to hold the iPad still, a screen cleaning wipe, a cloth to dry it off (can also be reused/repurposed for eyeglasses), a sticky dust remover and 1 small alcohol wipe.

IMPORTANT NOTE: the plastic guide/cradle is marked “top” so you can position the tablet correctly. That’s important because there is a notch on the side of the protector that does not cover the camera when changing the camera view for video chat or selfie.

The screen protector does not interfere with the tablet fitting into a bluetooth keyboard such as a “Magic keyboard” or the Logitech keyboard.

Use a credit card or something similar to get any air bubbles out and push the bubbles to the edge. Any remaining bubbles should work themselves out over night. It’s ok to put a little pressure on it. You can also use the included cloth to put between the screen protector and the credit card.

The thickness is just right and it looks clear.

I’m happy with purchase and wouldn’t hesitate to purchase again.

text:
I did allot of poking around online as to which one of these screen protectors to get as I am of the thinking it’s better to have one on my wonderful iPad.

This Zagg model kept coming up with rave reviews. Even my Geek Squad tech who services my electronics said this is the one to get, unless you are an artist and use the pencil for art work, the consider one of those paper-like screen protectors. Anyways, Best Buy didn’t have them so I ordered it from Amazon, as they sell everything known to mankind.

I see why people like this model, though initially it looks like just about every other out there. The packaging is great and the glass just appears of high quality. It’s expensive, so I had to get someone with more experience to throw it on as you only get 1 in the box (even though it comes with DIY apparatus). I really didn’t want to muck it up.

After a few months of having it now, it is like the surface came this way from Apple. Fit and finish is perfect. I used my iPad with the stock surface for a little while so I can attest there is a small difference in how it feels.

The cons are thus; it’s quite reflective and is slippery. So light bounces off this surface more readily than the Apple glass underneath. I don’t find it a dealbreaker but I do wish it wasn’t so. More significant is the glass is noticeably more slippery. Whether finger or Apple Pencil (gen2) it’s like a sheet of ice. I suppose the material used along with all the fancy chemical coatings gives you this. I also wish it wasn’t as slippery. Fun fact; don’t clean it as often and leave your fingerprints on it (worth a try) as it makes it less slippery. When this screen is cleaned with my Whoosh cleaner I could probably (but have not done so) slide it across a highway and it would keep up with speeding cars. Bad joke, but you get the idea.

However, it feels so smooth using the screen. Can’t attest to how much stronger it makes the screen in a drop but I’ll assume it helps with that too.

Anyways, good to know this Zagg screen will take all my abuse and not the actual iPad screen. So far not a single scratch has appeared and I use it allot with fingers and Apple Pencil.

Would a cheaper screen be equal? Can’t say. Maybe few can, that’s why a plathora of accolades are advertised with these products whether 10 bucks or a hundred. For me, I would purchase again if someone stole the screen (and left my iPad).

Recommended.

The RAYMCRAFT for iPad Pro 13-inch Case with Keyboard (M4, 2024) is a well-built, sturdy case. It’s heavier (928 g / 2.07 lb) and thicker than the equivalent Apple case (663 g / 1.74 lb), but not a dealbreaker, though.

The case’s surface feels nice and is easy to grip while carrying. The top of the case features a great pencil holder strap that securely holds the pencil in place. This strap stays out of the way by magnetically connecting to the back of the case while you use the pencil. It’s one of the best pencil holders I’ve seen. I have the pencil in a case and the strap has enough length to wrap around it also.

The iPad attaches firmly to the case and can be angled as desired.

The keyboard has all the standard keys in the same layout as the Apple iPad case, except for one. They replaced the profile key with a Bluetooth pairing key. The keys work well and provide a decent typing feedback. The keyboard also has lighting brightness and colour controls, which are a nice touch. There’s an ON/OFF button so you can save battery or turn it off if you just want it to function as a stand.

The trackpad works well, but it’s slightly smaller than the Apple iPad trackpad. The biggest issue I have is its sensitivity to palm touches while typing. If your palm or thumb moves up and down while typing and touches the trackpad, the cursor position changes and potentially activates other apps or menus, which is incredibly frustrating. The Apple keyboard/case also has this problem, but not as much as the RAYMCRAFT. My wife, who’s a much better typist than I am, couldn’t use the RAYMCRAFT keyboard because of the unpredictable behaviour of the trackpad’s touch sensitivity.

Overall, the RAYMCRAFT iPad Pro case and keyboard are a good deal for the price, especially if you don’t mind a bit more weight and thickness compared to the Apple one. Depending how you type, you may get frustrated with the touchy trackpad though.

text:
I also own the Apple Magic Keyboard but prefer the Zagg keyboard for so many different reasons.

The main thing I really didn’t like about the Apple keyboard is it didn’t provide wrap-around protection to my iPad. Unfortunately I dropped the Apple Keyboard (in the closed position with my iPad inside) a couple of times, and each time the iPad fell out or got damaged around its edges. On the other hand, this Zagg keyboard is PERFECT! It provides great wrap-around protection with a shock-absorbing rubber bumper. I also love that the keyboard and bumper are two separate pieces, allowing me to remove the iPad from the keyboard without having to remove it from the bumper.

Other great things about the Zagg:
• Keyboard feels good (9/10). For comparison, I would rate the Magic Keyboard as a 10/10.
• Has hot keys that the Magic Keyboard doesn’t have.
• I personally like that it has a separate battery and doesn’t cause parasitic drain on the iPad’s battery (with the Apple keyboard, my iPad seemed to run out of juice too quickly.)
• Unlike the Apple keyboard, the Zagg has a built-in holder for the Apple pen! And when you close up the keyboard, it securely holds the pen in place so you don’t lose it. The holder is also positioned along the side of the iPad, allowing the pen to continue charging. (With the Apple keyboard, I frequently didn’t bring the pen with me for fear of losing it).
• It can be paired with two different Bluetooth devices and quickly switched between the devices just by pressing an assigned hot key button. This is a FANTASTIC feature that more Bluetooth devices should incorporate (in fact, I would prefer if it had THREE hot keys to pair it with three different devices). I use the keyboard to switch between my iPad and iPhone.
• The Apple keyboard has an advantage in terms of the joint connecting the keyboard to the iPad is really strong and stays in whatever position you place it. That’s not true of the Zagg, which has two different slots that the bottom of the iPad must be placed into in order to keep it open. But (and again, this is a GREAT design feature), the two slots have a very strong magnet so when you place the iPad into it, it essentially locks into place.

I’ve never owned a Zagg product before but am really impressed by the quality and excellent design features of this keyboard.

text:
I also own the Apple Magic Keyboard but prefer the Zagg keyboard for so many different reasons.

The main thing I really didn’t like about the Apple keyboard is it didn’t provide wrap-around protection to my iPad. Unfortunately I dropped the Apple Keyboard (in the closed position with my iPad inside) a couple of times, and each time the iPad fell out or got damaged around its edges. On the other hand, this Zagg keyboard is PERFECT! It provides great wrap-around protection with a shock-absorbing rubber bumper. I also love that the keyboard and bumper are two separate pieces, allowing me to remove the iPad from the keyboard without having to remove it from the bumper.

Other great things about the Zagg:
• Keyboard feels good (9/10). For comparison, I would rate the Magic Keyboard as a 10/10.
• Has hot keys that the Magic Keyboard doesn’t have.
• I personally like that it has a separate battery and doesn’t cause parasitic drain on the iPad’s battery (with the Apple keyboard, my iPad seemed to run out of juice too quickly.)
• Unlike the Apple keyboard, the Zagg has a built-in holder for the Apple pen! And when you close up the keyboard, it securely holds the pen in place so you don’t lose it. The holder is also positioned along the side of the iPad, allowing the pen to continue charging. (With the Apple keyboard, I frequently didn’t bring the pen with me for fear of losing it).
• It can be paired with two different Bluetooth devices and quickly switched between the devices just by pressing an assigned hot key button. This is a FANTASTIC feature that more Bluetooth devices should incorporate (in fact, I would prefer if it had THREE hot keys to pair it with three different devices). I use the keyboard to switch between my iPad and iPhone.
• The Apple keyboard has an advantage in terms of the joint connecting the keyboard to the iPad is really strong and stays in whatever position you place it. That’s not true of the Zagg, which has two different slots that the bottom of the iPad must be placed into in order to keep it open. But (and again, this is a GREAT design feature), the two slots have a very strong magnet so when you place the iPad into it, it essentially locks into place.

I’ve never owned a Zagg product before but am really impressed by the quality and excellent design features of this keyboard.

Review is for the ZAGG - Pro Keys Wireless Keyboard with Trackpad and Detachable Case - Compatible with The Apple iPad 10.9" / 11" Pro. Bought for $149.99 in June 2021.

Your reviewer, being notoriously cheap, was looking for a lower-cost keyboard/trackpad combo for the iPad Pro and stumbled across the Zagg. Cheaper than the Logitech Combo Touch ($200) and Apple Magic Keyboard ($300), but how were the quality and features? Here's a rundown.

Positives
* Has Escape key.
* Has top row function keys.
* Has iPad cover protector that detaches from keyboard/trackpad.

Negatives
* Requires battery recharging (Logitech and Apple keyboards do not).
* Requires Bluetooth connection which randomly lags.
* Does not recognize 3-finger gestures.
* Keyboard is "chiclet" style keys which makes it feel cheap.

At $150, the Zagg is still not a cheap accessory. Love the top row function keys, and detachable screen protector for when you want to just use the iPad without the keyboard. The "chiclet" style keyboard feels cheap and "clicky". Deal killer for me, however, is that the Zagg does not support 3-finger gestures on its trackpad. So, no 3-finger app task manager although there is a dedicated keyboard function key for that.

I would not recommend this product. Too expensively priced not to support 3-finger trackpad gestures. Would recommend the Logitech Combo Touch or Apple Magic Keyboard (Renewed) instead.

text:
I also own the Apple Magic Keyboard but prefer the Zagg keyboard for so many different reasons.

The main thing I really didn’t like about the Apple keyboard is it didn’t provide wrap-around protection to my iPad. Unfortunately I dropped the Apple Keyboard (in the closed position with my iPad inside) a couple of times, and each time the iPad fell out or got damaged around its edges. On the other hand, this Zagg keyboard is PERFECT! It provides great wrap-around protection with a shock-absorbing rubber bumper. I also love that the keyboard and bumper are two separate pieces, allowing me to remove the iPad from the keyboard without having to remove it from the bumper.

Other great things about the Zagg:
• Keyboard feels good (9/10). For comparison, I would rate the Magic Keyboard as a 10/10.
• Has hot keys that the Magic Keyboard doesn’t have.
• I personally like that it has a separate battery and doesn’t cause parasitic drain on the iPad’s battery (with the Apple keyboard, my iPad seemed to run out of juice too quickly.)
• Unlike the Apple keyboard, the Zagg has a built-in holder for the Apple pen! And when you close up the keyboard, it securely holds the pen in place so you don’t lose it. The holder is also positioned along the side of the iPad, allowing the pen to continue charging. (With the Apple keyboard, I frequently didn’t bring the pen with me for fear of losing it).
• It can be paired with two different Bluetooth devices and quickly switched between the devices just by pressing an assigned hot key button. This is a FANTASTIC feature that more Bluetooth devices should incorporate (in fact, I would prefer if it had THREE hot keys to pair it with three different devices). I use the keyboard to switch between my iPad and iPhone.
• The Apple keyboard has an advantage in terms of the joint connecting the keyboard to the iPad is really strong and stays in whatever position you place it. That’s not true of the Zagg, which has two different slots that the bottom of the iPad must be placed into in order to keep it open. But (and again, this is a GREAT design feature), the two slots have a very strong magnet so when you place the iPad into it, it essentially locks into place.

I’ve never owned a Zagg product before but am really impressed by the quality and excellent design features of this keyboard.

text:
I did a bit of research into Apple knockoffs because the $450 CAD Apple was charging was asinine. I liked the concept, but I'm not paying that money especially if the apple case isn't durable, stainproof, or fully protective including the sides. I also

I settled on this one because I liked that it had function keys, reviews seemed solid, and it was the most affordable knock off I could find on Amazon while simultaneously feeling like it was the one I could best trust. I've only had this for like two days now, but thought I'd write in my first impressions.

Setting it up was confusing and I began to wonder if I had a defective product. After half an hour of failing to connect, I remembered that I had seen a review somewhere stating that you needed to press a couple on the keyboard to start setting up the bluetooth (FN + B for at least 3 seconds). Once I finally clued in to this, connection was quick and easy.

I'm actually finding the typing experience quite nice on this, and I love that is backlit. The function keys have also been super convenient and I am so happy I have them. I find them easy enough to access (and even if they were a bit of an awkward reach, I'd rather have them than not). The keyboard width is about the same as my 16" 2021 macbook pro. The keys feel quite nice to me, although I'm finding I'm making more typos than usual on it. I don't notice a delay when typing.

I didn't know how I would feel about the flap, because I find it looks aesthetically awkward when laid down on the table during use... but it is easy to fold up and place underneath during use, and I'm overall happy it is there because it helps protect the Apple Pencil and it helps everything feel slightly more secure and quality when closed.

The biggest flaw is the trackpad. The movements and gestures are quite now... but if you try to press down to click, if feels cheap and "crunchy". There's an area of it that feels "double crunchy" (hard to explain), which makes me feel like it isn't durable or might eventually fall apart or fail. When first receiving the product, there is a sticker beside the trackpad that guides the user to change the settings to "tap to click" for a better experience. The tab to click is definitely a better experience than the crunchy presses, and it seems pretty good at knowing when I'm navigating vs clicking (I've had trackpads that were ultra sensitive and kept clicking when they weren't supposed to in the past). However, I've found that sometimes you will still need to press down (like when highlighting text).

The ipad stays solidly in place inside of the case, though I which they took the opportunity to create more protection for the sides of the ipad.

It will add quite a bit of weight. This is something I was well aware of before purchasing. This isn't a big deal to me. The reality as that it needs to be heavy to be able to support the ipad's weight. It isn't as adjustable as a laptop, but is more adjustable than I would have expected.

I purchased this is black. It does leave greasy-looking finger marks... but otherwise feels nice and solid, but not necessarily like it'll be durable with heavy travel over years.

So far, I'm super happy with it, especially as I got it a during the Prime October sale slightly cheaper. If my opinion changes with time, I'll update.

This is a good alternative to the Apple Pencil Pro, especially at half the price, but buyers should consider 3 apects:
1) this does not magnetically attach to your iPad, so you will need to find a way to carry it so you don't lose it.
2) because it doesn't use the magnetic attachment for the Apple Pencil, it also doesn't charge when stored (Apple does wireless charging when attached). You will need to periodically charge the Crayon by plugging it in to a cable.
3) The Crayon has an on/off switch (and 3 small green led dots to indicate charge). The Apple Pencil solution doesn't. The iPad tells you charge level when you attached the Pencil to the iPad.

So it works differently. It is very responsive and tracks just like the Pencil does, but you have to manage it yourself with a cable. Not a deal breaker but I took off the 1 star because it doesn't integrate into the iPad as well as the Pencil. But for half the cost, it might be a perfect compromise.

Alles in allem bin ich echt zufrieden, das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis ist super.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have several keyboard cases across different iPads (including the official Apple Magic Keyboard), so I feel like I have a pretty good frame of reference here. Most of them work fine… but they all come with little trade-offs.

This one? Easily my favorite so far.

Just like the Apple OEM version, it’s completely self-supporting and the viewing angle is adjustable, but once you set it where you want it, it actually stays there. No wobbling, no slowly collapsing, no fighting with a floppy hinge. It’s honestly perfect for using on the couch or in bed, where other cases tend to feel unstable unless you’re sitting at a desk.

Pairing was ridiculously easy — Bluetooth connected in seconds. The fit is spot-on, and the whole thing feels surprisingly premium, like something Apple would actually sell (just without the Apple price tag attached).

The keys feel great and have the same familiar layout as the Magic Keyboard, and the trackpad is smooth, responsive, and doesn’t lag or glitch. The backlighting is also a really nice touch — bright enough to see clearly, but not so intense that it feels like a spotlight in your face at night.

It does need to be charged separately (and it won’t charge the Apple Pencil), but it comes with a USB-C cord, and honestly, the battery life is so good that you won’t be reaching for it often.

I have several keyboard cases across different iPads (including the official Apple Magic Keyboard), so I feel like I have a pretty good frame of reference here. Most of them work fine… but they all come with little trade-offs.

This one? Easily my favorite so far.

Just like the Apple OEM version, it’s completely self-supporting and the viewing angle is adjustable, but once you set it where you want it, it actually stays there. No wobbling, no slowly collapsing, no fighting with a floppy hinge. It’s honestly perfect for using on the couch or in bed, where other cases tend to feel unstable unless you’re sitting at a desk.

Pairing was ridiculously easy — Bluetooth connected in seconds. The fit is spot-on, and the whole thing feels surprisingly premium, like something Apple would actually sell (just without the Apple price tag attached).

The keys feel great and have the same familiar layout as the Magic Keyboard, and the trackpad is smooth, responsive, and doesn’t lag or glitch. The backlighting is also a really nice touch — bright enough to see clearly, but not so intense that it feels like a spotlight in your face at night.

It does need to be charged separately (and it won’t charge the Apple Pencil), but it comes with a USB-C cord, and honestly, the battery life is so good that you won’t be reaching for it often.

Overall, this is an excellent keyboard case and a fantastic value compared to the Apple Magic Keyboard. If you want that same experience without spending Apple-level money, this is absolutely worth it.

This keyboard case is a great match for my iPad Air 13 M2 (2024 model). The magnetic top cover holds the tablet securely in place, and pairing the keyboard was effortless. The overall design is clean and elegant, with excellent craftsmanship that gives the whole setup a premium feel. The keys have satisfying springiness and don't feel mushy at all, while the trackpad is smooth and responsive that allows you to skip the touchscreen almost completely. The latter is similar to one found on a laptop, where you can press the bottom section took in lieu of a mouse click.

Smart Features & Gestures:
I love how practical the function buttons are—they let me adjust screen brightness, control volume, and manage audio/video playback with ease. The trackpad also supports gesture controls with one, two, or three fingers as shortcuts for different functions, which adds a laptop-like convenience to everyday use. The manual includes a guide to these gestures, though I did notice a few typos that made things a little confusing at first.

Well-Thought-Out Flap Design:
The magnetic flap is cleverly designed. It works on both sides: folded forward when the case is closed and folded backward when open. I also appreciate the integrated slits to hold my Apple Pencil Pro, although I wish the flap material were a bit sturdier.

Minor Quirks
- I got the blue version, and while the color is quite appealing, the characters' low contrast makes the keyboard a little hard to read unless the backlight is on—and even then, certain colours like purple are not super crisp.
- The backlight isn’t fully uniform; a few keys (like the left Option and right CMD) are noticeably dimmer.
- This case adds a quite a bit of weight, so it’s best carried in a backpack if you’re on the go.
- Frequent removal of the Pencil might wear the flap out over time due to its tight fit and thinner material.

Final Thoughts
It’s a solid case that delivers on style and functionality at a fair $130 price point. Definitely worth considering if you're turning your iPad into your daily workhorse.

text:
This case is great for someone who wants cheap and durable protection for their iPad. My use case for my iPad is basic, and it will only leave the house for vacations and plane trips for the most part. The worse drop it may ever face is falling from waist height, so those that use their tablets in more rugged/outdoor environments may want to do more research.

Pros:
The case covers the entire tablet with the exception of the speaker holes, lock button, and camera. The camera hole is raised so the camera bump is protected from a fall. The lock button is recessed in the case for protection, but still allows you to utilize it for fingerprint unlocking. The charger port has a plastic flap to cover it when not in use. The built in screen protector is a nice addition that I prefer in tablet cases. It also has a spot above the front camera where you can attach a stylus (apple pencil or whatever), but it is convenient and does not add bulk to the case for those that don't use a stylus.

Cons:
The fitment of the rubber outer case to the inner hard plastic of the case is not super tight. If you push down on top/bottom of the rubber case, it lifts towards the front of the case and makes the case seem less premium. The little flap that covers the charger port also sticks out from the rest of the case after stretching the rubber from using the port to charge. This isn't a super big deal considering the case is only $20, but something to note.

The screen protector is not the best. It's flexible plastic, which is what I was expecting. However, the screen protector has visible dots in the plastic that make the screen of the iPad look worse. The difference between the screen with and without the screen protector is small, but noticeable. I have personally gotten use to this and basically don't notice it anymore, but to someone who is a lot more detail focused, it may be something to consider.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have lots of flash drives, and several that have both USB-A and USB-C connection because I move between several computing devices including Mac, Windows, Android, iOS, and Linux based systems. This drive worked well with all devices.

Beyond feeling like a solid and durable device, this has a distinct and satisfying click moving between the “A” “C” and “open” positions. The Lexar name has been very good to me with storage products in the last few years, and this seems to be no exception. The drive weighs in at 26.8g according to my digital coffee scale, and fits both C and A type USB ports precisely resulting in a perfect connection. The drive registered at 124,585,377,792 bytes of storage capacity. The drive arrived formatted with a FAT32 file system.

I didn’t benchmark this as such, what I did was use it in parallel with a major “Brand” drive I use daily, and this was 10x faster. Both are rated for the same speed, and I’ve wondered why my former daily driver seemed too slow and blamed it on the computers I generally use it with -- until I tried this drive. Suddenly I felt my worries were justified.

I moved several software packages in the 1-3GB range in a fraction of the time I normally do.

Given the pressures on current storage prices, I consider this a remarkable value as it was less expensive than the device I’m replacing and is both faster and feels less ‘plasticky.’

My only “note” is I wish it had a cap for both ends’ connectors, but that just means I don’t want it in my lint filled pocket and that is for the best in any case.

The packaging is attractive, which is not really a concern of mine, but it’s still nice to see.

The sturdy construction, the exceptional speed, and value proposition make this a five star product.

5/5, I'll get more to have on hand.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on March 20, 2026

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been running my home automation system (Home Assistant) from an SD card on a Raspberry Pi, which really worked surprisingly well, but it isn't a good idea long term because of the potential that the SD card will eventually fail from all of the system's reads and writes. I ordered this USB SSD drive to make my system more reliable and also for it to run much faster.

This drive has both a USB A and a USB C connector so it can connect to my laptop for initial setup and also to the older style connector on my Raspberry Pi. I formatted and installed the raspberry pi OS onto the drive using my laptop. The install was trouble free, and it was amazingly fast.

After that, I shut down my pi, removed the SD card, plugged in this solid state drive, and turned it back on. The system booted up as expected. It was a lot quicker, but that's to be expected on a new blank system. I restored a backup to it, which did run very quickly, and everything works as expected.

I'm really glad I ordered this, upgrading my home automation system has been on my to do list for a very long time. The new drive is fast, easy to use, and should be a lot more reliable going forward.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on March 21, 2026

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Had to reformat from FAT32 to exFAT out of the box to get the speed test to complete, but once done, it delivers close to advertised speeds. Write came in at 534.6 MB/s and read at 339.8 MB/s. The dual connector design (USB-A and USB-C) is a big plus — covers just about every device you'd need. Overall a solid little drive for the price.

As for the speed test breakdown, your drive handles most common video formats well:
Blackmagic RAW is limited — works for 1080p and some 2K/4K formats, but struggles at higher resolutions like 4320p60, 8K 60, and 12K.
ProRes 422 HQ fares similarly, with read generally outpacing write. It fails at 4320p60, 8K DCI, and 12K formats.
H.265 is the clear winner — it passes read and write for everything up through 8K DCI 60, which makes sense given how compressed the format is.
Bottom line: great drive for everyday use and compressed video workflows, but not suited for high-frame-rate RAW or ProRes work at 8K and above.

High Capacity and Dual Functionality, Minor Durability Concern

"The Lexar 512GB JumpDrive Dual Drive D400 is an impressive flash drive that offers both versatility and convenience. I love the dual functionality of Type-C and Type-A, which makes it incredibly easy to transfer files between different devices, from laptops to phones, without needing an adapter. The 512GB capacity is fantastic, offering ample storage for large files, photos, and videos, and the USB 3.2 speeds mean that transfers are quick and efficient.

The design is sleek and compact, making it easy to carry around in a pocket or bag. I also appreciate that it works seamlessly across different platforms, whether I’m using it on a Mac or a Windows PC, and even with my Android phone. It's especially useful for anyone who needs to frequently move files between older and newer devices.

The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is that the casing feels a bit flimsy compared to other drives I’ve used. I’m a little concerned about long-term durability, especially with frequent plugging in and out. It would have been great if it had a sturdier build or some sort of cap to protect the connectors.

Overall, though, this is a solid, high-capacity drive that offers fast performance and excellent compatibility with multiple devices. It's a great choice for anyone who needs both USB-C and USB-A in one convenient package."

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I should start off by saying this is my third Torras case. My first was an older version of this case that I had purchased when we got my son an iPad Air M1 and it exceeded my expectations. I was looking for something that had a built-in stand that was sturdy and I didn't want something that would add bulk to a premium item like an iPad. Although it was for my son, I wasn't too worried about impact resistance because we've taught him to be careful with his stuff. We did try one of those cases made for kids and they were huge and honestly, the stands were junk. That's what led me to search for something better. I had never heard of Torras before, but I noticed they had a different design than all the others on Amazon. The stand is super sturdy and it stays in the position you put it. We liked that case so much that we purchased an updated version of the Torras case for my daughter when we got her an iPad Air M4. The design was very similar, but they had redesigned how the Apple Pencil was held on which made the case even less bulky. Otherwise, it was the same high quality case that we were used to.

We decided to upgrade my son to an iPad Air M4 as well and we noticed that Torras released a new version of the case again. It looked very similar to the design of my daughter's case with some minor changes. We've been using it for a week and all I can say it that it's an upgrade in every way. Torras has changed the material that the sides of the case are made of. Now it's more like a bumper case on the edges which I assume adds a little bit of impact resistance as well as helping it grip on whatever surface you are placing it on. Also, this same material has been added to the fold out stand. This is greatly appreciated because now I don't have to worry about the metal stand scratching a wood table. In addition, the volume buttons are slightly different as well. I would say they feel more tactile and are easier to find. One last thing I noticed is that the back now has feet made out of the same grippy material. This helps give the iPad some stability when laying flat on a table. We were a little worried about the redesign of the Apple Pencil holder, but so far it's been great. The pencil is held deep enough where it hasn't been an issue with it coming loose.

I've included some pictures showing the new case alongside the previous versions. I know some people thing we are a little extra for getting our kids iPads, but I like my kids to have the best, so why not have the best case as well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I absolutely love this keyboard! I purchased it back in February 2022. It’s now May 2025 and the keyboard is still working well and holds a charge just fine even after 3+ years of use. Pairing the keyboard to a device is easy and I love how you can connect to 3 different devices with the keyboard. I generally use it with my desktop computer but over the years I have used it was my laptop and mobile devices as well. I have the light pink keyboard and the color pairs really well with the rechargeable pink mouse that is also made by Macally.

The keyboard is compact but it’s easy to type on. My only complaint about the keys is the UP and DOWN arrow keys—they’re the smallest on the board. Together they are the size of one of the round keys. You get used to it eventually, but it is easy to hit the wrong arrow button. The keys have a great feel to them and little bit of a sound but it’s fairly quiet.

Honestly, it’s a great little keyboard. It’s got a bit of weight to it which is nice when you’re using it with a tablet. It seems to be solidly constructed.

My only complaint is that I can never tell how much of a charge the battery has left. I wish there was a battery gage on the keyboard or that the battery level showed up on my computer or tablet, but it doesn’t. If it only had that, it would be perfect. It’s not a major issue, since the keyboard can be used when it’s being charged.

All in all though, I love it. The price is fair as well. I’ve purchased Apple keyboards before and those are far more expensive. This one was far cheaper and it seems to have great longevity. I’ve had other bluetooth keyboards but this one has been the best and has lasted the longest. I actually just purchased a second one to use with my tablet. Hopefully that one will be as good as this one.

One other thing is that this keyboard is FCC and EC certified. It’s listed on the label on the underside of the keyboard.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Overall this keyboard is exactly as described and works as intended. I debated on whether to give it a 4 or 5 star review because I was aware of the one issue I would have with it, but felt that it was still the best option for what I needed. The good:
- Way easier to type on than I anticipated when looking at the photos. This really is a full feeling keyboard with correct key size and spacing. Even the round keys didn’t bother me as I expected.
- I’m specifically using this for an iPad without a case. I’m a musician and my iPad doubles as my music stand and needs to fit into a stand holder which prevents me from having a case on it, otherwise I would just have a keyboard case for this iPad. However, since I don’t want to keep putting it in and taking it out of a case every time I use it for other reasons, this keyboard was the perfect solution. Unfortunately not having a case on it also has a slightly negative effect on the fit.

The (somewhat) Bad - The only issue I have, which I was fully aware of from the product listing photos, is that the iPad lays back at a fairly extreme angle (most pronounced in portrait orientation). I put a slim case on my iPad and it fit great (still had plenty of angle without risk of falling out, yet provided a better overall view). The reason I gave this 4 stars is that a minor design change would fix this. If there was a sliding lever on the back of the keyboard that pushed a shim along the inside of the holder gap, then I could adjust the angle of the iPad to my preference with or without a case on it.

Overall the best and most sturdy option for the money. Don’t hesitate to buy this. You just may want to find a way to shim it if you don’t have a case on your device.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: This is unequivocally the best iPad mini case and the reasons are simple. It is slim, protective, has amazing rear stands, and it comes with an Apple Pencil storage plug in case you don’t have an Apple Pencil to store. For the rear stands, they feel sturdy yet easy to adjust. The only thing that stops this case from being perfect is the fact that the stands don’t have grips on the edges which would stop the iPad from sliding if it’s standing up in a smooth slippery surface like some granite, etc. Still, I believe the stands are superior to other standing features of other cases from other brands. I was a huge fan and user of the Zulu case but then I realized, only after discovering this case, that I was unnecessarily smudging and getting my iPad’s screen dirty. Why? Because the six of the flap that, when closed, is the same side that is used as the bottom of the base to stand up the iPad. So, your iPad and the case can get very dirty and smudgy if the defaces you stand up your iPad on are not 100% clean which let’s be honest, they never are. Regarding the Apple Pencil ‘plug’, it’s extremely nice that they included it because not everyone has an Apple Pencil and this plug just makes the case “normal” instead of having an empty Apple Pencil slot on the side of the iPad case look like something is missing. Overall, this Torras case is so nice to hold and use. Another thing that’s holding it back from being the perfect case (besides no stand grips) would be the price. The price could definitely be lower. The build quality is still amazing but making it more affordable would be nice.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this for garage; I'm converting into a ManCave/Gym/Workshop and I wanted Apple Music to power my stereo system (Fosi amp + 2.1 speaker setup). My wife and my buddies, we all love TouchTunes at a bar, so I figured the closest I could get to that on a budget was to mount an iPad to the wall and connect it to my stereo.

This does that just about perfectly. It's extremely tough and secure once it's on the wall and it attached to the wall very easily.

Where is falls just short is in the lock, the fabrication, and charging cable access. It's also a little wonky to secure the inside frame plate with 4 screws as you're holding it up along with the iPad.

The lock itself is a little cheap; if you don't press down enough, it just kind grinds and doesn't want to move. There's also not a ton of clearance so I have to be careful not to scratch the paint off the wall when I turn the key. The lever on the lock also completely fell out at one point, as the little nut unscrewed. So, not a huge fan of the lock or key.

In regards to fabrication, the bent edge of the bottom of the unit I got doesn't seat perfectly and the won't close if I force it to, and if I do, the front is bowed. I have to kind of jimmy it on just enough and press hard, then lock it.

Lastly, when the front cover is on, you can't remove the charging cable. In my case, which may be rare, I'm using a lightning to usb-c data transfer cable to connect directly to my app, which doesn't charge the iPad. So I have to take the front plate off with the key, change to a charging cable, wait for it to charge, and then jimmy the front cover back on and lock it every time I need to charge the iPad. If I can ever find the proper Lightning to USB-C cable that can transfer lossless audio and charge the iPad at the same time (using a USB-C splitter), this won't be an issue.

So, I'm giving it a 4/5 stars. It's awesome when the iPad is charge and everything is locked in place, but it could be easier to put together and operate. I'd improve the lock, and maybe figure out a way to leave the iPad in the case while being able to remove it from a wall or stand for transport.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: After using the UGREEN Tablet Stand for a few weeks, I can confidently say that it is a well-rounded product, especially for those who use their devices for extended periods. Here’s my experience with it: One of the standout features of this stand is its sturdy build. Made from high-quality aluminum alloy, it holds my iPad Pro and even smaller devices like my phone without wobbling. The adjustable viewing angles (from 5° to 150°) make it super easy to find the most comfortable position, whether I’m working, watching movies, or video calling. I’ve been using it at my desk and even in the kitchen for recipes, and it doesn’t disappoint. I appreciate its compact, foldable design. It fits right into my backpack, making it an excellent option for travel or working from cafés. Despite its portability, it doesn’t sacrifice stability or durability, which is a major plus. The anti-slip silicone pads and rubber hooks keep my devices secure without leaving scratches. I’ve accidentally nudged it a few times, but the rubber feet held the stand firmly in place on various surfaces, ensuring that my tablet didn’t tip over. While the stand handles most of my devices well, I noticed that very small devices, like older smartphones, don’t sit as securely. Additionally, it would be nice if more color options were available, but this doesn’t affect its overall performance. Overall, the UGREEN Tablet Stand has proven to be reliable, flexible, and easy to use. It’s perfect for those who want a stable, adjustable stand for a variety of activities, from work to entertainment. The minor issues with smaller devices are not deal-breakers, but a broader color range could add a bit of flair. I highly recommend this product for anyone looking for an affordable and durable tablet stand.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I've been using the keyboard case for two weeks now. The case arrived quickly after ordering. Easy to install the iPad in the case and provides good protection to the iPad. Easy to pair the keyboard to the iPad bluetooth. The keyboard connects quickly at each start up. All the keys work and are lit well with a variety of keyboard color selections. Key functions are fairly intuitive, but will take some practice to remember the important ones. The track pad works flawlessly at this point (alot of comments about spotty performance of track pad). Good location for the apple pencil holder. The kickstand is stiff enough to allow for infinite viewing angles of the screen and holds the weight of the iPad well. The sliding camera cover is nice to have, but once a protective glass is put on the lens, the slide is harder to close, so it would have been nice to have just a little extra room for camera glass. The iPad fits in the case with the screen protector with no problem. The case on the short sides of the iPad where the speaker / microphone cut outs are located are a bit flimsy (rubbery), so it would have been nice to have some stiffer reinforcement in those locations. For the removable keyboard, I typically won't use it detached, but the snaps are stiff to unsnap and snap together and I can see this as a failure point in the future if this was a regular activity of keyboard removal. A magnetic system would have been great. Overall, a great case that provides good protection to an expensive iPad.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: This has been the perfect case for my Galaxy Tablet. It's listed here as a case for the S7, but the one I got was actually for the S8+ and, in any case, it fits perfectly and works like a charm. I rely heavily on the hinged plate on the back, which I fold out so it can support the tablet vertically. Then I can easily pull the magnetic latch on the keyboard toward me and it lays flat on the desk so I'm able to type very easily and conveniently on keys that give a little. I like that because I learned touch-typing back in the days of mechanical typewriters and I know it tend to thump each letter rather heavily. Using an actual keyboard gives me a better feel for the accuracy of my typing and doesn't feel like I'm drumming my fingers on a table. The BlueTooth connectivity does seem to fall asleep if not used for a while, but I've gotten used to that now; I've learned to just repeat the first letter of whatever I'm planning to write until the tablet seems to wake up and start showing letters on the screen. Then I backspace a bit and start typing whatever I had planned. There are, of course, times when there are no good surfaces to rest the table on and I need to hold the tablet while working. At those times, I can use the fold-out plate as a convenient grip by bending my wrist upward and resting it between my thumb and fingers. Then the tablet is (mostly) vertical on my wrist while the keyboard lays along my forearm. The snaps on the keyboard case hold onto their counterparts on the back of the tablet case and the parts seem to keep each other from falling off my arm while I'm typing (a bit more slowly) one-handed. I haven't used the stylus very often, but I do like that there's a very secure storage place for it at the bottom of the tablet case, as well as a slot for the stylus to stick to the back of the tablet so it can be detected and charged by the device. The only thing I don't really like is that the camera cover keeps falling out if I happen to leave the camera uncovered for more than a few minutes. I think I've just been lucky that I haven't lost the cover yet. Hopefully Nillkin can sell me a spare if that ever happens; I'd hate to have to buy a whole new set just to regain that thin piece of plastic.

It’s easy to clean and none of the plastic layers are peeling. Very sturdy. I’m going to give it five stars because it’s just that well made but I’ll be honest, the lack of backlighting is something that I’m struggling with. So I’ll probably still return it and try for a backlit model but I cannot overstate how well made the case is I guess :)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I wasn’t expecting a tablet case to change how I use my iPad this much, but this one really did. From the first day, it felt less like a typical folio and more like a compact workstation that happens to fold flat and disappear when I am on the go.

The folding system is the standout feature. It actually delivers on the multiple view angle idea instead of feeling like a gimmick. I can prop the iPad up high for eye-level reading at my desk, drop it into a lower angle for sketching, flip it for watching videos, or perch it in a more vertical position for note-taking in meetings. Once you get used to the origami-style folds, switching between setups is quick and almost intuitive. It really does feel like it adapts to how I am working instead of forcing me into one or two fixed angles.

Build and materials feel premium in a way that is immediately obvious. The MOVAS vegan leather has a soft, almost skin-like touch that makes it comfortable to hold for long stretches, and it still feels structured enough that the stand feels solid in every position. The magnets are strong, so the iPad locks into place with a reassuring snap and stays put when I tap, swipe, or draw. It is also impressively slim and light, which matters when you are carrying an iPad all day. It adds function without turning the device into a brick.

In day to day use, the ergonomic “floating” modes are quietly one of the best parts. Being able to raise the screen those extra couple of inches does make a difference for neck comfort during video streaming sessions. Combined with all the fine-grained angle options, it is easy to dial in a setup that feels good for hours instead of constantly hunching forward.

There are, however, a few drawbacks that keep this from feeling completely perfect. It is designed for direct magnetic attachment, so if you prefer running an additional case, that is not really an option here. The folding system, while versatile, has a learning curve. For the first few days I had to keep referencing the little diagram to remember how to get back to a particular configuration, and it is possible to end up in slightly unstable shapes if you are not paying attention. Price is also on the higher side for a case, even though the quality and flexibility help justify it. Finally, because it wraps like a folio and focuses on being slim and origami-friendly, it is more about desk and lap use than serious drop protection. If you are rough on your devices or want rugged corners, this may not be the only case you own.

Overall, though, this is easily one of the most thoughtfully designed iPad accessories I have used. The combination of multi-angle flexibility, elevated viewing modes, slim profile, and premium feel makes it an easy pick if your priority is turning your iPad into a more ergonomic tool.

Find shapes, find ways to use the other folds, and be less rigid in your usage. It's flexible and will work with you.

The second real gripe is that the attached folding cover magnets are still weaker than perfect and it can slide a little when folded over on top of the other part of the cover. Otherwise, it's an almost perfect folio that looks and feels great.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I wasn’t expecting a tablet case to change how I use my iPad this much, but this one really did. From the first day, it felt less like a typical folio and more like a compact workstation that happens to fold flat and disappear when I am on the go.

The folding system is the standout feature. It actually delivers on the multiple view angle idea instead of feeling like a gimmick. I can prop the iPad up high for eye-level reading at my desk, drop it into a lower angle for sketching, flip it for watching videos, or perch it in a more vertical position for note-taking in meetings. Once you get used to the origami-style folds, switching between setups is quick and almost intuitive. It really does feel like it adapts to how I am working instead of forcing me into one or two fixed angles.

Build and materials feel premium in a way that is immediately obvious. The MOVAS vegan leather has a soft, almost skin-like touch that makes it comfortable to hold for long stretches, and it still feels structured enough that the stand feels solid in every position. The magnets are strong, so the iPad locks into place with a reassuring snap and stays put when I tap, swipe, or draw. It is also impressively slim and light, which matters when you are carrying an iPad all day. It adds function without turning the device into a brick.

In day to day use, the ergonomic “floating” modes are quietly one of the best parts. Being able to raise the screen those extra couple of inches does make a difference for neck comfort during video streaming sessions. Combined with all the fine-grained angle options, it is easy to dial in a setup that feels good for hours instead of constantly hunching forward.

There are, however, a few drawbacks that keep this from feeling completely perfect. It is designed for direct magnetic attachment, so if you prefer running an additional case, that is not really an option here. The folding system, while versatile, has a learning curve. For the first few days I had to keep referencing the little diagram to remember how to get back to a particular configuration, and it is possible to end up in slightly unstable shapes if you are not paying attention. Price is also on the higher side for a case, even though the quality and flexibility help justify it. Finally, because it wraps like a folio and focuses on being slim and origami-friendly, it is more about desk and lap use than serious drop protection. If you are rough on your devices or want rugged corners, this may not be the only case you own.

Overall, though, this is easily one of the most thoughtfully designed iPad accessories I have used. The combination of multi-angle flexibility, elevated viewing modes, slim profile, and premium feel makes it an easy pick if your priority is turning your iPad into a more ergonomic tool.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I got this for my Samsung tablet, but have found that it works equally well with my Samsung phone and my HP laptop on both the touch screen itself as well as on the touchpad. I would say that, for those who have a hard time typing on your phone's keyboard, this can be a good solution because you can actually touch the letter you intended. The battery life is at least a few hours - not enough for a full day of work, though. For the price, I think I'm going to buy a couple so I always have one charged. One thing I expected to happen is that the charging port cover fell off and got lost within a few days...and it did. Not a deal breaker since the charging ports on my phone and tablet aren't covered, either. I also like that I have to double-tap the end to turn it on and off so it doesn't turn on accidentally. Now - if I could just remember not to tap my chin with it while thinking! :) Handwriting/drawing with it isn't terrible, you just have to write slower than usual to give it time to recognize and respond to what you're doing. It may depend on the app you use as well - I used the Notes app on my tablet and it was just OK. All in all, well worth the small price.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Apple Pencil is the best stylus accessory for the iPad but if you are like me and only spent 300 bucks on your Ipad, the idea of spending a third of that price on an accessory seems excessive. Thankfully, Logitech's alternative is a great solution for those of us who want Apple Pencil features without the cost.

The Logitech Pencil is a well-constructed, aluminum-built accessory that is designed in a rectangular shape that as a lefty, I find easier to grip than the Apple Pencil. Additionally, this shape doesn't roll or shift nearly as easily as does Apple's Pencil. I also like the charging implementation better than that of the 1st gen Apple Pencil as you don't have to worry about damaging the pencil by placing it awkwardly inside the iPad. This one just requires plugging into the standard lighting connector that shipped with your iPad.

The major drawback of the Crayon is its incompatibility. The Crayon only works with 6th Gen iPads, 3rd Gen iPad Air and the 5th Gen iPad Mini. This incompatibility error stems into cases as well. Most iPad cases that have dedicated slots/silos for the Apple Pencil will not accommodate the Crayon. In fact, I have not found any cases that have built-in slots that are made specifically for the Crayon but have heard Logitech offers one on their site. I can't confirm the veracity of that claim as I have opted to use a separate pencil carrier for my Crayon. I did see that replacement tips are currently $15 on Logitech's website and they last about as long as those for the Apple Pencil.

As for the functionality of the Crayon, it's as responsive as the Apple Pencil. In fact, you get all of the features of the Apple Pencil, except pressure sensitivity. If you are an artist, designer or the like you'll have to step up to the Apple Pencil or acclimate yourself with continually switching the thickness settings inside each app you intend to use. While you will see the 'tilt' feature advertised by Logitech as a means of adjusting from a fine line to a thicker one, in my usage I could not consistently trigger this functionality as it would work sometimes and fail others. I eventually gave up on it.

If you're a student or a professional or anyone else who has to take digital notes, highlight portions and/or add handwritten markups to them this is an excellent, cost-effective choice. You get 75% of the Apple Pencil's functionality at roughly 60% of the price. You also get a product that is easier to charge and cheaper to maintain. If you can live with the incompatibility issues you'll face with this offering and do not need pressure sensitivity for your workflow I recommend the Logitech Crayon over any other alternative to the Apple Pencil. However, if you are invested in the Apple Ecosystem or want to be certain you will have Day 1 access to all forthcoming features of Ipad OS, spending the extra $40 on the Apple Pencil is the way to go.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on July 9, 2019

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Although I have a Generation One Apple Pencil, I needed a backup stylus for my second (newest) ipad.

I work as a Professional Caricature Artist at both private and corporate events in Southeast Florida between Miami and West Palm Beach. Due to budget, most gigs opt for standard 'Traditional' Caricatures (Marker on Paper). Traditional Caricatures average between $100 to $150 per hour in Southeast Florida.

Last June (2021) at my request, another Caricaturist and friend taught me how to use the IOS program on my ipad called Procreate, allowing me to expand my art skills specifically at large Corporate venues where money is not an object. Digital Caricature Artist charge between $220 to $300 per hour. The 'WOW' factor where the ipad is connected via HDMI cable to a large monitor is amazing and attendees can view the Digital Art 'come to life.'

Sometimes, the 'charge' of both the Apple Pencil and ipad drains quickly when doing lots of drawings at gigs. Unlike the Gen 2 Apple Pencil, which 'attaches' magnetically to the ipad the First generation Apple Pencil MUST be inserted into the ipad 'lightning port'for charging and it takes between 15 to 25 minutes (depending on how much residual charge is left)

I recently purchased a second ipad (Gen 9) as a 'back up' and decided to investigate options.

The Logitech Crayon works flawless. Once fully charged (30 to 50 minutes at most) you press an area and the green light appears. It automatically works on your ipad. No 'pairing' which is required on Apple Pencils.

I did not see any significant change between the Logitech Crayon and my Apple Pencil Gen 1..except..the Apple Pencil is quieter. The Logitech Crayon has more of a mild 'metallic' sound when writing or drawing on the ipad screen. The point looks like plastic (not metal) and it is not a problem.

As far as 'pressure sensitivity', since I use the Software Digital Art Software called Procreate, I can easily adjust the opacity and width of the pen or brush strokes on the Procreate interface!

The Logitech Crayon arrived promptly (same day, if I recall) from Amazon in South Florida and I now use it more than the Apple Pencil.

Highly recommended. A great investment at about $70 for a high quality devise.

I really wanted to love this case because the transparent purple design is beautiful, and the keyboard battery life seems solid. Unfortunately, the build quality and listing accuracy do not match the price.

The biggest issue is the hinge design. There is only a single center hinge, and every time I open the case it feels like it is going to snap and it creaks loudly. For a product at this price point, this does not feel durable or reliable for long-term use.

The Apple Pencil holder is also poorly designed. It is not securely built into the case and instead clips on with a small plastic attachment. It frequently pops off during normal use, especially when removing the pencil, which is frustrating and inconvenient.

Another major concern is the listing itself. Many of the review photos appear to show a different version of the case (including one with a strap), which is not what I received and not an option on this listing. This makes the overall rating misleading, because it seems reviews from different products are being grouped together.

For the price I paid, I expected better quality control and accurate representation. I am returning this item and would not recommend it.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 star)

I really wanted to love this case because the transparent purple design is beautiful, and the keyboard battery life seems solid. Unfortunately, the build quality and listing accuracy do not match the price.

The biggest issue is the hinge design. There is only a single center hinge, and every time I open the case it feels like it is going to snap and it creaks loudly. For a product at this price point, this does not feel durable or reliable for long-term use.

The Apple Pencil holder is also poorly designed. It is not securely built into the case and instead clips on with a small plastic attachment. It frequently pops off during normal use, especially when removing the pencil, which is frustrating and inconvenient.

Another major concern is the listing itself. Many of the review photos appear to show a different version of the case (including one with a strap), which is not what I received and not an option on this listing. This makes the overall rating misleading, because it seems reviews from different products are being grouped together.

For the price I paid, I expected better quality control and accurate representation. I am returning this item and would not recommend it.

text:
Questa cover è pensata per la 10ima generazione dell'iPad da 10.9" uscita nel 2022.
La cover è realizzata da OtterBox che è un marchio specializzato in questo settore e che realizza prodotti di alta qualità. Si tratta di una cover Defender e si contraddistingue per la solidità e la protezione che offre all'iPad dato che è molto spessa e ha la certificazione militare MIL-STD 810G.
La cover è dotata anche di una protezione dello schermo e nella parte posteriore presenta due alette per sistemare l'iPad su una superficie ed usarlo senza mani.
Protegge in maniera davvero efficace dagli urti ma non solo: consente infatti di evitare accumuli di polvere nei punti di ingresso del dispositivo come la porta di ricarica.

I principali svantaggi di questa custodia sono l'ingombro, dato che aumenta il volume dell'iPad e anche il peso si sente, e il costo di circa 46 euro. In definitiva quindi si tratta di un prodotto perfetto per chi ha dei bambini che ovviamente non hanno la dovuta cura del dispositivo e accidentalmente possono farlo cadere, ma anche per chi vuole salvaguardare l'iPad senza correre alcun rischio con un investimento non contenuto ma comunque sostenibilissimo alla luce del costo dell'iPad che si va a preservare

text:
-= Lieferumfang =-
1 Otterbox Tablet Case für iPad

Die OtterBox Defender Kickstand Hülle für iPad 10,9" kommt mit dem Hinweis zu einer digitalen Anleitung auf der Umverpackung. Man landet dann auf einer Webseite mit zahlreichen Anleitungen und findet dabei allerdings keine, die genau auf das Case passt. Allerdings habe ich mir einfach die anderen Anleitungen angeschaut und hab dadurch die Mechanik verstanden. Zuerst muss die Silikonummantelung gelöst werden (Der Kickstand bleibt fest und die Ummantelung hängt nur lose). Anschließend lässt sich das Hardcase problemlos öffnen. Dann wird das iPad eingelegt und alles wieder verschlossen und die Silikonhülle wieder übergezogen.

Bestellt habe ich das Case im Rahmen von Amazon Vine zum kostenlosen Test. Es ist eigentlich für das iPad 10,9" vorgesehen. Da das iPad Air 5 jedoch die gleiche Größe hat und die meisten Cases dadurch kompatibel sind, habe ich es mir für das ipad Air 5 bestellt. Das Case passt auf jeden Fall darauf, man merkt die minimal verschobenen Ausschnitte jedoch. Allerdings schränken sie die volle Funktionalität in keinster Weise ein. Ich kann jeden Knopf drücken und alles reagiert. Auch das Touch-Display funktioniert mit dem Apple Pen hervorragend und das alles trotz Schutzfolie auf dem Display. Man merkt hier, dass es sich um ein 1A-High-Quality Produkt handelt. Ich habe noch kein so perfekt sitzendes Case gesehen, dass bis ins Detail so ordentlich verarbeitet ist. Selbst die Originale von Apple können da nicht mithalten.

Das Case schützt das Ipad vor Stößen, vor einem Fall und gibt einem das Gefühl von Sicherheit. Am Rand ist eine Lasche für den Apple Pencil angebracht. Diese finde ich allerdings wenig gelungen im Vergleich zum Rest, da es ein einfaches Gummi ist und der Stift im Zweifel heraus rutschen könnte. Umso besser ist dafür der rückseitige Kickstand mit dem das iPad stabil aufgestellt werden kann. Alles in allem ist das Case super. Es ist aber ehesten für die Bereiche gedacht, wo man das iPad nicht mit sich führt, sondern wenn man es immer Zuhause hat. Unterwegs ist eher ein Case sinnvoll mit Klappe.

-= Preis/ Leistung =-
Der Preis von 69,99 € hat mich erstmal geschockt, aber nachdem ich das Produkt nun testen konnte und man wirklich die hochwertige Qualität einmal sieht und anfassen kann, muss ich sagen, dass der Preis durchaus gerechtfertigt ist. Im Gegensatz zu den Original Produkten von Apple steckt hier wirklich was dahinter.

-= Fazit =-
Trotz der nicht so überzeugenden Halterung für den Stift ist das Case insgesamt wirklich ein echtes Highlight und ich kann es bedenkenlos weiterempfehlen. Daher gebe ich hier auch volle 5 Sterne.

text:
Quando acquisti un prodotto Apple, per ottenere la garanzia, hai due sole strade per le cadute e i danni accidentali.

Come sicuramente saprai, la cassa di Cupertino non ripara ma sostituisce i suoi Device a condizione però che questi siano integri esteticamente.

Se il tuo iPad cadesse accidentalmente solo dopo un mese dall’acquisto e per tua sfortuna dovesse scheggiarsi esteticamente e successivamente, per qualche motivo elettronico, non si accendesse più, la Apple non ti riconoscerebbe il prodotto in garanzia perché esteticamente non più idoneo alla sostituzione.

Anche se il problema fosse interno, di circuito elettronico, di batteria o di chip, se l’iPad è danneggiato esteticamente sarà tutto inutile e non avrai altra scelta che acquistare un nuovo dispositivo.

Ecco che l’acquisto di una cover come questa ha più che un senso.

Questa è un’azienda specializzata in questo tipo di prodotti.

Sono anni che usiamo cover della OtterBox per proteggere iPhone e iPad e sotto l’aspetto sicurezza e protezione non abbiamo mai avuto problemi.

Questa è una soluzione che però implica dei compromessi estetici.

Se invece l’estetica è per te la priorità, basta sottoscrivere una delle polizze Apple Care che ti proteggono da danni accidentali.

Noi abbiamo scelto sempre la soluzione cover perché con meno di 50 € il problema è certamente risolto.

Questa Cover è fatta di materiali leggeri, morbidi e piacevole al tatto. È relativamente sottile e l’iPad è protetto anche dalla parte frontale.

È dotata anche di piedini di appoggio per lavorare in comodità.

Ottimi i materiali e qualità certificata.
Il prezzo è rimasto il linea con quello richiesto gli anni passati.

Mentre tutti hanno aumentato i prezzi, in questo caso ci sembra che questo non sia avvenuto.

Anche l’eliminazione della confezione esterna ha probabilmente contribuito a mantenere il prezzo più accessibile.

Basta fare il confronto con le cover della Apple e farsi due conti per capirne la differenza.

Se l’estetica non è la tua priorità, mentre lo è la protezione del tuo iPad, acquista con fiducia questa cover che sarà probabilmente il tuo miglior acquisto dopo quello del tuo terminale by Apple.

Ci auguriamo di essere stati utili.

Grazie e alla prossima. Ciao..

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this product for recording myself on my phone for an online speech class, as well as to hold my tablet for various uses. FYI, I have used it with my 7th gen iPad and 6S Plus iPhone (I know, I’m due for an upgrade lol).

First off, the quality for the price is top notch! For what I needed it for, I have no complaints with the sturdiness. I can’t speak for using it outside on a windy day for example, but for pretty much any indoor or non-extreme-weather outdoor use I could think of, I would say go for it! The design of the product is far beyond what I expected at this price point. It’s divided into sections you can unlock individually and lock where you want them. The tripod part is sturdy as heck without taking up too much room (ie circumference).

As for the phone and tablet holders, these are pretty good overall. The phone holder is kind of strange for me because it kind of requires you to put your phone into the grip horizontally instead of giving an option, but once it’s in the grip, you can still adjust the connector to hold the phone vertically. Luckily the grip has cutouts on it to accommodate the phone’s charging port/microphone/etc while in the grip.
The tablet grip is much sturdier than I expected. I had doubts that it would be big or sturdy enough to hold my 7th gen iPad, but I haven’t had any problems. It’s a little strange for me in that the tablet goes in it diagonally, but it’s not something that I would call a negative. I also have a thick/bulky leather tablet case with a cover, so I have to remove the case to put it in this tablet grip. However, that’s not something that bothers me that much. I would guess that if you have a case that’s one of those plastic or silicone skins without much bulk, you might not need to remove it.
I have actually used this with my tablet for a couple “everyday” uses. I write articles for my job and I’ve used it a couple times to hold my tablet at about 3-3.5’ high while I sat on the couch with my Bluetooth keyboard. I can also see using it for looking at craft patterns or music tabs/sheets.

The only complaints I have so far are fairly minor.
1. The “ball joints” that tighten on the grips to connect them to the tripod (especially for the phone grip) seem a little junky. I can’t seem to get them fully connected without fear of breaking them off. However, that hasn’t stopped me from being able to tighten it enough to hold where I want. that would be my main concern about this product - worrying that those parts might not hold up for as long as I would like. However if that does happen, it seems like something that *might* be fairly universal to replace.
2. The tripod comes with a nice carrying case, but there isn’t enough room to pack all the pieces in it. The tripod itself fits nicely but it’s too small to hold all the other pieces, particularly the tablet grip. This is a minor annoyance lol. But it seems like if you’re going to the trouble to include a bag, at least make it big enough for all the parts?

Overall, if you need a sturdy little tripod for your phone and/or tablet, this is a great option! If you need something that would hold up to more than light wind, it might not be the one, but otherwise I’ve been so impressed with the quality of what I got for this price point. I’d definitely recommend this product!
Just make sure you check the measurements - I did and it fits my devices perfectly, but I could totally see overlooking that detail or guessing and being wrong.

text:
I bought this to use a music stand for the most part. I needed something that could hold an iPad and/or an iPhone while I sit/stand and practice. After a few weeks of use, I can say this does the trick! The clips to hold the phone or pad are spring loaded and very tightly secure the iPad/phone. Raising and lowering the height is a real snap, just unlatch any of the clips and up/down it goes. I’m 6’1, wearing my shoes 6’2+ and I can raise this to eye level. The 3 prong base can also be adjusted so the 3 feet can be wider or narrower depending on the stability you’re looking for. They have rubber caps and it’s a stable device, especially for under $30! The frame is metal or aluminum and it’s fairly sturdy. Could I have bought a $250 Nikon stand? Sure but total overkill. It comes with a bag to break it down and store it.

My criticisms are that the iPhone holder and iPad holder are attached to the same mechanism (see photos) It would be better if they were attached separately so I could comfortable attach my iPhone and iPad at the same time. I still can, but 4 more inches of space would be better. I’m still giving this 5 stars since I think the intent was to attach one or the other, I’m just being greedy.

text:
The Bottom Line
This case is a standout for those who want the functionality of a laptop but the flexibility of a tablet. The 360° rotating hinge is the "killer feature" here, allowing you to flip the screen for a presentation or fold it flat for drawing without removing the case. Plus, the transparent back is perfect for showing off your iPad's color or adding custom stickers.

Detailed Experience
The Hinge & Versatility: Most keyboard cases are "one-trick ponies." This one allows for Landscape, Portrait, and Tent modes. The hinge feels robust and holds its position even when I'm tapping aggressively on the screen.

Trackpad & Typing: The multi-touch trackpad is surprisingly responsive. It handles iPadOS gestures like three-finger swipes and pinch-to-zoom with minimal lag. The scissor-switch keys have a satisfying 1.3mm travel—much better than the "mushy" feel of cheaper silicone keyboards.

Backlit Vibe: The 7-color backlight isn't just for show; it’s genuinely helpful for late-night emails. You can toggle between steady colors or a "breathing" mode.

Pencil Integration: The dedicated pencil holder is positioned to allow for magnetic charging for the Apple Pencil Pro or 2nd Gen while keeping it secured during travel.

Things to Consider
Weight: Because of the sturdy hinge and battery, it adds noticeable heft to the iPad Air 13-inch. It turns your iPad into a "mini-laptop" in both power and weight.

Fingerprints: The transparent shell looks amazing but does attract fingerprints. A quick wipe with a microfiber cloth keeps it looking "tech-gallery" ready.
