title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I first got my iPad Pro I was strongly considering getting the Apple Magic Keyboard that they sell. Having done some research I discovered something that was a deal breaker for me. With the Apple keyboard when you remove the iPad from the keyboard there is no cover to protect the iPad in case of a fall or anything like that. I am very careful with my iPad, but as expensive as they are I can’t take that chance of not protecting it at all times.

I then decided that I wanted a case that would remain on the iPad that also had a full keyboard. This one is perfect for that except for one thing which I will discuss in a moment. First I will describe the features which I really like.

I really like the fact that the keyboard has a number of shortcut keys that are unique to Macs or iPads. For example it has a key that minimizes any open app and takes you to the Home Screen. It has keys that are great for music (fast forward, rewind, skip, volume control, etc.). It has a key which will quickly lock the screen and the last goes on. I like the fact that the “monitor” (i.e. the iPad itself) can be rotated 360 degrees and can be tilted in many positions. This allows for a multitude of viewing positions which is ideal if watching a video, or typing on it, or whatever. The iPad can also be folded flat over the keyboard so that you can just lay it on your lap when you don’t need the screen (the iPad, because with the keyboard on it, it feels like a laptop at this point).

The only drawback is that it is slightly heavy, but that’s the way it has to be in order to have these features and the keyboard. This is not a deal breaker for me because I almost never hold my iPad up when using it. I typically lay it down flat, or tilt it when using it. In that case I don’t feel the weight obviously. I have only had it about a week so I can’t comment on the battery life of the keyboard, but the percent of charge has gone down very slowly. With average use I would imagine that it would last at least weeks between charges. Then when you do need to charge it it charges with the same USB-C cable that it used to charge the iPad with. It charges pretty quickly as well.

I forgot to mention that it has a built in Apple Pencil holder which I also really like. It holds the pencil on very securely. Overall this keyboard case is just what I wanted, and I do recommend it!

[One-Year Update]
I've owned this keyboard for a full year, and I'd like to impart my thoughts for anyone on the fence about it. I'm going to be placing more consideration against the Magic Keyboard, as I recently caved and purchased it from a local computer store to try it out. While I did like it, I returned it in favor of using this one for a while longer.

1) Durability & Battery
This keyboard has held up well over time, minus some smudging and staining that has made me regret not purchasing the black model, on occassion. The keyboard surface is smooth and more or less unblemished, with no peeling in the silicone material around any of the buttons/trackpad. The keys are also all still intact. I cannot comment as to whether the keyboard of the first-party cases are susceptible to damage in this way, but I am pleasantly surprised as to how this one has held up. Also, the battery has not once failed me while using it. I charge it when I remember, and that is more than enough.

2) Typical Use
Minus the lack of the escape key, this does everything that I need a keyboard to do while using my iPad. The layout makes sense, there is no sticking of the keys, and the print on the keys have held up even to my oily fingers. (I am a chronic hair-toucher, so this is saying something I feel.)
I've modified the Trackpad on the software side for a) tap-to-click, and b) to increase the speed of the cursor. I did find after a while that I need to make a lot of repeated clicks with the trackpad, when it came to pressing it in, hence the former change. I will ding this justs lightly on part of the ESR, as I do not think it is an iPadOS issue - but, it is adequately addressed by adjusting the behavior in Settings. Not worth complaining about.

3) Value for Money
Especially when considering the durability of the materials, I think this is more than worth considering for your money. The only major drawback I noticed between it and its first-party counterpart, is the inability to instantly begin typing when you "open" the iPad. The magnetic pass-through charging is also a nice touch on the other case. However, neither of those things make up the additional value that the first-party cases asks for, when this one exists. If the first party ever approaches the cost of the ESR, maybe within a range of 80 USD or more, then I would say to go for that one vs. this. In reality though, the ESR win's blow for blow vs the First Party iPad case.

--
[OG Review, Shortened a Little]
I am going to compare how I feel about this case to the product it is likely duping, the Magic Keyboard. I have never owned the product*, but I have owned numerous Apple products, and I got some thoughts...

The ESR case is wickedly good quality. The case has a satisfying, velvety smooth finish, and the keys are responsive and nicely spaced. I usually make lots of typos with other bluetooth keyboards, but this one is designed very nicely, at least for the way that I type.

The inclusion of a silicone case is a MASSIVE boon, and the main reason I chose the ESR over other cantilever cases. Since I hate leaving the edges of the iPad unprotected in my bag, no other case would satisfy my desire for protection like this one does.

One con I can mention is that the weight of the iPad is greatly increased when using both parts of the case. If you were, say, also carrying a laptop or a lot of books with you, I would recommend picking between the silicone case or the keyboard, and leaving the other behind. Individually they aren't so bad -- it's when they are together that you will sweat, a little.

As an artist, I also appreciate that this case is magnetically compatible with my 2025 iPad Air. The magnet array of previous cases I have used seem to not play nicely with the Apple Pencil Pro, causing jittery or chopped up lines. Some sources mention these issues to be software related, but I can attest that they immediately went away when I put my iPad into this case.

I am so stoked to be able to stop looking for a case that will work for my needs. In my experience, the value is unmatched.

Although the attachment adds some weight, the IPad does not slip or wobble with the keyboard. Overall, this keyboard is highly recommended, 5-star, as it provides laptop feel and functionality while retaining the touchscreen ease of the IPad.

text:
I installed this in the staff room at my office. We did have a little 'charging nook', but cables kept disappearing. Even securing them to a table with a velcro strap wasn't enough to stop them from disappearing. I know most didn't mean to steal them, but it happened and this is the perfect solution!

I put the charging station under a security camera in a public spot so everyone could see what was happening at the station should anything happen. Installation was simple for a basic DIYer with a spirit level, a stud finder, a drill, and 10 minutes.

Once up the staff have really enjoyed having it. It gives their phones a safe place to charge when in need and the cables don't disappear unexpectedly. There are multiple redundant connections, and a few old ones (30 pin iPhone?!), but I added in a few extra USB-C to ensure we can charge multiple android and newer Apple phones.

The charging station itself is overbuild, a good thing. The cables are of decent quality and can't be easily removed without partially dismantling it. I added to this with some wall mounted cable ties that secure the charging cables to the wall.

A great addition to my office's staff room. Recommended for anyone looking for a centralized charging station.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in Canada on January 19, 2026

text:
We set up a multi-block charging area in our lunchroom about a year ago. Since then, we’ve spent a fair amount of money replacing two things: the charging blocks and the cords. So I liked the idea of being able to purchase a complete solution with a bit more upfront cost but having better organization and more security around the cords and blocks.

This unit mounts like a TV (bracket to the wall, sign to the bracket) and comes with 2 Micro-USB, 3 USB-C, and 3 iPhone cables. In our office, no one uses Micro-USB anymore, so we removed the back panel and swapped out the cords—we opted for 4 USB-C and 4 iPhone cables. Each side has two small screens, and the plate that holds the cords slides out of the way, making it easy to swap them. I appreciated that it came with a total of 6 USB-C, 4 Micro-USB (which, let’s be honest, are pretty much obsolete in 2025), and 6 iPhone cords.

You can also remove the board using four bolts, which makes it easy to apply your own vinyl to the front. It’s simple to trim with the board removed—a nice touch for customization.

What I like best is that the cords and blocks are secured, so we won’t need replacements unless a cord actually breaks. With the ability to swap out cords as needed, this feels like a solid long-term solution for us. Customizing the backer is worth it, though the green looks good as-is too.

✅ Pros
- Secure Setup: Cords and blocks are locked in, reducing theft and wear.
- Customizable Design: Easy to apply vinyl for branding or aesthetics.
- Cord Swapping: Flexible configuration—swap out cables to match your needs.
- Good Cable Variety: Comes with a generous supply of USB-C and iPhone cords.
- Compact & Organized: Mounts cleanly like a TV, with built-in screens and cord management.

⚠️ Cons
- Obsolete Cables: Includes Micro-USB cords, which are mostly irrelevant in 2025.
- Initial Setup Required: Swapping cords and customizing takes a bit of effort.
- Fixed Mounting: Not ideal if you need a portable or movable charging station.

🏁 Verdict
This charging station is a smart investment for shared spaces like offices or lunchrooms. It offers a clean, secure, and customizable setup that reduces cord replacements and clutter. While the Micro-USB inclusion feels outdated, the overall flexibility and build quality make it a worthwhile long-term solution—especially for environments with frequent use and multiple device types.

With an Octa-Core CPU and 8GB of RAM, this handy gadget performs brilliantly whether you're browsing the web or having a chat on a video call. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I use the Galaxy Tab A8 on stage and rehearsals for reference for songs (chords, sheet music, lyrics, etc). It can do more, but I'm not trying to push this to it's limits for what I need the screen to be on all the time for shows...although I will use it as a sleep/white noise machine for sleep on occasion (wish YT allowed for screen off but maintained audio, but that's TY for ya)...

It is what I was expecting.. a very good quality and performance for a mid ranged tablet. I would've gone with a smaller footprint tablet, but those were underpowered, and the screen was a lot worse that this. It's not trash, but I'd be paying Tab S8 money for a larger screen...I'm not looking to add weight to a mic stand mount to have it tip over, so this fit the bill.

Screen - as I mentioned, the screen is not trash. Looks rather smooth considering. Could be better in the brightness department as well, but this is because of the type of display that's used. Think older LED tv's to a 2K computer monitor. It's slight, but noticeable. I compared this to a mentioned S8. This is what you're paying for that (amongst other things). I'm okay with this compared to the price vs the S8. Like I also mentioned before, I would've gone for the smaller footprint, but trade off is a slightly worse screen for it's size, and the weight and performance (the 64bg and 128gb variant has 4G RAM, compared to the 32gb storage variant having only 3gb RAM).

Weight - compared to the S8, this wins the weight ratio to size for lighter tablet (even with a spigen lightweight case on this thing).

Performance - This is where the added RAM is helpful. My lead guitarist has this same tablet in the 32gb version, and the added ram is a super helpful when opening the PDFs for songs and lyrics while having the setlist up on the other half of the tablet for the split screen. Especially when leaving the screen timeout to never and having the brightness down enough to not be bothersome on stage to anyone else. It was a bit snappier when I compared it to a head to head test between the 2 (I adjusted the screen animations in Developer Options). It brought up several PDF's up a tad bit faster, but you can definitely make due with the 32gb, but I'd rather have that room for the PDF's and probably songs I've downloaded for reference on a 512gb microSD card and allow for the performance on the tablet not be bogged down by the tablet being full of files. I've also used this as a touchscreen mouse pad for a laptop connected to my TV as a HTPC via Bluetooth. I prefer a keyboard and trackball for this, but in a pinch, this using an app helps. No lag or problems.

Speakers - I do use this as a sleep machine when I need it, and it does help me. It's loud, bordering on annoying in a bedroom. But I've had no issues with the audio on it using as a browser, multimedia device, and using headphones (wired or wireless, via the headphone jack, Bluetooth, or dongle). Also I've adjusted some things in Dev Options for this as well...so no issues.

There's not a whole lot to say for this for what I use it for...It has worked flawlessly, so there are no regrets. This is a great little device.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I use the Galaxy Tab A8 on stage and rehearsals for reference for songs (chords, sheet music, lyrics, etc). It can do more, but I'm not trying to push this to it's limits for what I need the screen to be on all the time for shows...although I will use it as a sleep/white noise machine for sleep on occasion (wish YT allowed for screen off but maintained audio, but that's TY for ya)...

It is what I was expecting.. a very good quality and performance for a mid ranged tablet. I would've gone with a smaller footprint tablet, but those were underpowered, and the screen was a lot worse that this. It's not trash, but I'd be paying Tab S8 money for a larger screen...I'm not looking to add weight to a mic stand mount to have it tip over, so this fit the bill.

Screen - as I mentioned, the screen is not trash. Looks rather smooth considering. Could be better in the brightness department as well, but this is because of the type of display that's used. Think older LED tv's to a 2K computer monitor. It's slight, but noticeable. I compared this to a mentioned S8. This is what you're paying for that (amongst other things). I'm okay with this compared to the price vs the S8. Like I also mentioned before, I would've gone for the smaller footprint, but trade off is a slightly worse screen for it's size, and the weight and performance (the 64bg and 128gb variant has 4G RAM, compared to the 32gb storage variant having only 3gb RAM).

Weight - compared to the S8, this wins the weight ratio to size for lighter tablet (even with a spigen lightweight case on this thing).

Performance - This is where the added RAM is helpful. My lead guitarist has this same tablet in the 32gb version, and the added ram is a super helpful when opening the PDFs for songs and lyrics while having the setlist up on the other half of the tablet for the split screen. Especially when leaving the screen timeout to never and having the brightness down enough to not be bothersome on stage to anyone else. It was a bit snappier when I compared it to a head to head test between the 2 (I adjusted the screen animations in Developer Options). It brought up several PDF's up a tad bit faster, but you can definitely make due with the 32gb, but I'd rather have that room for the PDF's and probably songs I've downloaded for reference on a 512gb microSD card and allow for the performance on the tablet not be bogged down by the tablet being full of files. I've also used this as a touchscreen mouse pad for a laptop connected to my TV as a HTPC via Bluetooth. I prefer a keyboard and trackball for this, but in a pinch, this using an app helps. No lag or problems.

Speakers - I do use this as a sleep machine when I need it, and it does help me. It's loud, bordering on annoying in a bedroom. But I've had no issues with the audio on it using as a browser, multimedia device, and using headphones (wired or wireless, via the headphone jack, Bluetooth, or dongle). Also I've adjusted some things in Dev Options for this as well...so no issues.

There's not a whole lot to say for this for what I use it for...It has worked flawlessly, so there are no regrets. This is a great little device.

It does come with a few wallpapers but I downloaded a couple so show it's screen quality here. Brightness was at 14% here & in a dimly lit room so it has plenty of brightness. It feels very solid & to me & appropriate weight for it's size. I actually have a scale here & weighed the tablet. It weighs 1lb 10.6 ounces with the case on it. My wife has an 11" tablet & I weighed it in it's case & came up 1lb 12.4 ounces so it is a pretty standard weight. The overall value for what you receive here is excellent in price, especially when you add in all the goodies it comes with. text:
I've used this tablet for about a month now and I've got to say that it's very much improved over the previous generation's 11" x800 model. This being a 10" model feels like better proportions overall. The processor is swift, and switching between apps is snappy. One specific area of great improvement is boot time. This new model requires you to hold the power button for 3 seconds, then the screen turns off and the boot process starts. In total it takes around 30 seconds to go from fully powered off to booted up and ready to use. That's about half the time it took the previous model.

The included keyboard, mouse, and leather case are a nice addition and increase functionality quite a bit so you can do more intensive tasks.

One area I would say that could still use some attention by the developers is the charge speed. It's a pretty good sized battery, but no fast charging of any type so expect that if you are a heavy user, you may find yourself waiting for it to be juiced up. But for this price point I haven't found any tablets that do have fast charging so it's not really lacking class wise.

Overall, I'm very happy with this tablet and you get a great deal of functionality for the price.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Ordered the FIVAHIVA SS-35 to evaluate and give to one of the kids... but the wife ended up appropriating it. At first glance the exterior rubbery case provides more than adequate protection — but it is also a necessity since the back surface of the tablet can become unbearably hot to the touch without it during prolonged operation. Initial setup is quite easy; can be either a kid or adult Google profile. If choosing the kid profile it defaults to a child friendly GUI; permissions, apps and games can be managed via the parent's account.

Performance wise the tablet is low to mid tier. Connects to either WIFI 2.4ghz or 5Ghz networks. The screen features a native resolution of 1280x800 pixels or 720p, which is fine for most. It will run most modern Android games including 3D ones but it may underperform with some titles, such as large MOBAs or FPS. Battery life is good but not impressive — some games will deplete it quicker than others. A power adapter block and USB-C charging cable are included for convenience. The tablet has both front and rear facing cameras, great for taking selfies or using video chat software. Storage space can also be expanded via microSD cards (not included). Overall the only issue that keeps it from being a perfect budget tablet is the overheating issue (concealed by the thick case). That aside, it is a pretty good deal at current MSRP.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the Riwbox CT-7S Cat Ear Headphones for my daughter, and they have been a huge hit. If you are looking for a gift that looks cool but actually works well, these are a great pick.
What We Loved:
* The "Cool" Factor: The LED lights in the cat ears are bright and change colors. My daughter loves that they flash along to her music. It's a nice touch that you can turn them off if they get too distracting or if you want to save battery.
* Safety First: As a parent, the 85dB volume limit is the most important feature. I don't have to worry about her accidentally cranking the volume too high and hurting her ears while she's playing games or watching videos.
* Battery & Wired Mode: The battery life is solid (we get several days of casual use), but the best part is the included backup cable. If the battery dies during a long car ride, we just plug them in like regular headphones, and she can keep listening.
* Comfortable Fit: They are lightweight and the ear cushions are very soft. They fit her perfectly and are adjustable enough that she won't outgrow them immediately. Plus, they fold up, which makes them easy to toss in a backpack.
A Couple of Notes:
* Passive Noise Canceling: These don't have active noise cancellation, so if you're on a loud airplane, your child might still hear some engine hum, but for home and car use, they are perfect.
* Buttons: It took a minute to learn the button shortcuts (like holding the 'M' button to toggle the lights), but the manual is clear enough.
Overall Verdict:
These are fantastic headphones for the price. They are durable, safe, and the LED cat ears make them much more exciting than standard kid headphones. I’d definitely buy them again!
